questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A suspect was held for questioning at a police station regarding a recent robbery. A police detective advised the suspect of his Miranda rights, which the suspect understood, before asking the suspect about his whereabouts on the night of the robbery. During the questioning, the suspect's attorney called the police station to inform the detective that he was on his way. The detective did not relay this information to the suspect and continued questioning the suspect until he made an incriminating statement. The suspect was subsequently indicted for robbery.
Is the suspect's statement admissible at trial?

choices.A: No, because the detective violated the suspect's Sixth Amendment right to counsel.
choices.B: No, because the detective was required to inform the suspect that his attorney was on his way.
choices.C: Yes, because the suspect had not been indicted for the robbery at the time of questioning.
choices.D: Yes, because the suspect's statement was voluntary.

questions.explanation:
Right to counsel
Applicability Request Waiver
Fifth
Amendment		 Suspect has right to counsel when:
• in custody and
• subjected to interrogation 		Unambiguous
request
required		 Valid if made:
• knowingly
• intelligently

Amendment		 Defendant has right to counsel when:

• critical stage of prosecution 		No request

The Constitution guarantees the right to counsel in two places—the Fifth Amendment and the Sixth Amendment. The Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

• automatically attaches once formal judicial proceedings commence (e.g., indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

• guarantees that criminal defendants will thereafter have the assistance of counsel during all critical stages of prosecution (i.e., any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial).

Here, the suspect was questioned by the detective before the suspect had been indicted for robbery, so formal judicial proceedings had not yet commenced. Therefore, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel had not attached when the suspect made the incriminating statement (Choices A and C).

In contrast, the Fifth Amendment right to counsel applies when a suspect is subjected to a custodial interrogation before judicial proceedings commence. However, a suspect must invoke this right by making a specific, unambiguous statement requesting counsel. A suspect who received and understood the Miranda warnings but did not invoke his Miranda rights waives the right to remain silent by making an uncoerced statement to the police—and that statement is admissible at trial.

Here, the suspect received and understood his Miranda warnings, but the suspect never made a specific and unambiguous request for counsel. And because there is no indication that the suspect's incriminating statement was coerced, the suspect waived the right to remain silent by voluntarily making that statement. Accordingly, the suspect's statement is admissible at trial.

(Choice B) The detective was not required to inform the suspect that his attorney was on the way, nor was the detective required to inform the attorney that the suspect was being questioned.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once formal judicial proceedings commence. In contrast, the Fifth Amendment right to counsel applies whenever a suspect is subjected to a custodial interrogation, and a suspect must invoke this right by making a specific, unambiguous statement requesting counsel.

📚 References
  • Moran v. Burbine, 475 U.S. 412, 421–422 (1986) (holding that police are under no obligation to inform a suspect that an attorney has been trying to reach him and may even withhold that information intentionally, so long as the Sixth Amendment right to counsel has not yet attached).
questions.zh-question: 一名嫌疑人在警察局因一起近期抢劫案被拘留审讯。一名警探在询问嫌疑人抢劫案当晚的行踪之前，告知了嫌疑人其 Miranda 权利，嫌疑人表示理解。审讯期间，嫌疑人的律师致电警察局，告知警探他正在赶来。警探没有将此信息转告给嫌疑人，并继续审讯嫌疑人，直到他做出了一份有罪供述。嫌疑人随后被起诉抢劫罪。嫌疑人的供述在审判中是否可采纳？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为警探侵犯了嫌疑人的第六修正案 (Sixth Amendment) 律师权。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为警探有义务告知嫌疑人其律师正在赶来。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在审讯时嫌疑人尚未被起诉抢劫罪。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为嫌疑人的供述是自愿的。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was convicted of possession of a controlled substance with the intent to distribute and sentenced to 20 years confinement in a state prison. Five years into the man's confinement, prison officials began to suspect that the man was distributing drugs inside the prison. One day, the man was removed from his cell and taken to the prison dentist for what the guards told him was a "routine checkup." After the man exited the cell, guards entered and told the man's cellmate that they were going to search the cell. The cellmate did not object. The guards searched the cell without a warrant and found several grams of heroin hidden in a locked box under the man's bed.
The man was charged with distribution of a controlled substance within a secure facility and, under the state's three-strikes rule, faces life in prison. The man has moved to suppress the heroin.
Should the man's motion to suppress be granted?

choices.A: No, because the cellmate impliedly consented to the search of the cell.
choices.B: No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his cell or items therein.
choices.C: Yes, because the heroin was not in plain view when the guards searched the cell.
choices.D: Yes, because the locked box was a constitutionally protected area that required a warrant.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Common items & areas
with no reasonable expectation of privacy
  • Bank records
  • Things exposed to public view (e.g., open fields, abandoned property)
  • Physical characteristics (e.g., handwriting, vocal sound)
  • Conversations with undercover officers & informants
  • Pen registers (i.e., records of dialed telephone numbers)
  • Smells emanating from cars & other items
  • Prison inmate's cell
  • Automobile's vehicle identification number (VIN)

The Fourth Amendment is violated when the government conducts an unreasonable search or seizure—ie, when police act without a warrant and no exception applies. A Fourth Amendment search occurs if one of the following tests is met:

• Physical trespass test – the government physically intrudes upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information

• Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invades a person's subjective expectation of privacy that society would find objectively reasonable

In Hudson v. Palmer, the Supreme Court held that inmates have no privacy interest in their cells and no possessory interest in their items therein (eg, the locked box) that would entitle them to Fourth Amendment protections (Choice D). Therefore, the guards' search of the man's cell did not violate the Fourth Amendment, and the court should deny his motion to suppress.

(Choice A) Third parties (eg, a suspect's roommate) may consent to a warrantless search of property over which the third party had joint control and access. Here, the man's cellmate did not object to the search of the cell—ie, he impliedly consented. But since inmates have no reasonable expectation of privacy in their cells, the cellmate's consent was unnecessary.

(Choice C) Under the plain-view exception to the warrant requirement, officers may seize an item if (1) the item is in plain view, (2) it is immediately apparent that the item is contraband, and (3) the officer is lawfully in the area. But since prisoners have no reasonable expectation of privacy in their cells, reliance on the plain-view exception is unnecessary.

📌 Educational Objective

Inmates have no privacy interest in their prison cells or possessory interest in the items therein that would entitle them to Fourth Amendment protections. Therefore, officials may search an inmate's cell without implicating the Fourth Amendment.

📚 References
  • Hudson v. Palmer, 468 U.S. 517, 522–24 (1984) (holding that inmates hold no reasonable expectation of privacy in prison cells).
  • Wayne R. LaFave, 1 Search and Seizure 167; 2.4(d) (6th ed. 2020) (discussing privacy interests in detention facilities).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因意图分销而持有受管制药物被定罪，并被判处在州立监狱监禁20年。在该男子被监禁五年后，监狱官员开始怀疑他在监狱内分销毒品。一天，该男子被带出牢房，送往监狱牙医处，狱警告诉他这是一次“例行检查”。在该男子离开牢房后，狱警进入并告知其室友他们将要搜查该牢房。室友没有提出反对。狱警在没有搜查令的情况下搜查了牢房，并在该男子床下的一个上锁的盒子里发现了数克海洛因。

该男子被指控在安全设施内分销受管制药物，并且根据该州的三振出局法，将面临终身监禁。该男子已提出动议，要求排除该海洛因作为证据。

该男子的排除证据动议是否应被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为室友默示同意了对牢房的搜查。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该男子对其牢房或其中的物品没有合理的隐私期待。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为当狱警搜查牢房时，海洛因并不在显眼处。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为上锁的盒子是受宪法保护的区域，需要搜查令。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析
宪法第四修正案与监狱搜查

正确答案：B 不应批准动议，因为该男子对其牢房或其中的物品没有合理的隐私期待。
核心法律原则
Fourth Amendment (第四修正案) 保护人们免受政府“不合理的搜查和扣押”。要触发这一保护，个人必须在被搜查的地方拥有“合理的隐私期待” (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。 判例依据：Hudson v. Palmer (1984)

美国最高法院在 Hudson v. Palmer 案中明确裁定：出于监狱安全和管理的需要，囚犯在其牢房内不享有 Fourth Amendment 赋予的隐私权。

案情逻辑分析
⚖️ 前提判断： 本案的核心在于判断搜查是否受到宪法保护。如果 Fourth Amendment 不适用，那么是否拥有搜查令 (Warrant)、是否有相当理由 (Probable Cause) 都不再重要。
🔒 监狱环境的特殊性： 虽然该男子将海洛因放在“上锁的盒子”里，这表现了他主观上的隐私意图，但在监狱这一特定环境下，社会不承认这种隐私期待是客观合理的。
✅ 结论： 既然囚犯在牢房内没有隐私权，狱警的搜查行为（无论是否有搜查令，无论是否是“例行检查”）就不构成 Fourth Amendment 下的“搜查”。因此，不需要排除证据。
为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A (默示同意) 错误：
虽然第三方同意 (Third-party consent) 是无证搜查的一种例外情况，但在这里是多余的。因为根本不需要任何人的同意（无论是囚犯还是室友），狱警本身就有权随时搜查牢房。
选项 C (显眼例外 Plain View) 错误：
“显眼例外”原则通常用于让警方在没有搜查令的情况下扣押证据。但该原则的前提是 Fourth Amendment 适用。由于在此处 Fourth Amendment 根本不适用，讨论海洛因是否在“显眼处”没有法律意义。
选项 D (上锁盒子) 错误：
这是最具迷惑性的选项。在自由社会中，上锁的盒子通常享有极高的隐私期待。但在监狱中，Hudson 案的裁决延伸到了牢房内的所有物品。囚犯对牢房内的任何私人物品均无占有性隐私利益。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

“门槛测试” (Threshold Test)：

在处理 Criminal Procedure 的搜查问题时，第一步永远是问：“Fourth Amendment 是否适用？”

如果是以下区域，答案通常是 NO（即没有隐私期待，警察可以随意搜查）：

  • 监狱牢房 (Prison cells)
  • 露天田野 (Open fields)
  • 公共视野 (Public view)
  • 废弃物 (Abandoned property)

如果判定为上述区域，直接选择“没有隐私期待”或“不构成搜查”的选项，无需分析是否有搜查令。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A prosecutor presented to a federal grand jury the testimony of a witness in order to secure a defendant's indictment for theft of government property. The prosecutor did not disclose to the grand jury that the witness had been convicted four years earlier of perjury. The grand jury returned an indictment, and the defendant pleaded not guilty.
Shortly thereafter, the prosecutor took the case to trial, calling the witness to testify before the jury. The prosecutor did not disclose the witness's prior perjury conviction until the defense was preparing to rest. Defense counsel immediately moved for a mistrial, which the court denied. Instead, the court allowed the defense to recall the witness for the purpose of impeaching him with this conviction, but the witness could not be located. The court then allowed the defense to introduce documentary evidence of the witness's criminal record to the jury before resting its case. The jury convicted the defendant.
The defendant has moved for a new trial, arguing that the prosecutor's failure to disclose the witness's prior conviction in a timely manner violated the defendant's right to due process of law.
If the court grants the defendant's motion, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.A: The court found it reasonably probable that the defendant would have been acquitted had the defense had timely access to the information about the witness's conviction.
choices.B: The court found that the prosecutor had deliberately delayed disclosing the witness's conviction to obtain a strategic advantage.
choices.C: The defendant was unable to cross-examine the witness about the conviction.
choices.D: The prosecutor failed to inform the grand jury of the witness's conviction.

questions.explanation:
Exculpatory v. Impeachment
DNA Lab Report
crime scene
defendant
suspect 2
You have a perjury conviction, correct?

In Brady v. Maryland, the Supreme Court held that a defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose evidence that is both:

  • favorable to the defendant – evidence used to negate a defendant's guilt or mitigate punishment (exculpatory evidence) or to discredit the prosecution's witness (impeachment evidence) and
  • material to guilt or punishment – there is a reasonable probability that, had the evidence been disclosed, the result of the proceeding would have been different.

Here, the prosecutor failed to timely disclose its witness's prior perjury conviction (favorable evidence) since that information was not shared until the defense was preparing to rest and the witness could not be located. Therefore, the court would most likely grant the defendant's motion for new trial if it found it reasonably probable that the defendant would have been acquitted had the defense timely received that information (material evidence).

(Choice B) The prosecution violates a defendant's due process rights when it fails to timely disclose favorable and material evidence for any reason—purposely or unintentionally. Therefore, a finding that the prosecutor purposely delayed disclosing the witness's conviction for a strategic advantage is no basis for granting the motion.

(Choice C) The prosecution's untimely disclosure did not prevent the defendant from cross-examining the witness about the conviction (no violation of Sixth Amendment right to confront adverse witnesses). However, the untimely disclosure did violate the defendant's due process rights since it is probable that the outcome would have been different had the witness's conviction been disclosed earlier.

(Choice D) In United States v. Williams, the Supreme Court explained that a prosecutor is not required to present Brady evidence to the grand jury. Therefore, the prosecutor's failure to inform the grand jury of the witness's conviction did not violate due process and is not a basis for granting the defendant's motion.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose Brady evidence—ie, evidence that is favorable to the defendant (exculpatory or impeachment evidence) and material to guilt or punishment.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (federal due process clause).
  • Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83, 87 (1963) (recognizing that prosecution's withholding of favorable and material evidence violated due process).
  • United States v. Bagley, 473 U.S. 667, 682 (1985) (discussing when a failure to disclose evidence favorable to the defendant is material).
questions.zh-question:
一名检察官向联邦大陪审团呈交了一名证人的证词，以确保对一名被告人盗窃政府财产罪的起诉。该检察官未向大陪审团披露该证人曾在四年前因伪证罪被定罪。大陪审团发出了起诉书，被告人作了无罪答辩。

此后不久，检察官将此案提交审判，并传唤该证人在陪审团面前作证。直到辩方准备结束己方案情呈述时，检察官才披露该证人先前的伪证罪定罪记录。辩护律师立即动议审判无效，但被法庭驳回。法庭反而允许辩方重新传唤该证人，以便用此定罪记录来弹劾其证词，但该证人已无法找到。随后，法庭允许辩方在结束己方案情呈述前，向陪审团出示该证人犯罪记录的书面证据。陪审团裁定被告人有罪。

被告人已动议重新审判，主张检察官未能及时披露证人的先前定罪记录，侵犯了其获得正当法律程序的权利。

如果法庭批准被告人的动议，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 法庭认定，如果辩方及时获得了关于该证人定罪记录的信息，被告人有合理可能性被宣告无罪。
zh-choices.B: 法庭认定，检察官为获得战略优势而故意延迟披露该证人的定罪记录。
zh-choices.C: 被告人无法就该定罪记录对证人进行交叉询问。
zh-choices.D: 检察官未能将该证人的定罪记录告知大陪审团。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Brady Violations

核心考点：Brady 规则 (The Brady Rule) 根据 Brady v. Maryland (1963) 及其后续判例，如果检方未能披露对被告有利 (Favorable) 且具有重要性 (Material) 的证据，则违反了宪法第五修正案或第十四修正案的正当程序 (Due Process) 条款。
深度解析

本题考察的是检方未能及时披露“弹劾证据”（Impeachment Evidence）的后果。要赢得基于 Brady 违规的重审动议，被告必须证明以下三点：

  1. 证据对被告是有利的（包括开脱罪责的证据或弹劾证人的证据）；
  2. 证据被检方隐瞒了（无论是故意的还是无意的）；
  3. 证据是重要的 (Material)，即如果不隐瞒，案件结果可能会不同。

本案中，证人的伪证罪定罪记录显然是有利的弹劾证据。检方确实延迟披露了。因此，案件的关键在于第三点：重要性 (Materiality)。

选项分析
选项 A [正确]

理由：这是对 Brady 规则中“重要性”标准的准确描述。

根据 United States v. Bagley (1985)，证据是否“重要”取决于是否存在一种“合理可能性” (Reasonable Probability)，即如果证据被披露，诉讼结果会不同（例如被告被宣告无罪）。如果法庭批准重审，必然是因为法庭认定该证据的缺失损害了审判的公正性，足以改变结果。

选项 B [错误]

理由：Brady 违规不看检方的“意图”。

最高法院明确指出，无论检方是出于恶意 (Bad Faith) 还是疏忽 (Negligence) 未披露证据，只要证据有利且重要，就构成违规。因此，检方是否“故意”不是批准重审的必要条件。

选项 C [错误]

理由：这是事实描述，而非法律标准。

虽然被告确实未能进行交叉询问，但这只是造成“损害”的过程。批准重审的法律依据必须是这种缺失导致了结果可能不同（即选项 A 的标准）。如果证据无关紧要（Immaterial），即使无法交叉询问，也不会导致重审。

选项 D [错误]

理由：大陪审团规则不同。

在 United States v. Williams 案中，最高法院裁定检方没有义务向大陪审团 (Grand Jury) 展示开脱罪责的证据 (Exculpatory Evidence)。大陪审团的职责仅是决定是否有相当理由 (Probable Cause) 起诉，而非判定有罪无罪。

💡 MBE 提分技巧

在处理 Brady Violation 的题目时，请记住公式：

Favorable + Suppressed + Prejudice (Materiality) = Violation

很多干扰选项会强调检察官的“恶意”或“疏忽”，但请记住：检方的主观意图是不相关的 (Irrelevant)。重点永远在于未披露证据对审判结果的潜在影响。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
On May 1, 2013, a car driven by a delivery man struck a pedestrian. On July 1, 2013, the delivery man pleaded guilty to reckless driving (a misdemeanor) and was sentenced to 30 days in jail and a fine of $1,000. He served the sentence and paid the fine. On April 1, 2014, the pedestrian died as a result of the injuries she suffered in the accident. On March 1, 2017, a grand jury indicted the delivery man on a charge of manslaughter of the pedestrian. On May 15, 2017, trial had not begun and the delivery man filed a motion to dismiss the indictment on the ground of double jeopardy in that his conviction of reckless driving arose out of the same incident, and on the ground that the three-year statute of limitations for manslaughter had run.
How should the court rule on the delivery man's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion on both grounds.
choices.B: Grant the motion only on double jeopardy grounds.
choices.C: Grant the motion only on statute of limitations grounds.
choices.D: Grant the motion on either double jeopardy grounds or statute of limitations grounds.

An indictment should be dismissed if it violates the Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause, which generally prohibits multiple punishments or a second prosecution for the same offense—ie, when crimes have identical elements or all elements of one crime are also elements of the other. But a second prosecution is permitted if:

  • the defendant was convicted of a lesser offense at the first trial
  • the second trial involves a greater offense—ie, a more serious crime that includes all elements of the first crime—and
  • the facts necessary to establish the greater offense did not exist at the time of the first trial.

Here, the delivery man pled guilty to reckless driving (lesser offense) and was then indicted for manslaughter (greater offense). These crimes constitute the same offense since manslaughter—here, an unintentional killing of another during the commission of a misdemeanor—includes the elements of reckless driving. But since the pedestrian died after the man was convicted of reckless driving, the man could not have been prosecuted for manslaughter at the first trial. Therefore, the indictment does not violate double jeopardy (Choices B & D).

An indictment should also be dismissed if the statute of limitations—a statutory time limit for prosecuting a defendant for a crime—has expired before a prosecution has commenced. A statute of limitations starts to run (ie, the time limit begins) once all the elements of the crime have occurred. This helps ensure that defendants can adequately defend themselves with evidence and facts that have not been obscured by the passage of time.

Here, the three-year statute of limitations for manslaughter began when the pedestrian died on April 1, 2014. Therefore, it would not expire until April 1, 2017. And since the delivery man was indicted for manslaughter on March 1, 2017—one month before the statute of limitations was set to expire—the indictment should not be dismissed on this basis (Choices C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

Double jeopardy does not prohibit a second prosecution for the same offense when (1) the defendant was convicted of a lesser offense at the first trial, (2) the second prosecution involves a greater offense, and (3) the facts necessary to prove that offense did not exist during the first trial. But the defendant must be indicted before the statute of limitations expires.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • Diaz v. United States, 223 U.S. 442, 449 (1912) (holding that double jeopardy does not prevent a second prosecution for murder when victim was alive at the time of the first prosecution for assault and battery).
  • Toussie v. United States, 397 U.S. 112, 114–15 (1970) (explaining the significance of statute of limitations).
questions.zh-question: 法院应如何就该送货员的动议作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 基于两项理由均驳回该动议。
zh-choices.B: 仅以“一事不再理”为由批准该动议。
zh-choices.C: 仅以诉讼时效为由批准该动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

宪法保护 & 刑事程序
正确答案：A 法院应基于两项理由（一事不再理和诉讼时效）驳回被告的动议 (Deny the motion)。

本题考察了刑事程序中的两个核心概念：一事不再理 (Double Jeopardy) 的例外情况以及诉讼时效 (Statute of Limitations) 的起算点。

考点一：一事不再理 (Double Jeopardy)

一般原则：根据美国宪法第五修正案，通常禁止对“同一罪行”进行二次起诉。根据 Blockburger 测试，如果较轻的罪行（如鲁莽驾驶）是较重罪行（如过失杀人）的包含性犯罪 (Lesser Included Offense)，则通常禁止在定罪后再次起诉较重的罪行。

关键例外 (The Diaz Exception)：
如果证明较重罪行所需的必要事实 (Necessary Facts) 在第一次审判时尚未发生，则不适用一事不再理原则。

本案分析：

2013年7月1日
被告因鲁莽驾驶被定罪。此时受害人还活着。
2014年4月1日
受害人死亡。

由于构成过失杀人罪（Manslaughter）的关键要素——受害人死亡——在第一次审判时并未发生，因此政府可以在受害人死后提起新的指控。这不违反 Double Jeopardy。

考点二：诉讼时效 (Statute of Limitations)

起算规则：
诉讼时效从犯罪行为完成 (Complete) 之日起算。即犯罪的所有构成要件（Elements）都已满足的那一刻。

本案分析：

  • 犯罪完成日：过失杀人罪是结果犯，必须有“死亡”这一结果才构成犯罪。因此，时效从受害人死亡之日（2014年4月1日）开始计算，而不是事故发生日。
  • 时效届满日：三年时效将于 2017年4月1日 届满。
  • 起诉日期：大陪审团于 2017年3月1日 提起公诉。

因为起诉发生在时效届满之前（提前了一个月），所以诉讼时效未过。

结论与解题技巧

法院应驳回被告的两项抗辩理由：

  1. 一事不再理：不成立，因为定罪时受害人尚未死亡（例外情况）。
  2. 诉讼时效：不成立，因为时效从死亡日开始计算，起诉时未过期。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到“先定罪，后死亡”的题目，几乎总是考察 Diaz v. United States 确立的例外规则。记住：如果第一次审判时受害人还活着，后续的谋杀/杀人起诉通常是允许的。同时注意检查日期的计算起点。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The police suspected that a 16-year-old high school student had committed a series of burglaries. One day, two officers went to the student's high school and asked the principal to call the student out of class and to search his backpack. While the officers waited, the principal took the student into the hall where she asked to look in his backpack. When the student refused, the principal grabbed it from him, injuring the student's shoulder in the process. In the backpack, the principal found jewelry that she turned over to the officers.
The officers believed that the jewelry had been taken in one of the burglaries. They arrested the student, took him to the station, and gave him Miranda warnings. The student then asked to see a lawyer. The police called the student's parents to the station. When the parents arrived, the police asked them to speak with the student. The officers put the student and his parents in a room and secretly recorded their conversation with a concealed electronic device. The student immediately broke down and confessed to his parents that he had committed the burglaries.
The student was charged with the burglaries.
If the student moves to suppress the use of the jewelry, how should the court rule on his motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion on the ground that school searches are reasonable if conducted by school personnel on school grounds on the basis of reasonable suspicion.
choices.B: Deny the motion on the ground that the search was incident to a lawful arrest.
choices.C: Grant the motion on the ground that the search was conducted with excessive force.
choices.D: Grant the motion on the ground that the search was conducted without probable cause or a warrant.

A Fourth Amendment search must generally be authorized by a warrant based on probable cause, but this requirement is often relaxed in school settings to maintain a safe learning environment. Therefore, school officials do not need a warrant or probable cause to search a student on school grounds if:

  • they have reasonable suspicion that the student violated (or is violating) the law or school rules
  • the scope of the search is reasonably related to the suspected offense and
  • the search is not excessively intrusive given the student's age, sex, and the nature of the suspected offense.

However, if a school official conducts a search at the direction of the police, it must be supported by a warrant based on probable cause or an exception to the warrant requirement. Police cannot rely on the relaxed standards governing school searches.

Here, two officers asked the principal to call the student out of class and to search his backpack. The principal did so without a warrant and found jewelry that she then turned over to the officers. Since the principal's search was conducted at the direction of the police, a warrant based on probable cause was required (Choice A). Therefore, the court should suppress the use of the jewelry.
(Choice B) The search-incident-to-a-lawful-arrest exception allows officers to conduct a warrantless search of the person arrested and the areas in his/her immediate reach. This exception is inapplicable here because the student was not arrested.
(Choice C) A search conducted with excessive force may expose the police or persons acting at their direction to civil liability, but will not result in the suppression of evidence. So even if the principal used excessive force when she grabbed the student's backpack and injured him, the motion should not be granted on this basis.
📌 Educational Objective

School officials may search a student without a warrant if (1) they have reasonable suspicion that the student violated a law or school rule, (2) the scope of the search is reasonably related to the suspected offense, and (3) the search is not excessively intrusive. However, a warrant is required if the search is conducted at the direction of the police.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • New Jersey v. T.L.O., 469 U.S. 325, 340–42 (1985) (holding that school officials need only reasonable suspicion that a student violated the law to search the student).
  • Coolidge v. New Hampshire, 403 U.S. 443, 487–88 (1971) (recognizing that searches carried out by individual acting at the direction of police are scrutinized as though they were carried out by police themselves).
questions.zh-question:
警方怀疑一名16岁的高中生犯下了一系列入室犯法罪。一天，两名警官来到该学生的高中，要求校长将该学生叫出教室并搜查其背包。在警官等待期间，校长将学生带到走廊，要求查看他的背包。当学生拒绝时，校长从他手中抢过背包，在此过程中弄伤了学生的肩膀。校长在背包里发现了珠宝，并将其交给了警官。

警官认为这些珠宝是其中一起入室犯法罪的赃物。他们逮捕了该学生，将他带到警察局，并向他宣读了 Miranda 警告。该学生随后要求见律师。警方将学生的父母叫到警察局。父母到达后，警方要求他们与学生交谈。警官将学生和他的父母安排在一个房间里，并用一个隐蔽的电子设备秘密录下了他们的谈话。学生立即情绪崩溃，向父母承认自己犯下了入室犯法罪。

该学生被控犯有入室犯法罪。

如果该学生动议排除使用该珠宝作为证据，法院应如何裁定其动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，理由是如果学校搜查由学校人员在校园内基于合理怀疑进行，则是合理的。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，理由是该搜查是合法逮捕的附带搜查。
zh-choices.C: 支持动议，理由是该搜查使用了过度武力。
zh-choices.D: 支持动议，理由是该搜查在没有合理依据或搜查令的情况下进行。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
核心法律规则

本题考察的是第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment) 在学校环境中的适用标准，特别是当学校人员作为警方代理人 (Agent of the Police) 时的特殊规则。

正确答案分析：选项 D

法院应支持 (Grant) 学生的动议，理由是该搜查是在没有合理根据 (Probable Cause) 或搜查令 (Warrant) 的情况下进行的。

推理逻辑：

  • 一般原则：根据 New Jersey v. T.L.O. 案，学校官员为了维持校园秩序，自行搜查学生时只需要合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，无需搜查令。
  • 本案例外：本案中，校长并非出于学校管理目的自行搜查，而是应警方的要求 (at the behest of the police) 进行搜查。
  • 代理人理论：当私人或非执法类政府人员（如校长）在警方的指示下行动时，他们被视为警方的代理人 (Agent)。
  • 结论：既然校长是警方的代理人，就必须遵守警方搜查的严格标准：即必须拥有搜查令 (Warrant) 和合理根据 (Probable Cause)。本案中警方没有搜查令，因此搜查违宪，获得的珠宝应根据排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule) 被排除。
为什么选项 A 错误？

选项 A 引用了标准的“学校搜查规则”（即只需合理怀疑）。这是一个典型的干扰项。

错误原因：该规则仅适用于学校官员独立发起搜查以维护学校环境的情况。一旦警方介入并指挥搜查，为了防止警方利用学校官员规避第四修正案的要求，必须恢复到更严格的搜查令标准。

为什么选项 B 错误？

选项 B 提到了合法逮捕附带搜查 (Search Incident to Lawful Arrest)。

错误原因：虽然这是一种无需搜查令的例外情况，但它要求搜查必须发生在逮捕之后或与逮捕同时发生。本案中，是先非法搜查发现了珠宝，才导致了逮捕。警方不能用搜查出的证据来反向证明搜查的合法性。

为什么选项 C 错误？

选项 C 关注过度武力 (Excessive Force)。

错误原因：虽然校长弄伤学生可能导致民事诉讼（如 Section 1983 侵权诉讼），但单纯的过度武力通常不会导致证据被排除（除非行为极其恶劣以至于“震惊良知”，即 Rochin 标准，但这极少适用）。证据被排除的根本原因是缺乏搜查令，而不是因为校长抢夺背包的动作。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理涉及“第三方搜查”（如室友、家长、学校老师）的题目时，务必首先检查：警方是否参与、鼓励或指挥了这次搜查？

  • 如果是自发行为 ➡️ 私人搜查，第四修正案不适用（证据可用）。
  • 如果是警方指示 ➡️ 视为警方搜查，必须有搜查令或例外情况。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police officers had probable cause to believe that drug dealing was routinely taking place in a particular room at a local motel. The motel manager authorized the officers to enter the room and provided them with a passkey. Without obtaining a warrant, the officers knocked on the room's door, announced their presence, and told the occupants that they would like to speak with them. The officers then heard yelling and repeated flushing of the toilet. They then used the passkey and entered the room, where they saw the occupants dumping drugs into the toilet.
The occupants of the room were charged with drug dealing and have moved to suppress the drugs.
Should the court grant the motion to suppress?

choices.A: No, because exigent circumstances justified the officers' entry.
choices.B: No, because the motel manager consented to the officers' entry.
choices.C: Yes, because exigent circumstances cannot excuse the lack of a warrant.
choices.D: Yes, because the officers cannot benefit from exigent circumstances that they created.

questions.explanation:
Exigent situations/circumstances
(exception to warrant requirement)
Evanescent evidence Imminent threat that evidence of crime will be lost or destroyed
Emergency situation Immediate threat of physical harm to police and/or public
Hot pursuit Immediate pursuit of fleeing felony suspect

A court should grant a motion to suppress evidence obtained during an unreasonable Fourth Amendment search. A search is generally unreasonable if it is conducted without a warrant. But a warrantless search is reasonable when exigent circumstances create a compelling need for immediate police action (Choice C). Exigent circumstances exist when police reasonably believe that a warrantless entry and/or search is needed to:

  • prevent imminent destruction of relevant evidence (ie, evanescent evidence)
  • protect police and/or the public from immediate physical harm (ie, emergency situation) or
  • pursue a fleeing suspect after a felony occurs (ie, hot pursuit).

Here, police officers had probable cause to believe that a motel room was being used for drug dealing. After they knocked, announced their presence, and asked to speak with the occupants, the officers heard yelling and repeated flushing of the toilet. This created a reasonable belief that the occupants were flushing the drugs (imminent destruction of evidence), so exigent circumstances justified the officers' warrantless entry. Therefore, the court should deny the occupants' motion to suppress the drugs found in the room.

(Choice B) Motel managers lack the authority to consent to a warrantless police entry of a guest's room. This is because they do not have the right to use or occupy the room during the guest's stay (no actual authority) and courts have held that police cannot reasonably believe that managers do (no apparent authority).

(Choice D) Police cannot benefit from exigent circumstances that they created by engaging (or threatening to engage) in conduct that violates the Fourth Amendment—eg, by immediately kicking down a door to obtain entry. But since the officers acted lawfully when they knocked on the door and announced their presence, they did not create the exigent circumstance. Therefore, this is not a basis for granting the occupants' motion to suppress.

📌 Educational Objective

An exigent circumstance permits police to conduct a warrantless search when they reasonably believe that it is necessary to (1) prevent imminent destruction of relevant evidence, (2) protect police and/or the public from immediate physical harm, or (3) pursue a fleeing suspect after a felony occurs.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Kentucky v. King, 563 U.S. 452, 460–62 (2011) (explaining the exigent circumstances exception to the warrant requirement).
questions.zh-question:
警官有合理理由相信，在一家当地汽车旅馆的某个特定房间里，经常有毒品交易发生。汽车旅馆经理授权警官进入该房间，并向他们提供了一把万能钥匙。在未获得搜查令的情况下，警官们敲了房间的门，表明了身份，并告知房客他们想与他们谈话。然后，警官们听到了喊叫声和马桶反复冲水的声音。于是他们使用了万能钥匙进入房间，看到房客正在将毒品倒入马桶。

该房间的房客被控贩毒，并已申请排除这些毒品作为证据。

法院应否批准该排除证据的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为紧急情况为警官的进入提供了正当理由。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为汽车旅馆经理同意了警官的进入。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为紧急情况不能作为没有搜查令的借口。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为警官不能从他们自己制造的紧急情况中获益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Search & Seizure

正确答案：A
(No, because exigent circumstances justified the officers' entry.)

本题考察的核心是美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）中关于无证搜查（Warrantless Search）的例外情况，特别是紧急情况（Exigent Circumstances）的应用。

1. 核心规则：紧急情况例外

通常情况下，警方进入私人住宅（包括酒店房间）进行搜查必须持有搜查令（Warrant）。但在紧急情况（Exigent Circumstances）下，如果警方有合理理由（Probable Cause）相信如果不立即行动会导致严重后果，可以免除搜查令要求。

常见的紧急情况包括：

  • 易逝证据（Evanescent Evidence）： 证据面临被立即销毁的风险。
  • 紧急追捕（Hot Pursuit）： 正在追捕逃跑的重罪嫌疑人。
  • 紧急援助（Emergency Aid）： 需要立即进入以保护生命安全。

在本案中，警方听到“马桶反复冲水的声音”（repeated flushing of the toilet），结合之前的毒品交易情报，这创造了证据正在被销毁（Destruction of Evidence）的合理信念。因此，警方强行进入是合理的。

2. 难点辨析：警方是否“制造”了紧急情况？

这是本题最具迷惑性的地方（对应选项 D）。被告通常会辩称：是警察敲门才导致我们冲毒品的，警察不能利用自己制造的紧急情况来规避搜查令。

关键判例：Kentucky v. King (2011)
美国最高法院裁定：只要警方的行为本身是合法（Lawful）的（例如敲门并表明身份，即 "Knock and Talk"），即使这种行为引发了嫌疑人销毁证据的反应，警方依然可以利用这一紧急情况进入房间。

为何选项 D 错误：
只有当警方通过违反或威胁违反第四修正案的方式（例如大喊“开门，否则我们要把门踢开！”而当时他们并没有搜查令）来制造紧急情况时，才会被禁止利用该紧急情况。本题中，警方只是敲门并要求谈话，这是完全合法的调查手段。

3. 其他选项为何错误
选项 B (Consent by Manager) 错误：
虽然酒店经理有权进入房间进行清洁或维修，但他们没有权限（Authority）同意警方进入客人的房间进行搜查。客人在租住期间对房间享有合理的隐私期待（Expectation of Privacy）。警方不能依赖经理的同意（参考判例 Stoner v. California）。
选项 C (Warrant Required) 错误：
该选项说法过于绝对。紧急情况恰恰是搜查令要求的公认例外（Exception）。只要存在真正的紧急情况，就不需要搜查令。
💡 MBE 考试通关技巧

看到 "Knock and Talk"（警察敲门表明身份）+ "Flushing Sounds"（冲水声/销毁证据的声音）的组合时：

  1. 首先确认警察敲门时没有威胁非法暴力。
  2. 如果行为合法，那么听到的冲水声就构成了销毁证据的紧急情况。
  3. 结论：警方可以立即破门而入，无需搜查令，证据不会被排除。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
Police, who had probable cause to arrest a man for a series of armed robberies, obtained a warrant to arrest him. At 6:00 a.m. they surreptitiously entered the man's house and, with guns drawn, went to the man's bedroom, where they awakened him. Startled, the man asked, "What's going on?" and an officer replied, "We've got you now." Another officer immediately asked the man if he had committed a particular robbery, and the man said that he had. The police then informed him that he was under arrest and ordered him to get dressed.
Charged with robbery, the man has moved to suppress the use of his statement as evidence.
What is the man's best argument for granting his motion?

choices.A: He was not informed that he was under arrest until after he made the statement.
choices.B: The police did not give him the required Miranda warnings.
choices.C: The police did not have a search warrant authorizing entry into the house.
choices.D: The statement was not voluntary.

questions.explanation:
A motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if police obtained that statement in violation of the defendant's constitutional rights—including the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. To comply with this privilege, police must inform suspects of their Miranda rights before a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation occurs when a person is:

  • in custody – placed under formal arrest OR restrained in his/her freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave and
  • subjected to interrogation – questions, words, or actions directed at a suspect that police know or should know are likely to elicit an incriminating response.

Here, the man was in custody when police surreptitiously entered his bedroom with guns drawn at 6:00 a.m. because a reasonable person would not feel free to leave. Police then interrogated the man by asking if he had committed a robbery without first Mirandizing him. Therefore, the best argument for suppressing his incriminating response is that the police did not give him the required Miranda warnings before the custodial interrogation.

(Choice A) Before interrogating a suspect in their custody, police need only inform the suspect of his/her Miranda rights—not that he/she is under arrest.

(Choice B) The police did not give him the required Miranda warnings.

(Choice C) Police may lawfully enter a suspect's home if they have a valid arrest warrant or search warrant. Here, police had a valid arrest warrant that authorized them to enter the man's home, so they did not need a search warrant to do so.

(Choice D) A statement is involuntary if the totality of the circumstances—eg, level of police coercion, length of interrogation, suspect's characteristics, Miranda warnings—shows that it was the product of police coercion. Since challenging the voluntariness of a statement involves more factors than a Miranda challenge, this is not the man's best argument for suppression.

📌 Educational Objective

Officers must administer the Miranda warnings before interrogating a suspect in custody. A suspect is in custody when he/she is placed under formal arrest OR police have restrained his/her freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 444–45 (1966) (listing the warnings required prior to custodial interrogations).
  • Orozco v. Texas, 394 U.S. 324, 327 (1969) (recognizing that suspect can be in custody in his own bedroom).
questions.zh-question:
警方有合理理由（probable cause）逮捕一名涉嫌一系列持械抢劫案的男子，并获得了逮捕令。早上6点，他们偷偷进入该男子的住所，并拔出枪支，进入其卧室将他唤醒。该男子受惊，问道：“怎么回事？”一名警官回答：“我们抓到你了。”另一名警官立即询问该男子是否实施了某一起特定的抢劫案，该男子承认了。随后，警方告知他已被逮捕，并命令他穿上衣服。

该男子被控抢劫罪，他已提出动议，要求排除其陈述作为证据。

支持其动议获准的最佳论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 直到他做出陈述后，才被告知已被逮捕。
zh-choices.B: 警方没有向他发出必要的Miranda警告。
zh-choices.C: 警方没有获得授权进入该住宅的搜查令。
zh-choices.D: 该陈述并非自愿做出。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法与刑诉：宪法保护 / Miranda custody requirement

正确答案：B。要点是：被告人在羁押状态（custody）下接受了会引发自证其罪风险的讯问，却未先获告知 Miranda warnings，因此该陈述最有力的排除理由成立。

核心法律规则

羁押（custody） — 本题的门槛条件：是否已被正式逮捕，或自由被限制到理性人不会觉得可以离开。
讯问（interrogation） — 警方明知或应知会引出不利回答的问题，本题里直接问抢劫事实。
Miranda 警告（Miranda warnings） — 羁押讯问前必须告知的程序性保障，是本题排除陈述的关键。
自证其罪特权（privilege against self-incrimination） — 第五修正案核心保护，防止被迫供述成为证据。
合理人标准（reasonable person standard） — 判断是否在羁押中时，看的不是主观感受，而是客观是否能自由离开。
规则概述

当警方对嫌疑人实施羁押讯问（custodial interrogation）时，必须在提问前先给出 Miranda 警告（Miranda warnings）。若嫌疑人已处于 custody，且问题是为获取可能自认有罪的回应，未警告所得陈述通常可被排除。

Miranda 关注的是“是否在羁押中接受讯问”，而不是“是否已经正式宣布逮捕”。

本题规则 常见混淆规则
Miranda 只看“羁押 + 讯问”，先问后警告就可能压制陈述。 只是说明正式逮捕时间，不自动决定陈述能否使用。
进入住宅、持枪、清晨叫醒，可能构成理性人不会觉得能离开。 搜查令/逮捕令合法性，和是否需要 Miranda 是两条不同问题线。
是否自愿是另一层审查，通常比 Miranda 更广。 把“没警告”直接等同于“非自愿”，属于过度推论。

事实应用逻辑

timing / 时间点 custody / 羁押状态 interrogation / 讯问 Miranda warnings / 警告先行 suppression / 排除证据

第一步，看6:00 a.m.、警察持枪、直接进入卧室并叫醒他；这不是随意谈话场景，而是高度控制环境，理性人很难觉得能自由离开。

第二步，警方在他刚醒来时立刻问“你是否实施了某次抢劫”，这是典型会诱发自认不利事实的 interrogation。

第三步，关键缺口是先问后告知逮捕，而不是先给 Miranda warnings；所以压制的最佳理由是程序性违背第五修正案保障。

清晨进入卧室 持枪控制现场 先问抢劫事实 后告知逮捕

判断顺序：先确认是否 custody，再看是否 interrogation，最后检查是否已先给 Miranda 警告。

常见陷阱：很多考生会被“他当时还没被正式宣布逮捕”误导，但 Miranda 不要求先宣布逮捕才算羁押。只要自由被实质限制到理性人不敢离开，且警方在此状态下发问，就触发警告要求。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

警察在持枪进入卧室并立即提问时，已构成 custodial interrogation；官方规则要求先给 Miranda warnings。题目最强压制点正是先讯问、后警告，故该陈述可争取排除。

为什么排除其他选项：

  • ✕ A：把“未正式宣布逮捕”误当成“尚未羁押”；关键字 理性人不会觉得能离开 已排除它。
  • ✕ C：把进入住宅的争点错拉成搜查令问题；本题争点是 Miranda，不是门票合法性。
  • ✕ D：把“未警告”直接等同于“非自愿”；但自愿性审查还要看胁迫强度，不能只凭这一点成立。
这题建议用什么方法？ 先用“羁押 → 讯问 → 警告”三步法做元素检查，再用时间线定位先后顺序。出题人故意把“正式逮捕时点”和“搜查令”放进来，诱使考生跑偏到程序形式，而忽略真正的 Miranda 触发点。
考试速记：只要看到“自由明显受控 + 警方马上发问”，先想 Miranda warnings；是否已正式逮捕，通常不是决定性前提。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A police officer had a hunch, not amounting to probable cause or reasonable suspicion, that a man was a drug dealer. One day while the officer was on highway patrol, her radar gun clocked the man's car at 68 mph in an area where the maximum posted speed limit was 65 mph. The officer's usual practice was not to stop a car unless it was going at least 5 mph over the posted limit, but contrary to her usual practice, she decided to stop the man's car in the hope that she might discover evidence of drug dealing. After she stopped the car and announced that she would be writing a speeding ticket, the officer ordered the man and his passenger to step out of the car. When the passenger stepped out, the officer saw that the passenger had been sitting on a clear bag of what the officer immediately recognized as marijuana. The officer arrested both the man and the passenger for possession of marijuana.
At their joint trial, the man and the passenger claim that their Fourth Amendment rights were violated because the officer improperly (1) stopped the car for speeding as a pretext for investigating a hunch rather than for the stated purpose of issuing a traffic ticket and (2) ordered the passenger to step out of the car even though there was no reason to believe that the passenger was a criminal or dangerous.
Are the man and the passenger correct?

choices.A: No, as to both the stop of the car and the officer's order that the passenger step out of the car.
choices.B: No as to the stop of the car, but yes as to the officer's order that the passenger step out of the car.
choices.C: Yes, as to both the stop of the car and the officer's order that the passenger step out of the car.
choices.D: Yes as to the stop of the car, but no as to the officer's order that the passenger step out of the car.

questions.explanation:
Man observed speeding
Probable cause
Officer stops
man's car to find evidence
Reasonable seizure
Occupants ordered out
of car
Permitted for
officer safety
Officer sees
marijuana
Evidence in
plain view
Valid arrest

A vehicle stop violates a driver's and a passenger's Fourth Amendment right against unreasonable seizures if the stop is conducted without a warrant or an objectively justifiable basis like:

  • reasonable suspicion – specific and articulable facts to support a belief that a vehicle occupant is, or will be, involved in criminal activity or
  • probable cause – a reasonable belief that an occupant has violated the law (including a traffic law).

A seizure is reasonable—even if it is used as a pretext or excuse to investigate a hunch—if there is an objectively justifiable basis for the vehicle stop. Therefore, the officer's subjective motivation for the stop is irrelevant. The driver and passenger(s) can then be ordered out of the vehicle while the officer addresses the matter justifying the stop since this additional intrusion is minimal and helps ensure officer safety. And evidence discovered during this process can create probable cause for an arrest.

Here, the officer stopped the car because she hoped to find evidence of drug dealing (subjective motivation). But she had probable cause to believe that the man had violated a traffic law since she clocked him driving 68 mph in a 65-mph zone (objectively justifiable basis). Therefore, the stop was reasonable under the Fourth Amendment (Choices C & D). As a result, the officer properly ordered the man and the passenger out of the car while she wrote the speeding ticket (Choices B & C). And since no Fourth Amendment rights were violated, the officer lawfully discovered the marijuana and validly arrested the man and the passenger.

📌 Educational Objective

A warrantless vehicle stop is a reasonable Fourth Amendment seizure if the officer has an objectively justifiable basis for the stop—ie, reasonable suspicion or probable cause. The officer's subjective motivation is irrelevant. And during a legal stop, the officer can order the driver and passenger(s) to exit the vehicle.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • When v. United States, 517 U.S. 806, 813 (1996) (recognizing that an officer's subjective intentions play no role in the reasonableness of a seizure under the Fourth Amendment).
  • Maryland v. Wilson, 519 U.S. 408, 415 (1997); Pennsylvania v. Mimms, 434 U.S. 106, 111 (1977) (holding that an officer can order a driver and passengers out of a vehicle during a valid traffic stop).
questions.zh-question:
一名警官有一种直觉，认为一名男子是毒贩，但这种直觉并未达到“相当理由”(probable cause)或“合理怀疑”(reasonable suspicion)的程度。一天，当这名警官在高速公路上巡逻时，她的雷达测速枪测得该男子的车速为每小时68英里，而该区域的最高限速为每小时65英里。该警官通常的做法是，除非车辆超速至少5英里，否则不会拦车。但与她通常的做法相反，她决定拦下该男子的车，希望能够发现毒品交易的证据。拦下车并宣布她将开具一张超速罚单后，警官命令该男子及其乘客下车。当乘客下车时，警官看到乘客一直坐在一袋透明的袋子上，警官立即认出袋子里装的是大麻。警官以持有大麻的罪名逮捕了该男子和乘客。

在他们的合并审判中，该男子和乘客声称他们受Fourth Amendment保护的权利受到了侵犯，因为警官不当地（1）以超速为借口拦截车辆，实为调查一个直觉，而非为了开具交通罚单的既定目的；以及（2）在没有理由相信乘客是罪犯或有危险的情况下命令其下车。

该男子和乘客的主张是否正确？

zh-choices.A: 否，就拦截车辆以及警官命令乘客下车这两项而言，主张均不正确。
zh-choices.B: 否，就拦截车辆方面而言主张不正确；但就命令乘客下车方面而言主张正确。
zh-choices.C: 是，就拦截车辆以及警官命令乘客下车这两项而言，主张均正确。
zh-choices.D: 是，就拦截车辆方面而言主张正确；但就命令乘客下车方面而言主张不正确。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：
选项 A (No / No)
即：拦截车辆和命令乘客下车均未侵犯权利。

本题考察的是美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）中关于交通拦截（Traffic Stops）的两个核心规则。

考点 1：借口拦截 (Pretextual Stops)

规则：只要警察有拦截车辆的客观依据（Objectively Justifiable Basis），例如观察到交通违规，那么警察的主观动机（Subjective Motivation）就是无关紧要的。

即使警察实际上是想调查毒品（但没有足够的理由），只要车确实超速了，拦截就是合法的。

Case: Whren v. United States (1996)

本案分析：

  • 限速 65 mph，司机开 68 mph。
  • 客观上：已经构成了违反交通法规（Traffic Violation）。这提供了相当理由 (Probable Cause) 进行拦截。
  • 主观上：警察的“直觉”和“通常做法（超速5英里才拦）”在法律上不影响拦截的有效性。
考点 2：命令乘客下车

规则：在合法的交通拦截过程中，出于警官安全（Officer Safety）的考虑，警察有权命令驾驶员和所有乘客下车。

这一命令不需要额外的合理怀疑（Reasonable Suspicion）来证明乘客是危险的或有罪的。

Case: Maryland v. Wilson (1997)

本案分析：

  • 既然拦截本身是合法的（见考点1），警察就有权控制现场。
  • 命令乘客下车是标准的程序性权力，无需证明乘客有嫌疑。
  • 当乘客下车时，大麻暴露在“一目了然” (Plain View) 之下，因此警察可以合法扣押证据并进行逮捕。
💡 MBE 避坑指南

1. 不要被“通常做法”迷惑： 题目中提到警察通常只拦超速5英里以上的车，这属于警察的行政裁量权或个人习惯，不改变法律标准。只要超速1英里，法律上就有权拦截。

2. 区分“命令下车”与“拍身搜查”：

  • 命令下车 (Order out)： 自动允许，无需额外理由。
  • 拍身搜查 (Frisk/Pat-down)： 需要额外的合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，即相信嫌疑人持有武器且危险 (Armed and Dangerous)。
本题只问了“命令下车”，所以是合法的。如果题目问警察能否直接搜身，答案可能不同。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The police suspected a woman of growing marijuana in her private residence. Narcotics officers went to her neighborhood in the middle of the night. Nothing unlawful could be seen from the street, so the officers walked into her neighbors' yard and looked in through the woman's kitchen window, which had neither drapes nor shades. The officers observed what appeared to be marijuana plants being cultivated under grow lights in the kitchen. Using this information, the officers obtained a search warrant. The execution of the warrant netted numerous marijuana plants.
The woman was charged with possession of marijuana. She has moved to suppress the marijuana plants recovered when the warrant was executed, claiming that the evidence supporting the warrant was obtained through a search that violated the Fourth Amendment.
Should the marijuana plants be suppressed?

choices.A: No, because regardless of the lawfulness of the police conduct beforehand, they did obtain a warrant to search the woman's home.
choices.B: No, because the woman could have no reasonable expectation of privacy concerning activities that she exposed to the view of her neighbors.
choices.C: Yes, because no unlawful activities could be observed by the officers from any public vantage point.
choices.D: Yes, because the officers' clandestine observation of the plants violated the woman's reasonable expectation of privacy concerning activities occurring in her home.

questions.explanation:
The woman argued that the recovered marijuana plants should be suppressed because the evidence supporting the search warrant for those plants was obtained through an unlawful Fourth Amendment search. A Fourth Amendment search occurs when one of the following tests is met:

  • Physical trespass test – the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area, like a person's yard, to obtain information.
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invaded (1) a person's subjective expectation of privacy (2) that society would find objectively reasonable.

A search is unlawful if it was conducted without a warrant and no exception to the warrant requirement applies. However, a court will only suppress evidence obtained from an unlawful search if the defendant has standing to challenge it—ie, a legitimate expectation of privacy (or an ownership or possessory interest) in the area or item searched. Therefore, a defendant cannot challenge an unlawful search of a third party's premises since it infringed on the third party's right to privacy—not the defendant's.

Here, a search occurred under the physical trespass test when the officers intruded upon the neighbors' yard. But the woman lacks standing to challenge that search because she has no legitimate privacy expectation in that yard. And though the officers looked through her uncovered window and saw marijuana plants in her kitchen, she had no objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in what she knowingly exposed to others—including her neighbors. Therefore, no search occurred under the reasonable expectation of privacy test, and her motion should be denied.

(Choice A) A court must always determine if a search warrant is supported by valid probable cause—ie, that probable cause stemmed from lawful police conduct. Therefore, the lawfulness of the police conduct before they obtained a search warrant must be considered even after the warrant was issued.

(Choice C) Persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in activities knowingly exposed to others (eg, neighbors). Here, although no unlawful activities could be seen from a public vantage point (eg, the street), the woman's activities could be seen—through an uncovered window—from her neighbors' yard (knowingly exposed to others). As a result, the police did not violate her right to privacy, and her motion will not be granted on this basis.

(Choice D) The officers' clandestine (ie, secret) observation of the marijuana plants did not violate the woman's reasonable expectation of privacy since privacy expectations in activities exposed to one's neighbors (or the public) are objectively unreasonable.

📌 Educational Objective

A Fourth Amendment search occurs when the government (1) physically intrudes upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information or (2) invades a person's subjective and objectively reasonable expectation of privacy. But when police search a third party's premises, a defendant has no standing to challenge that search.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347, 351 (1967) ("What a person knowingly exposes to the public, even in his own home or office, is not a subject of Fourth Amendment protection").
  • Rakas v. Illinois, 439 U.S. 128, 134 (1978) (explaining that a defendant only has standing to contest a search that violated his/her own Fourth Amendment rights).
questions.zh-question:
警方怀疑一名女子在其私人住宅中种植大麻。缉毒警官在半夜前往其住所附近。从街道上看不到任何违法情况，因此警官进入其邻居的院子，通过该女子未拉窗帘也未设遮挡的厨房窗户向内窥视。警官观察到厨房内似乎有大麻植物在生长灯下被培育。利用这些信息，警官获得了一张搜查令。执行该搜查令时查获了大量大麻植物。

该女子被控非法持有大麻。她已提出动议，要求排除执行搜查令时收缴的大麻植物，声称支持该搜查令的证据是通过违反Fourth Amendment的搜查获得的。

这些大麻植物是否应被排除？

zh-choices.A: 不应排除，因为无论警方此前的行为是否合法，他们确实获得了搜查该女子住宅的搜查令。
zh-choices.B: 不应排除，因为该女子对于其暴露给邻居视野的活动，不能有合理的隐私期待。
zh-choices.C: 应排除，因为警官从任何公共视点都无法观察到任何违法活动。
zh-choices.D: 应排除，因为警官对植物的秘密观察侵犯了该女子对其住宅内活动的合理隐私期待。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Fourth Amendment
⚖️ 核心考点：诉讼资格 (Standing) 要对警方的搜查提出异议（Motion to Suppress），被告必须证明自己的第四修正案权利被侵犯了。如果警方侵犯的是第三方的权利，被告无权挑战该证据。

案情逻辑拆解

1
警官进入邻居的院子：
这可能构成了对邻居的非法入侵（Trespass）。但是，本案被告（该女子）对邻居的院子没有所有权或占有权，因此她没有诉讼资格 (Standing) 来挑战警官进入邻居院子的行为。
2
警官透过窗户观察：
该女子没有拉窗帘（neither drapes nor shades）。根据 Katz 测试，对于一个人明知并暴露给公众（knowingly exposes to the public）的事物，不存在合理的隐私期待 (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。
✅ 正确答案：B

理由：因为该女子将厨房内的活动暴露在了邻居可以看到的视野中，她对此没有合理的隐私期待。

虽然警官是从邻居的院子（非公共区域）进行观察的，但由于被告对邻居的院子没有隐私期待，且她自己没有采取措施遮挡视线，因此警方的观察不构成第四修正案下的“搜查”。
❌ 常见误区 (选项 C & D)
  • 选项 C 错误： 即使从“公共视点”（街道）看不到，也不代表她就有隐私权。关键在于她是否将活动暴露给了任何人（包括邻居）。
  • 选项 D 错误： 仅仅因为观察是“秘密的”（clandestine）并不违法。如果警察站在他们有权站的地方（或者至少是被告无权驱逐他们的地方），且被告没有遮挡窗户，那么这种观察就没有侵犯隐私权。
💡 MBE 实战技巧 遇到“非法搜查”题目时，第一步永远是问：“被搜查的地方属于谁？”
如果是第三方的地盘（如邻居的院子、朋友的车但被告只是乘客且无所有权），被告通常没有 Standing 提出异议，即使警方的行为对第三方来说是非法的。
相关判例与原则：
1. Rakas v. Illinois (1978): 被告只能对侵犯其自身隐私权的搜查提出异议。
2. Katz v. United States (1967): "What a person knowingly exposes to the public... is not a subject of Fourth Amendment protection."

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was arrested in his girlfriend's apartment after her neighbors had reported sounds of a struggle and the police had arrived to find the man bent over his girlfriend's prostrate body. The girlfriend was rushed to the hospital where she lapsed into a coma. Despite the explanation that he was trying to revive his girlfriend after she suddenly collapsed, the man was charged with attempted rape and assault after a neighbor informed the police that she had heard the girlfriend sobbing, "No, please no, let me alone."
At trial, the forensic evidence was inconclusive. The jury acquitted the man of attempted rape but convicted him of assault. While he was serving his sentence for assault, the girlfriend, who had never recovered from the coma, died. The man was then indicted and tried on a charge of felony murder. In this common law jurisdiction, there is no statute that prevents a prosecutor from proceeding in this manner, but the man argued that a second trial for felony murder after his original trial for attempted rape and assault would violate the double jeopardy clause.
Is the man's claim correct?

choices.A: No, because he was convicted of the assault charge.
choices.B: No, because his girlfriend had not died at the time of the first trial and he was not placed in jeopardy for murder.
choices.C: Yes, because he was acquitted of the attempted rape charge.
choices.D: Yes, because he was convicted of the assault charge.

questions.explanation:
Double jeopardy clause
Same offense
Distinct offenses
Felony murder
  • Unintentional killing of another person
+
Rape (inherently dangerous felony)
  • Sexual intercourse with woman
    (other than his wife)
  • Against her will by force or threat of
    immediate force
Felony murder
  • Unintentional killing of another person
  • Inherently dangerous felony
Assault
  • Attempted battery or
  • Intentionally placing another in
    apprehension of imminent harmful contact

The Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause protects criminal defendants from undue government harassment by prohibiting (1) multiple punishments for the same offense and (2) a second prosecution for the same offense after a conviction or acquittal. Two crimes constitute the same offense when:

  • both crimes have identical elements or
  • every element of one crime is also an element of the other crime (as seen here).

Here, the man was convicted of assault and acquitted of attempted rape at the first criminal trial. The girlfriend then died, and the man was indicted for felony murder—a crime requiring proof that the defendant:

  • unintentionally killed another
  • during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony.

Since felony murder requires proof of the underlying felony, they are considered the same offense. And because the man was acquitted of attempted rape (underlying felony) at the first trial, a second trial for felony murder (same offense) would violate the double jeopardy clause.

(Choices A & D) Common law assault—an attempted battery or intentionally placing another in apprehension of imminent harmful contact—is not considered an inherently dangerous felony. Therefore, the man's assault conviction is unrelated to his subsequent felony murder charge.

(Choice B) A second prosecution is permitted when the facts necessary to establish the greater offense did not exist at the time of the initial prosecution. Here, the man was acquitted of attempted rape (underlying felony) at the first trial, and no new facts regarding this felony were discovered before the second trial. Therefore, the girlfriend's subsequent death does not permit a second prosecution of felony murder (since attempted rape still cannot be proven). But her death would have permitted a second prosecution had the man been convicted of attempted rape.

📌 Educational Objective

Double jeopardy prohibits multiple punishments or a second prosecution for the same offense. Two crimes are considered the same offense when they have identical elements or when every element of one crime (eg, an underlying felony) is also an element of the other crime (eg, felony murder).

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • Brown v. Ohio, 432 U.S. 161, 169 (1977) ("Whatever the sequence may be, the Fifth Amendment forbids successive prosecution and cumulative punishment for a greater and lesser included offense").
  • Harris v. Oklahoma, 433 U.S. 682, 682–83 (1977); Whalen v. United States, 445 U.S. 684, 694 (1980) (holding that felony murder and the underlying felony are the same offense for double jeopardy purposes).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在其女友的公寓中被捕，此前其邻居报告听到了挣扎的声音，警察赶到后发现该男子正俯身于其女友俯卧的身体上。该女友被紧急送往医院，随后陷入昏迷。尽管该男子解释称他是在女友突然倒下后试图使其苏醒，但在一名邻居告知警方她听到女友哭着说“不，求你了，别碰我”之后，该男子仍被控以强奸未遂罪和攻击罪。

在审判中，法医证据尚无定论。陪审团宣告该男子强奸未遂罪名不成立，但裁定其攻击罪名成立。在他因攻击罪服刑期间，从未从昏迷中恢复的女友死亡。该男子随后被起诉并因重罪谋杀罪受审。在这个普通法司法管辖区，没有成文法阻止检察官以这种方式行事，但该男子辩称，在他因强奸未遂和攻击罪接受初次审判后，再因重罪谋杀罪进行第二次审判将违反一事不再理原则。

该男子的主张是否正确？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为他已被裁定攻击罪名成立。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为在第一次审判时其女友尚未死亡，他并未因谋杀罪而受到审理风险。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为他已被宣告强奸未遂罪名不成立。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为他已被裁定攻击罪名成立。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Double Jeopardy
✅ 正确答案：C
是，因为他已被宣告强奸未遂罪名不成立。
⚖️ 核心法律原则

一事不再理原则 (Double Jeopardy) 禁止对同一罪行进行二次起诉。在重罪谋杀 (Felony Murder) 的语境下，最高法院在 Harris v. Oklahoma 案中确立：

重罪谋杀罪 & 基础重罪
=
同一罪行 (Same Offense)

因为重罪谋杀包含了基础重罪的所有构成要件 (Lesser Included Offense)。

🔍 逻辑推演步骤

1
第一次审判结果：
被告被宣告 强奸未遂 (Attempted Rape) 无罪 (Acquitted)。这意味着法律上认定他没有实施该重罪。
2
第二次起诉意图：
检察官试图起诉 重罪谋杀 (Felony Murder)。
3
关键冲突：
要证明重罪谋杀，检察官必须证明被告实施了基础重罪（即强奸未遂）。
但是，由于被告在第一次审判中已被宣告该罪名不成立，附带禁反言 (Collateral Estoppel) 原则（并入双重危险条款）禁止检察官再次尝试证明这一要素。
❌ 为什么选项 B 是最大的陷阱？

选项 B 引用了著名的 Diaz 例外规则：如果受害者在第一次审判后死亡，通常允许对谋杀进行第二次起诉，因为第一次审判时谋杀罪尚未“完成”。

但是！ 这个例外有一个前提：被告不能已经被宣告基础重罪 无罪。如果基础重罪（强奸未遂）被否定了，那么重罪谋杀的根基就不存在了，无论受害者是否随后死亡。

❌ 为什么选项 A 和 D 错误？

攻击罪 (Assault) 在本案中不是重罪谋杀的基础重罪（通常指内在危险的重罪）。即使它是，强奸未遂的无罪判决才是阻碍起诉重罪谋杀的关键。攻击罪的定罪与重罪谋杀的指控没有直接的阻断或允许关系。

💡 MBE 拿分技巧

看到 Felony Murder 的题目，立即检查 Underlying Felony（基础重罪）的状态：

  • 如果基础重罪被 Acquitted (宣告无罪) ➡️ 绝对不能再起诉重罪谋杀（本题情况）。
  • 如果基础重罪被 Convicted (定罪) 且受害者后来死亡 ➡️ 可以起诉谋杀（这是 Diaz 例外）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was awaiting trial for his involvement in a fraud scheme that preyed on the elderly. Prior to trial, a reporter called the prosecutor to ask some questions for a news story he was writing on the defendant's upcoming trial. The reporter asked the prosecutor if he was confident that the right person had been apprehended for the fraud scheme. The prosecutor responded, "Well, he would not talk to police without his lawyer, and innocent people speak to the police."
Was the prosecutor's statement proper?

choices.A: No, because it is improper for a prosecutor to comment on the defendant's guilt or innocence.
choices.B: No, because it is improper for a prosecutor to speak to a reporter about an ongoing case.
choices.C: Yes, because a prosecutor has a constitutional right to speak freely to reporters.
choices.D: Yes, because a prosecutor is only prohibited from commenting on a defendant's failure to testify at trial.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Sixth Amendment right to jury trial
Applies to serious
crimes
  • General rule – possible sentence of > 6 months' imprisonment (or actual sentence of > 6 months if no statutory maximum provided)
  • Exception – sentence ≤ 6 months if additional penalties are so severe that legislature likely intended for crime to be serious
Waiver • Free, knowing & intelligent request for bench trial
Composition
  • Jury pool – fair cross section of community
  • Impaneled jury – impartial & unbiased
Size
  • State court – at least 6 jury members
  • Federal court – 12 jury members unless parties stipulate otherwise
Unanimity • Unanimous verdict required to convict

The Sixth Amendment guarantees a criminal defendant the right to trial by an impartial jury. Impartiality has two requirements:

  • the jury pool must be selected from a fair cross section of the community and
  • the impaneled jury must be unbiased and able to decide the case based on the evidence presented at trial.

Due to the potential prejudicial impact of such extrajudicial statements on the jury pool, a prosecutor may not express opinions about the defendant's guilt or innocence. This prohibition ensures that the right to a fair trial is not violated before the trial even begins.

Here, the reporter asked the prosecutor if he was confident that the right person had been apprehended. The prosecutor responded, "Well, he would not talk to police without his lawyer, and innocent people speak to the police." This response tends to show that the prosecutor believes that the right person was apprehended, thereby suggesting that the defendant is guilty. And because a prosecutor cannot comment on the defendant's guilt or innocence, the prosecutor's statement was improper.

(Choices B, C, and D) A prosecutor is not prohibited from speaking to reporters about an ongoing case, but a prosecutor is limited in what he can speak about in public in order to ensure a fair trial for the defendant. For example, a prosecutor may not comment on a defendant's failure to testify at trial or on the defendant's guilt or innocence.

📌 Educational Objective

A prosecutor is prohibited from expressing opinions about the defendant's guilt or innocence.

📚 References
  • Sheppard v. Maxwell, 384 U.S. 333, 362 (1966) (stating that due process requires that the accused receive a trial by an impartial jury free from outside influences).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因涉嫌参与针对老年人的诈骗计划而正在候审。审判前，一名记者致电检察官，就他正在撰写的关于被告即将开庭审判的新闻报道提出了一些问题。记者询问检察官是否确信已抓获诈骗计划的正确嫌疑人。检察官回应道：“嗯，他没有律师就不跟警察说话，而无辜的人会跟警察说话。”
检察官的此番言论是否恰当？

zh-choices.A: 不恰当，因为检察官评论被告有罪或无罪是不恰当的。
zh-choices.B: 不恰当，因为检察官就正在进行的案件与记者交谈是不恰当的。
zh-choices.C: 恰当，因为检察官拥有与记者自由交谈的宪法权利。
zh-choices.D: 恰当，因为检察官仅被禁止评论被告在审判中未作证。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman was subpoenaed to appear before a grand jury. When she arrived, she was taken into the grand jury room to be questioned. She answered preliminary questions about her name and address. She was then asked where she had been at a certain time on a specified night when a murder had occurred. Before answering the question, the woman said that she wanted to consult her attorney, who was waiting outside the grand jury room, and she was allowed to do so. When she returned to the grand jury room, she stated that she refused to answer the question because the answer might incriminate her.
The prosecutor believes that the woman's nephew committed the murder. The nephew has said that he was with the woman at the time of the murder, and the prosecutor believes that this alibi is false. The prosecutor does not believe that the woman is guilty of the murder, either as a principal or as an accomplice, although he does believe that the woman may be guilty of other crimes. The prosecutor wants to compel the woman to answer the question by whatever means will result in the least harm to the prosecution's case.
Which of the following steps should the prosecutor take to get the woman to answer the question?

choices.A: Ask the woman's attorney to explain to the woman that the rules of evidence do not apply in grand jury proceedings, and to advise her that she cannot refuse to testify.
choices.B: Prepare the documents necessary to grant the woman immunity from any future prosecution for any crime she might disclose in the course of her testimony.
choices.C: Prepare the documents necessary to grant the woman immunity from any future use against her of her grand jury testimony or any evidence derived from it.
choices.D: Request the grand jury to order the woman to answer the question.

questions.explanation:
Immunity overrides privilege against self-incrimination
Use & derivative
use immunity*		 Prevents use of testimonial communications against witness in criminal
proceeding
Transactional
immunity		 Prevents prosecution of witness for crimes related to testimonial communications
*Minimum grant of immunity required under Fifth Amendment

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination allows a witness to refuse to testify when:

  • the government attempts to compel the witness to testify (eg, by issuing a subpoena) and
  • the witness reasonably believes that testimony may be self-incriminating (ie, could be used, or
    lead to other evidence that might be used, against the witness in a criminal prosecution).

Despite this privilege, the witness can still be compelled to testify if the government grants the witness use
and derivative use immunity—immunity that prevents the witness's testimony, and any evidence derived
from it, from being used against him/her in a criminal proceeding (eg, before a grand jury).

Here, the grand jury attempted to compel the woman to testify when it issued a subpoena. If she
reasonably believes that her answer may incriminate her in other crimes, she can invoke her privilege
against self-incrimination and refuse to answer the prosecutor's question. However, the prosecutor can
override this privilege by preparing the documents necessary to grant her use and derivative use immunity.

(Choice A) Although the rules of evidence do not apply in grand jury proceedings, a witness's privilege
against self-incrimination does apply. Therefore, the woman can refuse to testify unless she is granted immunity.

(Choice B) A witness can also be compelled to testify if he/she receives transactional immunity, which
protects the witness from prosecution for any crimes related to the witness's testimony. However, use and
derivative use immunity is the prosecution's best option because it only prevents the use of the witness's
testimony (and any evidence derived from it) against the witness in a criminal proceeding.

(Choice D) Since the woman possesses the privilege against self-incrimination, the grand jury cannot order
her to answer the question unless she is granted use and derivative use immunity or transactional immunity.

📌 Educational Objective

A witness can be compelled to testify—even after invoking his/her privilege against self-incrimination—if
he/she is granted use and derivative use immunity, which prevents the witness's testimony (or any evidence
derived from it) from being used against the witness in a criminal prosecution.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Kastigar v. United States, 406 U.S. 441, 452–53 (1972) (explaining use and derivative use immunity).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性被传唤至大陪审团前作证。她到达后，被带入大陪审团室接受讯问。她回答了关于姓名和地址的初步问题。随后，她被问及在谋杀案发生的特定夜晚的某个时间，她身在何处。在回答该问题前，该女性表示希望咨询她正在大陪-审团室外等候的律师，并获得了许可。回到大陪审团室后，她声明拒绝回答该问题，因为答案可能会使她自证其罪。

检察官认为该女性的侄子犯下了谋杀罪。该侄子声称案发时与该女性在一起，但检察官认为这个不在场证明是伪造的。检察官不认为该女性犯有谋杀罪，无论是作为主犯还是从犯，但他确实认为该女性可能犯有其他罪行。检察官希望通过对控方案件损害最小的方式，强迫该女性回答问题。

检察官应采取以下哪一步骤来让该女性回答问题？

zh-choices.A: 要求该女性的律师向她解释，证据规则不适用于大陪审团程序，并建议她不能拒绝作证。
zh-choices.B: 准备必要的文件，授予该女性豁免权，使其免于因其证词中可能披露的任何罪行而在未来受到任何起诉。
zh-choices.C: 准备必要的文件，授予该女性豁免权，使其在大陪审团的证词或由此衍生的任何证据，在未来均不得用于对其不利的指控。
zh-choices.D: 请求大陪审团命令该女性回答问题。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

大陪审团与第五修正案豁免权
核心考点：强制证言与豁免权 根据美国宪法第五修正案 (Fifth Amendment)，任何人不得被迫在刑事案件中自证其罪。这一特权适用于大陪审团 (Grand Jury) 程序。

要强迫证人放弃该特权并作证，政府必须授予其豁免权 (Immunity)。

两种豁免权的较量

本题的关键在于区分两种不同类型的豁免权，并根据题目中“对控方案件损害最小”的要求进行选择。

类型 定义与效力
使用及衍生使用豁免权
(Use and Derivative Use Immunity)		 范围较窄：仅保证不使用该证词及其衍生的证据来指控证人。
后果：如果检方有完全独立的证据来源，仍可起诉证人。这是宪法要求的最低限度。
交易豁免权
(Transactional Immunity)		 范围最宽：如同“洗澡”一样，彻底免除因证词涉及的罪行而受到的任何起诉。
后果：即使有独立证据，也不能起诉证人。

选项深度解析

✅ 选项 C (正确答案)

授予使用及衍生使用豁免权。

理由：题目明确指出检察官认为该女性可能犯有“其他罪行”，并希望采取“对控方案件损害最小”的手段。
根据最高法院判例 Kastigar v. United States，使用及衍生使用豁免权足以满足第五修正案的要求并强迫证人作证。同时，它为检方保留了未来若发现独立证据仍可起诉该女性的可能性。这是检方的最佳策略。

❌ 选项 B (错误)

授予交易豁免权。

理由：虽然这也能强迫作证，但它的保护范围太广（Blanket protection）。如果授予此权，检方将永远无法起诉该女性在该证词中披露的任何罪行，这违背了题目中“损害最小”的目标。

❌ 选项 A (错误)

告知证据规则不适用。

理由：虽然联邦证据规则 (Federal Rules of Evidence) 大多不适用于大陪审团（例如允许传闻证据），但特权 (Privileges) 是例外。第五修正案的反对自证其罪特权在大陪审团中依然有效。

❌ 选项 D (错误)

直接命令回答。

理由：如果没有授予豁免权，大陪审团无权命令证人放弃宪法赋予的沉默权。这种命令是违宪的。

🎓 MBE 答题技巧：
当题目问及“检察官应采取什么行动”且涉及第五修正案时，请注意区分合宪性 (Constitutionality) 和 策略性 (Strategy)。

Use/Derivative Use Immunity 是打破沉默权的“万能钥匙”，也是检方最喜欢的工具，因为它既符合宪法（Kastigar 标准），又保留了起诉的可能性。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The police had accumulated reliable information that a man operated a large cocaine-distribution network, that he and his accomplices often resorted to violence, and that they kept a small arsenal of weapons in his home.
One day, the police received reliable information that a large brown suitcase with leather straps containing a supply of cocaine had been delivered to the man's home and that it would be moved to a distribution point the next morning. The police obtained a valid search warrant to search for and seize the brown suitcase and the cocaine, and they went to the man's house.
The police knocked on the man's door and called out, "Police. Open up. We have a search warrant." After a few seconds with no response, the police forced the door open and entered. Hearing noises in the basement, the police ran down there and found the man with a large brown suitcase with leather straps. They seized the suitcase and put handcuffs on the man. A search of his person revealed a .45-caliber pistol. The man cursed the police and said, "You never would have caught me with the stuff if it hadn't been for that lousy snitch!"
The police then fanned out through the house, looking in every room and closet. They found no one else, but one officer found an Uzi automatic weapon in a box on a closet shelf in the man's bedroom.
In addition to charges relating to the cocaine in the suitcase, the man is charged with unlawful possession of weapons. The man moves pretrial to suppress the use as evidence of the weapons seized by the police and of the statement he made.
As to the Uzi automatic weapon, should the court grant the man's motion to suppress?

choices.A: No, because the police were lawfully in the bedroom and the weapon was immediately identifiable as being subject to seizure.
choices.B: No, because the police were lawfully in the house and had probable cause to believe that weapons were in the house.
choices.C: Yes, because once the object of the warrant—the brown suitcase—had been found and seized, no further search of the house was permitted.
choices.D: Yes, because the search exceeded the scope needed to find out if other persons were present.

questions.explanation:
A court should suppress evidence taken during a Fourth Amendment search or seizure conducted without a warrant or an exception to the warrant requirement. A protective sweep—ie, a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—is reasonable if:

  • police have a reasonable suspicion (ie, a belief based on specific and articulable facts) that there is someone who poses a threat in the area being swept and
  • the sweep is limited to a cursery inspection of places in which a person could hide (eg, closet, laundry room).

Evidence or contraband found in plain view during a protective sweep may be seized without a warrant and admitted against the defendant at trial.

Here, the man was known to have violent accomplices, so the police had a reasonable suspicion that there was someone who posed a threat in the home. This authorized the protective sweep after the suitcase was seized and the man was arrested (Choice C). But that sweep should have been limited to places where persons could hide—not a box on a closet shelf. Therefore, the Uzi found in that box should be suppressed.

(Choice A) The police were lawfully in the bedroom and the Uzi was immediately identifiable as contraband once the box in the closet was opened. But they wrongfully opened that box since a person could not hide there. Therefore, the Uzi found in the box should not be admitted as evidence at trial.

(Choice B) Although the police were lawfully in the house to execute the search warrant for the suitcase and cocaine, the warrant did not authorize the seizure of weapons. And although the police had probable cause to believe that there were weapons in the house, this did not permit their continued search of the home once the suitcase and cocaine were seized.

📌 Educational Objective

Police may conduct a protective sweep—a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest— if (1) they have a reasonable suspicion that there is a dangerous person in the area to be swept and (2) the search is limited to a cursory inspection of places where a person could hide.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Maryland v. Buie, 494 U.S. 325, 334–36 (1990) (explaining that officers may conduct a protective sweep if they have reasonable suspicion that a dangerous person is in the area swept).
questions.zh-question:
警方已掌握可靠情报，一名男子经营着一个庞大的可卡因分销网络，他和他的同伙经常诉诸暴力，并在其家中存放了少量武器。

一天，警方接到可靠情报，一个装有可卡因的带皮带的棕色大手提箱已被送到该男子家中，并将在第二天早上被转移到一个分销点。警方获得了一份有效的搜查令，以搜查并扣押该棕色手提箱和可卡因，然后他们前往该男子的住所。

警察敲了敲该男子的门，并喊道：“警察。开门。我们有搜查令。”几秒钟后无人回应，警察便强行破门而入。听到地下室有噪音，警察跑下楼，发现该男子和一个带皮带的棕色大手提箱。他们扣押了手提箱，并给该男子戴上手铐。对其进行人身搜查时，发现了一把.45口径的手枪。该男子咒骂警察说：“要不是那个该死的告密者，你们根本抓不到我的人赃俱获！”

随后，警察在整栋房子里散开，搜查了每个房间和壁橱。他们没有发现其他人，但一名警官在该男子卧室的一个壁橱架子上的盒子里发现了一把Uzi自动武器。

除了与手提箱中的可卡因有关的指控外，该男子还被控非法持有武器。该男子在审前提出动议，要求排除警方缴获的武器及其所作陈述作为证据使用。

关于那把Uzi自动武器，法院是否应批准该男子的排除动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为警察合法地身处卧室，并且该武器可立即被辨认为应予扣押的物品。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为警察合法地身处该房屋内，并有合理根据相信房屋内有武器。
zh-choices.C: 是的，因为一旦搜查令的目标——那个棕色手提箱——被找到并扣押，就不再允许对房屋进行进一步搜查。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为搜查超出了查明是否有其他人在场所需的范围。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Search & Seizure
核心考点：保护性扫视

本题考察的是第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）下，警方在执行逮捕时进行保护性扫视（Protective Sweep）的合法范围。

根据最高法院判例 Maryland v. Buie (1990)，警方在逮捕嫌疑人时，如果基于合理怀疑（Reasonable Suspicion）认为现场可能藏有其他构成威胁的人员，可以对房屋进行快速扫视。

🔍 法律规则详解

保护性扫视必须满足两个条件：

  • 目的限制：仅为了寻找可能伏击警察的人（Persons），而不是寻找证据。
  • 范围限制：仅限于检查能够藏人的地方（Places where a person could hide）。
✅ 正确答案分析 (D)

选项 D 是正确的。

推理逻辑：

  1. 搜查令结束：警方一旦在地下室找到了搜查令指定的目标（手提箱），搜查令的效力即告终止。他们不能继续依据搜查令搜查房屋。
  2. 扫视的启动：由于警方有情报显示嫌疑人有暴力同伙，他们在逮捕后有权进行“保护性扫视”以确保安全。
  3. 范围越界：扫视只能查看能藏人的地方（如衣柜、床下）。一个人不可能藏在壁橱架子上的盒子里。

因此，打开盒子寻找武器超出了“寻找人员”的必要范围，违反了第四修正案。该证据（Uzi冲锋枪）应被排除。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

  • 选项 A (Plain View): “一目了然法则”前提是警察必须合法处于该位置。虽然警察可以进入卧室扫视，但他们无权打开那个盒子。因为盒子内部不是“一目了然”的，且人藏不进去，所以打开盒子的行为是非法的。
  • 选项 B (Probable Cause): 即使警方有“合理根据”相信屋里有武器，但在没有针对武器的搜查令（Search Warrant）或紧急情况（Exigent Circumstances）下，他们不能进行无证搜查。搜查令仅限于毒品手提箱。
  • 选项 C (Too Broad): 这个选项错在过于绝对。它声称找到手提箱后“不允许任何进一步搜查”。实际上，为了警员安全，保护性扫视是允许的，只是不能搜查无法藏人的微小空间。
💡 MBE 实战技巧：

记住“大象装不进火柴盒”原则！

如果警方依据搜查令找“被盗的钢琴”，他们不能打开抽屉搜查；如果他们找“非法入境者”或进行“保护性扫视”，他们不能打开放在架子上的小盒子。

解题关键：永远先看搜查的目标是什么，再判断搜查的物理范围是否合理。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A police officer stopped a driver who had run a red light. Upon approaching the car, the officer noticed a strong odor of alcohol and immediately asked whether the driver had been drinking. The driver admitted having had several alcoholic drinks that evening.
The driver, charged with driving while intoxicated, moved to suppress the officer's testimony regarding the driver's statement about his drinking. The driver argued that the officer had elicited the statement without providing the requisite Miranda warnings. The prosecutor has responded that the statement should be allowed in the prosecution's case-in-chief or, at a minimum, should be allowed as impeachment in the event the driver testifies and denies drinking.
How should the court rule regarding the driver's statement admitting his drinking?

choices.A: The statement should be allowed, because although the driver was in custody, the officer's spontaneous utterance upon smelling alcohol did not rise to the level of interrogation.
choices.B: The statement should be allowed, because the driver was not in custody for Miranda purposes when the admission was made.
choices.C: The statement should be suppressed both in the prosecution's case-in-chief and as impeachment evidence, even if the driver testifies.
choices.D: The statement should be suppressed in the prosecution's case-in-chief, but it may be used as impeachment evidence if the driver testifies.

questions.explanation:
A defendant's motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if law enforcement failed to provide Miranda warnings prior to a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation occurs when a person is:

  • in custody – placed under formal arrest or restrained in his/her freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter and leave and
  • subjected to interrogation – express questions, words, or actions directed at a suspect that an officer knows or should know are likely to elicit an incriminating response.

Although traffic stops restrain freedom of movement, drivers are generally not in custody for Miranda purposes because those police encounters are typically brief.

Here, the officer stopped the driver for a red-light violation (traffic stop). The officer noticed a strong odor of alcohol and immediately asked the driver if he had been drinking (interrogation). However, the officer was not required to give Miranda warnings before doing so because the driver was not in custody for Miranda purposes. Therefore, the driver's statement admitting his drinking should be allowed in the prosecution's case-in-chief.

(Choice A) The officer's question about drinking was directed at the driver and reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response; therefore, it was an interrogation. But since the driver was not in custody, his statement should be admitted.

(Choices C & D) Since the officer was not required to provide Miranda warnings, the prosecution should be allowed to use the driver's admission in its case-in-chief. But even if that admission was suppressed, it could be used as impeachment evidence if the driver later testifies.

📌 Educational Objective

Miranda warnings protect persons from self-incrimination when they are in custody and subjected to interrogation (custodial interrogations). Since drivers are generally not in custody during traffic stops, Miranda warnings need not be provided before brief police questioning.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berkemer v. McCarty, 468 U.S. 420, 440 (1984) (recognizing that a person is not in custody during an investigatory detention).
questions.zh-question:
一名警察拦下了一名闯红灯的司机。在靠近车辆时，警察闻到一股浓烈的酒味，并立即询问司机是否饮酒。司机承认当晚喝了几杯含酒精的饮料。

该司机被控酒后驾车，并动议排除警察就司机关于其饮酒的陈述所作的证词。司机辩称，警察在未提供必要的米兰达警告的情况下诱使其作出陈述。检察官则回应称，该陈述应被允许在控方主案中采纳，或者至少在司机作证并否认饮酒时，应被允许用作弹劾证据。

法院应如何就司机承认其饮酒的陈述作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 该陈述应被采纳，因为尽管司机处于被羁押状态，但警察在闻到酒味后的自发询问并未达到审讯的程度。
zh-choices.B: 该陈述应被采纳，因为在作出承认时，司机并未因米兰达规则之目的而处于被羁押状态。
zh-choices.C: 无论司机是否作证，该陈述在控方主案中和作为弹劾证据都应被排除。
zh-choices.D: 该陈述在控方主案中应被排除，但如果司机作证，则可被用作弹劾证据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Miranda Warnings

✅ 正确答案：B 该陈述应被采纳，因为在作出承认时，司机并未因米兰达规则之目的而处于被羁押状态 (Not in custody for Miranda purposes)。
⚖️ 核心法律规则

本题考察的是美国宪法第五修正案下的米兰达警告 (Miranda Warnings) 触发条件。

只有在同时满足以下两个条件时，警方才必须提供米兰达警告：
  1. 羁押 (Custody)： 嫌疑人的行动自由受到重大限制（类似正式逮捕）。
  2. 审讯 (Interrogation)： 警方明知可能引出有罪供述的言语或行为。
