初步接触 (Initial Contact) 警察询问，女子无视并走开。此时为自愿接触，女子有权离开。
命令与服从 (Command & Submission) 警察喊“站住”，女子停下并举手。关键点：此时发生了扣押 (Seizure)。
丢弃物品 (Discarding Object) 女子在被扣押后扔掉可卡因。
搜查与逮捕 (Search & Arrest) 警察捡起物品并逮捕女子。
核心考点：Terry Stop 的合法性
根据 Terry v. Ohio，警察进行调查性截停（Investigatory Stop）必须基于合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，即必须有具体的事实表明犯罪正在进行或即将发生。
判例规则 (Rule of Law):
仅身处“高犯罪率地区”(High-crime area) 本身不足以构成拦截公民的合理怀疑 (Brown v. Texas)。

在本案中，警察拦截该女子的唯一依据是她出现在毒品交易频发的地区。当她行使权利拒绝回答并走开时，警察并没有额外的理由怀疑她犯罪。因此，警察命令她停下（且她确实停下了）构成了一次非法扣押 (Unlawful Seizure)。

✅ 正确答案：C

理由：因为警方是在非法扣押之后才获得了可卡因。

根据证据排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule)，由于最初的截停（Seizure）是非法的（缺乏合理怀疑），因此作为该非法行为直接结果（Direct Result）而获得的所有证据（即被丢弃的可卡因）都必须被排除。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误： 即使后来发现了毒品（有了逮捕的合理根据 Probable Cause），但这不能反过来证明最初拦截行为的合法性。
选项 B 错误（常见陷阱）： 虽然通常丢弃物（Abandoned Property）不受宪法保护，但如果是因警察的非法行为（非法截停）而被迫丢弃的，这种丢弃不被视为“自愿”，证据仍需排除。
选项 D 错误： 警察是否知道那是可卡因并不重要，关键在于截停人本身是否合法。
MBE 策略：先判断警察行为是否合法，再看证据链是否被污染。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police officers had probable cause to believe that a man had committed a series of armed bank robberies with an accomplice.
The officers obtained a valid arrest warrant for the man and went to his house to arrest him. The officers found the front door ajar and could hear a radio playing inside. They knocked on the door, identified themselves as police officers, and stated that they had a warrant. Getting no response, the officers entered the house. After the officers called the man's name several times and again identified themselves as police officers, the man emerged from the basement and was arrested. The officers went into the basement to look for the accomplice. They opened a closet door and found cocaine in plain view. They did not find the accomplice.
The man was indicted for cocaine possession. He has moved to suppress the cocaine as evidence on the ground that it was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment.
Should the court grant the motion to suppress?

choices.A: No, because the officers discovered the cocaine during a lawful protective sweep of the house looking for the man's accomplice.
choices.B: No, because the search was incident to the man's arrest.
choices.C: Yes, because the officers did not have a search warrant.
choices.D: Yes, because the officers did not have probable cause to believe that cocaine would be in the closet.

questions.explanation:
Valid arrest warrant issued
Officers knock & announce presence
Entry into home permitted
Officers enter & arrest man
Valid arrest
Believe armed suspect present
Authorized protective sweep
Cocaine found in closet
Plain view
(admissible)

A court should deny a defendant's motion to suppress if the contested evidence was obtained during a reasonable Fourth Amendment search. A protective sweep—ie, a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—is reasonable if:

  • police have a reasonable suspicion (ie, a belief based on specific, articulable facts) that the premises harbor someone who poses a threat to the safety of persons at the scene and
  • the sweep is limited to a cursory inspection of places where a person could hide.

Evidence or contraband found in plain view during the sweep may be seized without a warrant and admitted at trial.

Here, officers arrested the man pursuant to a warrant as he emerged from the basement of his home. The officers then conducted a protective sweep of the premises. That sweep was lawful because the man was suspected of committing armed bank robberies with an accomplice (reasonable suspicion of danger) and the sweep was limited to the basement and closet (places a person could hide). Therefore, the cocaine found in plain view during the sweep was lawfully seized and should be admitted (not suppressed) at trial.

(Choice B) The search incident-to-lawful-arrest exception to the warrant requirement allows officers to conduct a warrantless search of an arrested person and the areas in his/her immediate reach. This exception does not apply here since the basement was not in the man's reach. Therefore, this is not a basis to deny the motion to suppress.

(Choice C) Police do not need a search warrant to conduct a protective sweep—or to seize evidence found in plain view during that sweep—if they reasonably suspect that a dangerous person is in the area to be searched (and the search is limited to places a person could hide).

(Choice D) Police did not have probable cause to believe that cocaine would be found in the closet. But since the cocaine was discovered during a lawful protective sweep, they did not need probable cause (or a warrant) to seize it.

📌 Educational Objective

Police can conduct a protective sweep—a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—if they reasonably suspect that a dangerous person may be on the premises and the sweep is limited to places where a person may be found. Evidence found in plain view during the sweep may be seized without a warrant.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Maryland v. Buie, 494 U.S. 325, 334–36 (1990) (explaining that officers may conduct a protective sweep if they have reasonable suspicion that a dangerous person is in the area swept).
questions.zh-question:
警官有相当理由相信一名男子与一名同伙共同实施了一系列持械银行抢劫。

警官获得了对该男子的有效逮捕令，并前往其住所进行逮捕。警官发现前门虚掩，并能听到室内有收音机在播放。他们敲了门，表明自己是警察，并声明他们持有逮捕令。在没有得到回应后，警官进入了房屋。在警官多次呼叫该男子姓名并再次表明警察身份后，该男子从地下室走出来并被逮捕。警官进入地下室寻找同伙。他们打开一个壁橱门，发现了清晰可见的可卡因。他们没有找到同伙。

该男子因持有可卡因而被起诉。他以可卡因是违反第四修正案获得的为由，申请排除该证据。

法院是否应批准该排除动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为警官是在为寻找该男子的同伙而对房屋进行合法的保护性搜查时发现可卡因的。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该搜查是附随于该男子被捕而进行的。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为警官没有搜查令。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为警官没有相当理由相信壁橱里会有可卡因。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A 法院不应批准排除动议，因为这是合法的保护性搜查 (Protective Sweep)。
⚖️ 核心法律规则：保护性搜查
Protective Sweep (Maryland v. Buie)
这是一种为了保护警察和现场人员安全而进行的快速、有限的搜查。它是无证搜查 (Warrantless Search) 的例外情况之一。

根据最高法院判例，保护性搜查分为两种情况，本题考查的是第二种（需要合理怀疑）：

  • 前提：警察必须有合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，认为逮捕现场可能藏匿着其他危险人物。
  • 范围：仅限于对可能藏人的地方（如壁橱、床底）进行粗略检查 (Cursory Inspection)。
  • 结果：在合法搜查范围内，如果发现一目了然 (Plain View) 的违禁品，可以合法扣押。
🔍 本案逻辑链条

让我们将规则应用到题目中的事实：

1. 为什么可以搜查地下室？
警察知道嫌疑人有同伙 (Accomplice) 且涉及持械 (Armed) 抢劫。这构成了“存在危险人物”的合理怀疑。嫌疑人刚从地下室出来，警察有理由检查地下室是否藏有同伙。

2. 为什么可以打开壁橱？
壁橱是一个可以藏人 (Places a person could hide) 的空间。搜查范围是合法的。

3. 为什么可卡因可以作为证据？
虽然警察没有搜查毒品的搜查令，也没有理由相信壁橱里有毒品，但他们在合法寻找同伙时，发现了一目了然 (Plain View) 的可卡因。因此，扣押是合法的。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B (SITA) 错误
这是最强的干扰项。附随逮捕的搜查 (Search Incident to Arrest) 仅限于被捕者的“翼展范围” (Wingspan/Immediate control)。嫌疑人已被逮捕，地下室通常超出了其直接控制范围。本题的合法性基础是“保护性搜查”，而非 SITA。
选项 C (无搜查令) 错误
保护性搜查是第四修正案搜查令要求的例外 (Exception)。只要满足条件，不需要搜查令。
选项 D (无相当理由) 错误
警察不需要对“发现毒品”有相当理由 (Probable Cause)。他们只需要对“存在危险人物”有合理怀疑。一旦进入合法位置，Plain View 规则允许扣押毒品。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理第四修正案题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 是否有搜查令？ (本题：有逮捕令，无搜查令)
  2. 是否适用例外情况？
    • 如果是为了找证据 ➔ 考虑 SITA（仅限翼展范围）。
    • 如果是为了找人/安全 ➔ 考虑 Protective Sweep（全屋可能藏人的地方）。
  3. Plain View 的应用： 只要警察合法待在那个位置，看到的东西就是合法的证据。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
During jury selection at a criminal trial, the defendant used all of his peremptory challenges to strike men from the jury. The prosecution objected to the defendant's actions. The defendant provided a gender-neutral reason for striking the potential male jurors, which the court found to be pretextual.
Was the defendant's use of peremptory challenges unconstitutional?

choices.A: No, because the Constitution does not prohibit criminal defendants from exercising discriminatory peremptory challenges.
choices.B: No, because the defendant struck members of his own gender from the jury.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant's actions prevented the selection of an impartial jury.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant's actions violated the equal protection clause.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Jury panel challenges
Peremptory Disqualify potential juror for any reason except discrimination based on race, ethnicity, or sex
For cause Disqualify potential juror for a stated reason for believing juror cannot be fair or impartial (eg, bias, prejudice, past experience)

Peremptory challenges are objections to potential jurors that can generally be raised without any reason or explanation during the jury-selection process. However, the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause prohibits prosecutors and criminal defendants from striking potential jurors based solely on their race, ethnicity, or gender. The following three-part test (the Batson test) is used to determine whether a peremptory challenge has violated the equal protection clause:

  • The moving party must establish a prima facie case of discrimination (e.g., the defendant used peremptory challenges to strike only male jurors).
  • The party who exercised the peremptory challenge must then provide a neutral reason for the peremptory challenge (e.g., the strikes were based on age, not gender).
  • If a neutral reason is provided, then the burden shifts back to the moving party to prove that the nonmoving party's reason was pretextual (e.g., the defendant struck a 21-year-old man but not a 21-year-old woman).

Here, the court found that the criminal defendant's reason for striking only men from the jury was pretextual. Therefore, the defendant's use of peremptory challenges was unconstitutional because the challenges violated the equal protection clause.

(Choice A) The equal protection clause prohibits prosecutors and criminal defendants from exercising discriminatory peremptory challenges by striking potential jurors based solely on their race, ethnicity, or gender.

(Choice B) The equal protection clause prohibits a party from striking potential jurors based solely on their gender—regardless of whether the party is a member of that gender. That is because litigants and potential jurors alike have a right to jury-selection procedures that are free from racial, ethnic, and gender discrimination.

(Choice C) Criminal defendants have a Sixth Amendment right to an impartial jury (i.e., an impartial group of citizens selected from a fair cross-section of the community). However, this right does not trump equal protection principles that preclude all litigants from using peremptory challenges in a discriminatory manner.

📌 Educational Objective

The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause prohibits prosecutors and criminal defendants from striking potential jurors based solely on their race, ethnicity, or gender.

📚 References
  • Batson v. Kentucky, 476 U.S. 79, 84 (1986) (setting forth the three-prong test for evaluating when the use of peremptory challenges violates the equal protection clause).
  • J.E.B. v. Alabama, 511 U.S. 127, 130–31 (1994) (holding that peremptory challenges cannot be used to strike jurors based on their gender).
questions.zh-question: 在刑事审判的陪审团遴选过程中，被告用尽了他所有的无因回避（peremptory challenges）以将男性从陪审团中排除。控方反对被告的行为。被告为排除这些潜在男性陪审员提供了一个性别中立的理由，但法院认为该理由是借口（pretextual）。被告使用无因回避（peremptory challenges）是否违宪？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为宪法不禁止刑事被告行使歧视性的无因回避（peremptory challenges）。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为被告将自己性别的成员从陪审团中排除。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为被告的行为阻止了公正陪审团的选出。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为被告的行为违反了平等保护条款（equal protection clause）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
On an interstate highway, a police officer encountered a car being driven well below the posted minimum speed limit. The officer stopped the car. After approaching the driver's window, the officer noticed that the driver's eyes were bloodshot and that the driver appeared nervous. The officer asked if the driver had any weapons or drugs in his possession, and the driver informed the officer that he had a handgun in his backseat but that he was licensed to lawfully carry it. The officer immediately asked the driver to exit the car. The driver complied.
The officer asked the driver if he would consent to a search of his car and the driver replied, "Sure." While searching the car, the officer found two pounds of marijuana, a scale, and several plastic baggies underneath the passenger seat. The officer asked, "Does this marijuana and paraphernalia belong to you?" The driver confessed that it did. The officer then handcuffed and arrested the driver for possession of marijuana with intent to distribute.
If the driver moves to suppress his admission about the marijuana and paraphernalia belonging to him, how will the court likely rule on his motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the driver consented to the officer's search of his car during the traffic stop.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the driver was not in custody at the time that he made the incriminating statement to the officer.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the driver was effectively placed in custody when he was ordered out of his car by the officer.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the officer's question was intended to elicit an incriminating response from the driver.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

A motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if law enforcement failed to provide Miranda warnings prior to a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation occurs when a person is:

  • in custody – placed under formal arrest or so restrained in his/her freedom of movement that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter and
  • subjected to interrogation – express questions, words, or actions directed at the person that an officer knows or should know are likely to elicit an incriminating response.

Although traffic stops restrain freedom of movement, drivers are generally not in custody for Miranda purposes because such encounters are typically brief and temporary.

Here, the driver made an incriminating statement when asked whether the marijuana and paraphernalia belonged to him. But since the driver was not in custody during this traffic stop, the officer did not need to administer Miranda warnings. Therefore, the court will likely deny the driver's motion to suppress.

(Choice A) The driver's consent to a search of his car pertained to his Fourth Amendment protection against unreasonable searches and seizures—not the admissibility of his statement. The determining factor for the statement's admissibility is whether the driver was subjected to a custodial interrogation.

(Choice C) Merely asking a person to step out of the vehicle during a traffic stop does not render the person "in custody" for Miranda purposes.

(Choice D) The officer's question to the driver was intended to elicit an incriminating response. However, the driver was not entitled to Miranda warnings because he was not in custody.

📌 Educational Objective

Miranda warnings must be provided to suspects before they are subjected to custodial interrogations. Since drivers are generally not in custody during traffic stops, Miranda warnings are not needed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berkemer v. McCarty, 468 U.S. 420, 440 (1984) (recognizing that a person is not in custody during an investigatory detention).
questions.zh-question:
在一条州际公路上，一名警官遇到一辆远低于规定最低限速行驶的汽车。警官拦停了该车。靠近驾驶员车窗后，警官注意到驾驶员双眼充血，神情紧张。警官询问驾驶员是否持有任何武器或毒品，驾驶员告知警官其后座有一把手枪，但他持有合法携带该枪支的许可证。警官立即要求驾驶员下车。驾驶员遵从了指示。

警官询问驾驶员是否同意搜查其车辆，驾驶员回答：“当然可以。”在搜查车辆时，警官在乘客座位下方发现了两磅大麻、一个秤和几个塑料袋。警官问道：“这些大麻和相关用具是你的吗？”驾驶员承认是他的。警官随后给驾驶员戴上手铐，并以意图分销而持有大麻的罪名将其逮捕。

如果驾驶员提出动议，要求排除其关于大麻和相关用具归其所有的供认，法院将可能如何裁定该动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为在交通截停期间，驾驶员同意了警官对其车辆的搜查。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为驾驶员在向警官作出有罪陈述时，并未处于羁押状态。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为当警官命令驾驶员下车时，驾驶员已被有效置于羁押状态。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为警官的问题旨在引出驾驶员的有罪答复。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Miranda Rights
✅ 正确答案：选项 B
核心考点：羁押讯问 (Custodial Interrogation)

本题考察的核心是 Miranda 警告 的触发条件。根据 Miranda v. Arizona，警方只有在对嫌疑人进行“羁押讯问”时，才必须宣读 Miranda 权利。

公式：
羁押 (Custody) + 讯问 (Interrogation) = 需要 Miranda

如果缺少其中任何一个要素，警方未宣读 Miranda 权利并不影响供词的可采性 (Admissibility)。

深度解析：为什么选 B？

虽然警官的问题（“这些大麻是你的吗？”）明显构成了讯问 (Interrogation)，因为这旨在引出有罪供述，但关键在于羁押 (Custody) 这一要素缺失。

法律依据 (Berkemer v. McCarty, 1984)：

  • 最高法院裁定，普通的交通截停 (Traffic Stop) 通常不构成 Miranda 意义上的“羁押”。
  • 虽然驾驶员的行动自由受到限制（不能直接开走），但这种拘留通常是短暂的 (Temporary) 和公开的 (Public)。
  • 因此，这种环境不像警察局审讯室那样具有“强迫性气氛” (Coercive Atmosphere)。

在本案中，驾驶员虽然被叫下车，但并未被戴上手铐，也未被告知被捕。因此，他当时并未处于“羁押”状态，警官无需给予 Miranda 警告，供词有效。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 A (Consent to Search)：混淆概念
同意搜查涉及的是第四修正案（搜查与扣押），而本题讨论的是供词的可采性（第五修正案）。同意搜查并不意味着放弃了反对自证其罪的权利，两者是独立的法律问题。

❌ 选项 C (Ordered out of car)：法律误解
根据 Pennsylvania v. Mimms，出于警官安全考虑，在合法交通截停中命令驾驶员下车是允许的，这一行为本身并不将普通的交通截停转化为“羁押”。

❌ 选项 D (Intent to elicit)：只对了一半
这个选项正确地指出了警官的行为构成了“讯问”。但是，MBE 题目中常见的陷阱是：仅仅有讯问是不够的，必须同时满足“羁押”这一条件。因为没有羁押，所以即便有讯问意图，也不需要 Miranda。

💡 MBE 实战技巧

在处理涉及 Miranda 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 看环境：是在警察局审讯室，还是路边？（路边通常 = 非羁押）。
  2. 看束缚：嫌疑人是否被戴上手铐？是否被告知 "You are under arrest"？（如果没有，通常 = 非羁押）。
  3. 看顺序：是先问话后逮捕，还是先逮捕后问话？

记住：普通的交通违章截停（Terry Stop）不是 Custody。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Four hours into a defendant's assault trial, the lawyers gathered in the judge's chambers to discuss an evidentiary issue. While there, the judge received a phone call from his wife telling him that her mother had suddenly died. Without asking the lawyers what they wanted to do, the judge brought the lawyers back into the courtroom, declared a mistrial, excused the jury, and rushed home to his wife.
A new jury was impaneled the next day before a second judge.
The defendant has objected to the second trial on double jeopardy grounds.
Would the second trial violate the prohibition against double jeopardy?

choices.A: No, because the first judge acted in good faith in declaring a mistrial.
choices.B: No, because the first trial did not produce a verdict.
choices.C: Yes, because the second judge's evidentiary rulings might be inconsistent with those of the first judge.
choices.D: Yes, because there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial.

questions.explanation:
No double jeopardy protections
(retrial permitted for same offense)
No attachment
  • Jury was not impaneled & sworn or
  • Judge did not begin to hear evidence
Mistrial
  • Requested by defendant or
  • Based on manifest necessity
Appeal
  • Appellate court discovered trial error & remanded case
New facts
  • Facts necessary for greater offense did not exist at first trial
Guilty plea to lesser offense
  • Greater offense was charged at time of plea to lesser offense

The Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause bars multiple punishments and a second prosecution for the same offense following a conviction or an acquittal (ie, a final judgment). Since a mistrial terminates a trial prior to a final judgment, double jeopardy permits a retrial when (1) the defendant requested the mistrial or (2) the mistrial was based on a manifest necessity—ie:

• an unforeseeable event made it highly necessary to terminate the proceedings (eg, the death of a juror) and

• the judge exercised sound and rational discretion before declaring the mistrial (eg, allowing both sides the opportunity to speak, considering the available alternatives).

Here, the judge learned that his mother-in-law had suddenly died (unforeseeable event) and declared a mistrial. But the judge did so without considering other alternatives like postponing the trial or substituting another judge (no exercise of sound and rational discretion). As a result, there was no manifest necessity for the mistrial, and a second trial would violate the double jeopardy clause.

(Choice A) The judge acted in good faith since he declared the mistrial to tend to personal issues—not to prejudice the defendant. But since there was no manifest necessity for the mistrial, the defendant cannot be retried.

(Choice B) Although the first trial did not produce a verdict (since the judge declared a mistrial), double jeopardy prohibits a second prosecution because the mistrial was not based on a manifest necessity. If it had been, the second trial would have been permissible.

(Choice C) While the second judge's evidentiary rulings might be inconsistent with those of the first judge, the double jeopardy clause is violated due to the lack of a manifest necessity for the mistrial. Had the mistrial been based on a manifest necessity, a second trial before a different judge would not have violated the double jeopardy clause despite the risk of inconsistent evidentiary rulings.

📌 Educational Objective

Double jeopardy does not bar a second prosecution following a mistrial if the defendant requested the mistrial or it was based on a manifest necessity—(1) when an unforeseeable event made it highly necessary to end the proceedings and (2) the judge exercised sound and rational discretion before doing so.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • United States v. Perez, 22 U.S. 579, 580 (1824) (holding that a retrial is permitted when it is based on a manifest necessity).
  • United States v. Jorn, 400 U.S. 470, 486–87 (1971); Arizona v. Washington, 434 U.S. 497, 514–17 (1978) (explaining that a judge must exercise sound and rational discretion when determining whether manifest necessity exists).
  • Love v. Morton, 944 F.Supp. 379, 390–91 (D.N.J. 1996) (finding that there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial when the judge's mother-in-law died because he failed to exercise sound and rational discretion).
questions.zh-question:
在一名被告人的攻击罪审判进行四小时后，律师们聚集在法官办公室内讨论一个证据问题。在此期间，法官接到妻子的电话，得知他岳母突然去世。法官没有询问律师们的意见，就将他们带回法庭，宣布审判无效，解散了陪审团，然后赶回家中陪伴妻子。

第二天，在第二位法官面前组成了新的陪审团。

被告人以一事不再理为由反对第二次审判。

第二次审判是否违反禁止一事不再理的原则？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为第一位法官在宣布审判无效时是出于善意。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为第一次审判没有作出裁决。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为第二位法官的证据裁定可能与第一位法官的不一致。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为宣布审判无效不具备明显必要性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law / Double Jeopardy
正确答案
选项 D
⚖️ 核心考点：明显必要性 (Manifest Necessity)

根据美国宪法第五修正案的一事不再理条款 (Double Jeopardy Clause)，如果法官在没有被告同意的情况下宣布无效审判 (Mistrial)，除非存在“明显必要性”，否则禁止重审。

逻辑推演路径
1
风险何时附着 (Attachment of Jeopardy)？
在陪审团审判中，陪审团宣誓就职时，风险即已附着。本案中审判已进行4小时，因此一事不再理保护已生效。
2
法官的行为是否恰当？
法官因家庭紧急情况（岳母去世）宣布无效审判。虽然理由正当，但最高法院要求法官在宣布无效审判前必须行使“健全的自由裁量权” (Sound Discretion)。
3
为何没有“明显必要性”？
法官没有咨询律师，也没有考虑替代方案（如休庭延期、更换法官等）。这种仓促的决定 (acted precipitously) 意味着不存在法律意义上的“明显必要性”。
参考判例：United States v. Jorn; Love v. Morton
4
结论
由于缺乏明显必要性，且被告未同意无效审判，第二次审判违反了一事不再理原则。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (Good Faith) 错误：
法官的主观善意 (Good Faith) 不能弥补程序上的错误。即使法官不是为了伤害被告，但他未能考虑替代方案，依然导致重审被禁止。
选项 B (No Verdict) 错误：
这是无效审判的定义，而不是允许重审的理由。只有在被告请求无效审判或存在明显必要性时，未获裁决的案件才能重审。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

在涉及 Mistrial 的题目中，如果法官是因为突发状况（生病、缺席等）直接宣布无效审判，一定要检查法官是否“尝试过其他补救措施”。如果法官“立即”或“未咨询双方”就解散陪审团，通常意味着缺乏 Manifest Necessity，从而禁止重审。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A department store had experienced a growing incidence of shoplifting. At the store's request, the police concealed a detective at a vantage point above the women's apparel fitting rooms where she could see into these rooms, where customers tried on clothes. The detective saw a teenager enter a fitting room, shut the door, stuff a dress into her purse, leave the fitting room, and start for the street door. By prearranged signal, the detective notified another police officer near the door, who detained the teenager as she started to go out into the street. The teenager was placed under arrest, and the dress was retrieved from her purse.
The teenager is charged with shoplifting. At trial, she moves to suppress the introduction of the dress into evidence.
How will the court likely rule on her motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the detective could see into the room and thus the teenager's activities were legitimately in plain view.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the search and seizure were made incident to a valid arrest based on probable cause.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy while using a department store fitting room.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the police should have secured a search warrant to search her purse.

questions.explanation:
4th Amendment illegal search timeline
Teenager
enters fitting
room
Detective watches
teenager steal
dress in fitting room
Detective
notifies police
officer
Officer searches
teenager's
purse
Stolen dress
found in the
purse
Reasonable
expectation of
privacy
Unreasonable
(warrantless) search
Fruit of illegal search
= fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine applies

The Fourth Amendment protects persons from unreasonable government searches and seizures. A Fourth Amendment search occurs when one of the following tests is met:

  • Physical trespass test – the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area—a person's body, home, papers, or effects—to obtain information.
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invaded (1) a person's subjective expectation of privacy (2) that society would find objectively reasonable.

A Fourth Amendment search is presumptively unreasonable if it is conducted without a warrant. And under the fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine, any evidence that stems from an unreasonable search should be suppressed at trial.

Here, the physical trespass test is not met since a department store fitting room is not a constitutionally protected area. However, the reasonable expectation of privacy test is met since society would find the teenager's subjective expectation of privacy in the fitting room objectively reasonable. And since the detective did not have a warrant to search the fitting room, the search was unreasonable and violated the Fourth Amendment.

Due to the unreasonable search, the detective was able to see the teenager stuff a dress into her purse. The detective then notified another police officer, who arrested the teenager and retrieved the stolen dress. And since the seizure of the dress (fruit) stemmed from the unreasonable search (poisonous tree), the court should grant the teenager's motion to suppress the introduction of the dress into evidence.

(Choice A) Under the plain view doctrine, police may seize an item without a warrant if (1) it is in plain view, (2) they immediately recognize it as contraband, and (3) they are lawfully in the area—eg, they have a warrant to search the premises for another item. Here, the detective could plainly see into the fitting room and immediately recognized the dress as evidence of the crime. But since she was there unlawfully (eg, without a warrant), this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice B) After making a valid arrest based on untainted probable cause, police may (1) conduct a warrantless search of a person's body and the area within his/her immediate control and (2) seize any evidence discovered in that search. But here, the teenager's arrest was based on tainted probable cause (the warrantless search of the fitting room), so the search of her purse and seizure of the dress were incident to an invalid arrest.

(Choice C) The police should have secured a search warrant based on untainted probable cause to search the teenager's purse. However, the police could not do so since they only had tainted probable cause supplied by the detective's unreasonable search of the dressing room. Therefore, the court will likely grant the motion to suppress because the detective violated the teenager's reasonable expectation of privacy.

(Choice D) The police should have secured a search warrant based on untainted probable cause to search the teenager's purse. However, the police could not do so since they only had tainted probable cause supplied by the detective's unreasonable search of the dressing room. Therefore, the court will likely grant the motion to suppress because the detective violated the teenager's reasonable expectation of privacy.

📌 Educational Objective

A Fourth Amendment search occurs when the government (1) physically intrudes upon a constitutionally protected area or (2) invades a person's subjective and objectively reasonable expectation of privacy. A warrantless Fourth Amendment search is presumptively unreasonable, and any evidence that stems from the search should be suppressed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347, 361 (1967) (establishing the reasonable expectation of privacy test).
  • United States v. Jones, 565 U.S. 400, 407 (2012) (explaining the physical trespass test).
questions.zh-question:
一家百货公司遭遇了日益增多的商店盗窃事件。应商店要求，警方将一名侦探隐藏在女装试衣间上方的一个有利位置，从那里她可以窥视顾客试穿衣服的这些房间。该侦探看到一名青少年进入试衣间，关上门，将一件连衣裙塞进她的手提包，离开试衣间，然后走向临街的大门。通过预先安排的信号，该侦探通知了门口附近的另一名警官，当该青少年正要走到街上时，这名警官将其拘留。该青少年被逮捕，连衣裙也从她的手提包中被搜出。

该青少年被控商店盗窃。在审判中，她提出动议，要求排除将该连衣裙作为证据采纳。

法院很可能会如何裁定她的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为侦探可以看到房间内的情况，因此该青少年的活动合法地处于一目了然（plain view）的状态。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为搜查和扣押是基于合理根据（probable cause）的有效逮捕的附带行为。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为个人在使用百货公司试衣间时拥有合理的隐私期待。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为警方本应获得搜查令才能搜查她的手提包。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Search & Seizure
核心考点：Katz 测试

本题的核心在于判断警方的行为是否构成了美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）下的“搜查”（Search）。

根据 Katz v. United States (1967) 确立的标准，如果满足以下两点，即构成搜查：
  1. 个人表现出了主观的隐私期待 (Subjective expectation of privacy)；
  2. 这种期待被社会认为是客观合理的 (Objectively reasonable)。

如果构成了“搜查”，警方通常需要搜查令 (Warrant)，否则该搜查被推定为不合理。

本案分析
1. 试衣间的性质
试衣间 (Fitting room) 是顾客更换衣物的私密空间。顾客关上门，主观上显然有隐私期待。社会普遍认为在试衣间内不应被偷窥，因此这种期待是客观合理的。
2. 警方的行为
警方在没有搜查令的情况下，通过隐藏位置窥视试衣间内部。这侵犯了被告的合理隐私期待 (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy, REP)。
3. 结论
警方的窥视行为构成了非法的无证搜查 (Illegal warrantless search)。
证据排除规则

由于最初的观察是非法的，根据“毒树之果”原则 (Fruit of the Poisonous Tree Doctrine)，由此衍生的所有证据都必须被排除。

毒树 (Poisonous Tree)
非法窥视试衣间
⬇️
果实 (Fruit)
看到偷窃行为 ➔ 逮捕 ➔ 搜查手提包 ➔ 发现连衣裙

因此，法院应批准排除连衣裙作为证据的动议。

✅ 正确答案：选项 C

"Grant the motion, because an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy while using a department store fitting room."

这是最直接的法律依据。因为存在合理的隐私期待，警方的窥视才构成搜查；因为没有搜查令，搜查才非法；因为搜查非法，证据才被排除。

❌ 易错项辨析：选项 A

Plain View (一目了然法则) 为什么不适用？

Plain View Doctrine 适用的前提是警方必须合法地处于 (lawfully present) 能够观察到证据的位置。

在本案中，侦探是通过侵犯隐私（非法搜查）才获得了观察位置，因此不能援引 Plain View 原则来洗白其发现的证据。

❌ 易错项辨析：选项 B

Search Incident to Arrest (逮捕附带搜查) 为什么不适用？

SIA 必须基于合法的逮捕 (Valid Arrest)。本案中，逮捕的理由（Probable Cause）完全来自于非法的偷窥。由于“毒树之果”效应，逮捕本身也是非法的，因此附带的搜查也是非法的。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到 Fourth Amendment 题目，首先问自己：
"Did the police intrude on a reasonable expectation of privacy?"
如果是，且没有 Warrant 或 Exception，那就是违宪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A necktie salesman was charged with the murder of a woman who had been strangled and whose body was found in the woods near his home. The salesman suffers from a neurological problem that makes it impossible for him to remember an occurrence for longer than 48 hours.
After the salesman was charged, the police visited him and asked if they might search his home. The salesman consented. During their search, the police found a diary written by the salesman. An entry dated the same day as the woman's disappearance read, "Indescribable excitement. Why did no one ever tell me that killing gave such pleasure to the master?"
The salesman was charged with murder. His attorney has moved to exclude the diary from evidence on the ground that its admission would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination. His counsel has also argued that the salesman could not give informed consent to the search because more than 48 hours had passed since the making of the entry and hence he could not remember the existence of the incriminating entry at the time he gave his consent. There is no evidence that the police officers who secured the salesman's consent to the search were aware of his memory impairment.
Should the court admit the diary into evidence?

choices.A: No, because the salesman was not competent to consent to a search.
choices.B: No, because use of the diary as evidence would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination.
choices.C: Yes, because the salesman's consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct and the salesman was not compelled to make the diary entry.
choices.D: Yes, pursuant to the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule.

questions.explanation:
The salesman argues that the warrantless search of his home violated the Fourth Amendment because he could not give informed consent to the search. However, consent need only be given freely and voluntarily (ie, without police coercion)—informed consent is not required. Therefore, police do not need to inform a suspect of his/her right to refuse consent or the incriminating evidence they hope to obtain.

Here, due to his neurological condition, the salesman could not remember the incriminating diary entry when he consented to the police search. But since his consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct or other coercive measures, it was given voluntarily. Therefore, the police had valid consent to search the salesman's home, and the diary discovered during the search should not be excluded on Fourth Amendment grounds.

The salesman also argues that admitting the diary would violate his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. This privilege protects persons from being compelled to produce or create self-incriminating evidence—ie, evidence that could be used (or lead to other evidence that might be used) against him/her in a criminal prosecution. But this protection does not apply to documents obtained during a constitutional search since the government did not compel the person to produce or create them.

Here, the diary entry is incriminating because it implicates the salesman in the woman's murder. But admitting this evidence would not violate his privilege against self-incrimination since (1) it was discovered during a lawful search of his home (no compelled production) and (2) the salesman was not compelled to create the diary entry (Choice B). Therefore, the court should deny the salesman's motion and admit the diary into evidence.

(Choice A) Incompetency (eg, neurological or mental illness) alone does not invalidate a person's consent. Instead, it is one factor used to determine if consent was voluntary. But the salesman's competency is not an issue here since there is no evidence that the police knew about his neurological condition (or took advantage of it to coerce his consent).

(Choice D) The good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule allows the admission of illegally seized evidence if police reasonably believed that they were acting lawfully (eg, relying on a warrant later deemed invalid). But this exception does not apply here since the officers legally searched the salesman's home and seized the diary.

📌 Educational Objective

Police may conduct a warrantless search if the person consented to the search voluntarily—ie, without police coercion—even if the consent was not informed. Additionally, the privilege against self-incrimination only applies to the compelled production or creation of evidence—not evidence discovered during a constitutional search.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Schneckloth v. Bustamonte, 412 U.S. 218, 225–28 (1973) (explaining that consent must be voluntary and not the result of police coercion).
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 35–36 (2000) (explaining that contents of documents that a defendant was not compelled to create are not privileged).
questions.zh-question:
一名领带销售员被指控谋杀一名妇女，该妇女被勒死，其尸体在他家附近的树林中被发现。该销售员患有神经系统问题，导致他无法记住任何超过48小时的事件。

在该销售员被指控后，警方拜访了他，并询问是否可以搜查他的家。该销售员表示同意。在搜查过程中，警方发现了一本该销售员写的日记。一篇与该女子失踪同日期的条目写道：“难以形容的兴奋。为什么从来没有人告诉我，杀戮能给主人带来如此大的快感？”

该销售员被控犯有谋杀罪。他的律师已动议将日记排除在证据之外，理由是采纳日记将侵犯销售员反对自证其罪的特权。其律师还辩称，该销售员无法对搜查作出知情同意，因为距离写下该日记条目已超过48小时，因此他在同意搜查时已不记得存在这条可致其入罪的记录。没有证据表明，获得销售员搜查同意的警官知道他的记忆障碍。

法院是否应该将该日记采纳为证据？

zh-choices.A: 不应采纳，因为该销售员不具备同意搜查的法律能力。
zh-choices.B: 不应采纳，因为使用该日记作为证据将侵犯销售员反对自证其罪的特权。
zh-choices.C: 应该采纳，因为销售员的同意并非通过警方的故意不当行为获得，且销售员并未被强迫写下日记条目。
zh-choices.D: 应该采纳，依据证据排除规则的善意例外原则。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law / Criminal Procedure
Topic: Search & Seizure / Self-Incrimination
正确答案：选项 C Yes, because the salesman's consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct...

核心考点深度解析

1. 第四修正案：同意搜查 (Consent Search)

本题的关键在于判断被告的“同意”是否有效。根据 Fourth Amendment，警方在获得有效同意的情况下可以进行无证搜查。

法律标准：同意必须是自愿的 (Voluntary)，即没有警方的胁迫 (Coercion)。

误区警示：法律不要求“知情同意” (Informed Consent)。

  • 警方不需要告知嫌疑人他有权拒绝。
  • 嫌疑人不需要确切记得家里有什么罪证。

本案分析：虽然被告有记忆障碍，但警方并不知道这一点，也没有利用这一点进行胁迫。在“总体情况” (Totality of the Circumstances) 下，他的同意是自愿的。

2. 第五修正案：反对自证其罪 (Self-Incrimination)

被告律师辩称日记违反了 Fifth Amendment。这个论点是错误的。

✍️
自愿书写
(非强迫制作)
+
👮‍♂️
合法搜查
(非强迫提交)
=
✅
可采纳

原理：第五修正案保护的是“被强迫的” (Compelled) 证言。

  • 被告写日记时是自愿的（没有警察拿枪指着他写）。
  • 警方获取日记是通过合法的搜查（Consent Search），而不是通过传票强迫被告“交出”日记。

因此，日记作为证据不违反第五修正案。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (Competence)

错误理由： 精神或神经问题本身不会自动导致同意无效。只有当警方利用这种精神状态进行胁迫，或者该状态导致当事人完全无法理解其行为性质时才无效。本案中警方不知情，且无胁迫行为。

选项 B (Privilege)

错误理由： 如上所述，第五修正案不保护在合法搜查中被扣押的、自愿撰写的私人文件。

选项 D (Good Faith)

错误理由： Good-faith exception 通常适用于警方依赖了一份后来被判定无效的搜查令 (Warrant) 的情况。本案是无证搜查 (Warrantless Search)，依据的是同意，因此该例外原则不适用（也不需要适用，因为搜查本身就是合法的）。

🎓 MBE 考试通关秘籍

1. 区分 "Voluntary" vs. "Informed"：
在 Fourth Amendment 同意搜查中，只要没有胁迫 (Coercion) 就是有效的。不要被“嫌疑人不知道后果”或“嫌疑人记性不好”所迷惑。

2. 私人文件的获取方式：
如果是警方搜出来的（Search），通常不涉及第五修正案问题；如果是强迫被告交出来的（Subpoena），才可能涉及第五修正案的“强迫性行为”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
After a liquor store was robbed, the police received an anonymous telephone call naming a store employee as the perpetrator of the robbery. Honestly believing that their actions were permitted by the U.S. Constitution, the police talked one of the employee's neighbors into going to the employee's home with a hidden recording device to engage him in a conversation about the crime. The neighbor went to the employee's home and was invited inside. During the conversation in the employee's home, the employee admitted having committed the robbery.
The employee was charged with the robbery in state court. He has moved to suppress the recording on the grounds that the method of obtaining it violated both his federal and his state constitutional rights.
Assume that a clear precedent from the state's highest court would result in a finding that the conduct of the police in making the recording violated the employee's rights under the state constitution, and that excluding the recording is the proper remedy.
Should the court grant the employee's motion?

choices.A: No, because the employee's federal constitutional rights were not violated, and this circumstance overrides any state constitutional provisions.
choices.B: No, because the police were acting in the good-faith belief that the federal Constitution permitted their actions.
choices.C: Yes, because the making of the recording violated the employee's federal constitutional rights.
choices.D: Yes, because the making of the recording violated the state constitution.

questions.explanation:
Constitutional protections
Broader state protections = Ceiling
U.S. Constitution = Floor
(minimum protections)
Narrower state protections prohibited

Although the federal Constitution sets a "floor" for personal liberties, state constitutions may offer protections that exceed the minimum federal constitutional requirements. And when a state's highest court sets clear precedent regarding a state constitutional right, lower state courts (trial and intermediate courts) must follow that precedent when resolving a similar legal issue.

Here, the employee moved to suppress (ie, exclude) the recording from evidence on the grounds that it was obtained in violation of his state and federal constitutional rights. The state's highest court has set a clear precedent establishing that the recording violated the employee's state constitutional rights and should be excluded from evidence. Therefore, the state court must follow this precedent and suppress the recording on this ground.

(Choices A & C) A defendant's Fourth Amendment rights are not violated when a government informant speaks with the defendant and secretly records their conversation (as seen here). However, compliance with the federal Constitution does not excuse a violation of a defendant's broader state constitutional protections. Therefore, the motion to suppress the recording should be granted on state constitutional grounds.

(Choice B) Under the good-faith exception, evidence obtained in violation of a defendant's federal constitutional rights is admissible if the police reasonably believed that they were acting lawfully (eg, that their actions were permitted by a prior court ruling). But here, the police's good-faith belief that the federal Constitution permitted the recording is irrelevant since this state's clear precedent holds that their actions violated the state constitution.

📌 Educational Objective

State constitutions may offer greater protections than the federal Constitution—eg, a state exclusionary rule can suppress more evidence than the federal exclusionary rule. And lower state courts must comply with precedents from the state's highest court that interpreted those protections.

📚 References
  • Ker v. California, 374 U.S. 23, 34 (1963) (explaining that states can grant broader rights than the U.S. Constitution).
questions.zh-question:
一家酒类商店被抢劫后，警方接到一个匿名电话，指认一名商店员工为抢劫案的作案人。警方真诚地相信他们的行为符合美国宪法的规定，于是说服该员工的一位邻居带着一个隐藏录音设备前往该员工家中，与他谈论这起犯罪。邻居去了员工家并被邀请入内。在员工家中的谈话期间，该员工承认实施了抢劫。
该员工在州法院被控抢劫。他已提出动议，要求排除该录音，理由是获取该录音的方式侵犯了他的联邦和州宪法权利。
假设州最高法院的一项明确判例将导致认定警方制作录音的行为侵犯了该员工根据州宪法享有的权利，并且排除该录音是适当的补救措施。
法院是否应该批准该员工的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为该员工的联邦宪法权利并未受到侵犯，并且此情况凌驾于任何州宪法规定之上。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为警方是善意地相信联邦宪法允许他们的行为。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为制作该录音侵犯了该员工的联邦宪法权利。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为制作该录音侵犯了州宪法。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：宪法保护层级

D

正确选项

核心法律原则

Federalism (联邦主义) Supremacy Clause (至高条款)

本题考察的是美国宪法与州宪法之间的关系，即“底线与天花板”理论。

  • 联邦宪法 (U.S. Constitution)：设定了个人权利保护的最低标准 (Floor)。任何州不得提供低于此标准的保护。
  • 州宪法 (State Constitution)：可以提供比联邦宪法更高、更广泛 (Broader) 的保护。

案情深度解析

1. 联邦宪法层面：
根据美国最高法院的判例（如 United States v. White），警方使用线人（"False Friend"）携带窃听器进入嫌疑人家中录音，并不违反第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment)。因为嫌疑人是自愿向第三方透露信息，他承担了该第三方可能是警方线人的风险。

2. 州宪法层面：
题目明确指出：该州最高法院有明确判例 (Clear Precedent)，认定这种行为违反了州宪法。

3. 结论：
虽然警方的行为符合联邦宪法，但违反了提供“更高保护”的州宪法。在州法院审理州法指控的案件中，必须遵循州最高法院对州宪法的解释。因此，证据必须被排除。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A 错误：
虽然联邦法律是最高法律（Supremacy Clause），但这仅适用于州法试图剥夺联邦权利的情况。州法给予被告更多权利并不与联邦法律冲突，因此联邦宪法不会“覆盖” (Override) 州宪法提供的额外保护。

选项 B 错误：
善意例外 (Good-faith exception) 通常适用于联邦第四修正案的排除规则。但在本案中，排除证据的依据是州宪法。如果州最高法院决定不承认善意例外，或者认定州宪法的违规不能通过善意来补救，那么警方的善意信念就无关紧要。

选项 C 错误：
这是一个事实错误。如前所述，根据现行联邦判例，秘密录制与线人的对话并不违反联邦宪法权利。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

当题目中出现“州最高法院判例” (State Supreme Court Precedent) 且涉及个人权利时，请记住：

  1. 州可以给被告更多权利，不能给更少。
  2. 如果州宪法说“这是违法的”，即使联邦最高法院说“这是合法的”，在州法院系统中，州法说了算。
  3. 这就是所谓的 Independent and Adequate State Grounds（独立且充分的州法依据）。
MBE Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Law Review

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was validly arrested for the murder of a store clerk and was taken to a police station where he was given Miranda warnings. When an interrogator asked the defendant, "Do you understand your Miranda rights, and are you willing to give up those rights and talk to us?" the defendant replied, "Yes." When asked, "Did you kill the clerk?" the defendant replied, "No." When asked, "Where were you on the day the clerk was killed?" the defendant replied, "Maybe I should talk to a lawyer." The interrogator asked, "Are you sure?" and the defendant replied, "I'm not sure." The interrogator then asked, "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" and the defendant replied, "Because I killed the clerk. It was an accident, and I think I need a lawyer to defend me." At that point all interrogation ceased. Later, the defendant was formally charged with murdering the clerk.
The defendant has moved to suppress evidence of his statement "I killed the clerk" on the ground that this statement was elicited in violation of his Miranda rights. Should the defendant's motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because although the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" did not constitute custodial interrogation.
choices.B: No, because the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, and his conduct prior to making the statement constituted a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
choices.C: Yes, because although the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, his conduct prior to making the statement did not constitute a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, and the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" constituted custodial interrogation.

questions.explanation:
Right to counsel
Applicability Request Waiver
Fifth
Amendment		 Suspect has right to counsel when:
  • in custody and
  • subjected to interrogation
 Unambiguous
request
required		 Valid if made:
  • knowingly
  • intelligently
  • voluntarily
Sixth
Amendment		 Defendant has right to counsel when:
  • judicial proceedings commence and
  • critical stage of prosecution
 No request
required
(attaches
automatically)

Police must inform suspects of their Fifth Amendment Miranda right to counsel before a custodial interrogation. Police are free to question a suspect if he/she waives this right, but must stop questioning once the suspect makes an unambiguous request for counsel (eg, "I want a lawyer"). If police fail to honor that request and continue to question the suspect without the presence of counsel, the court should suppress the suspect's responses.

Here, the defendant validly waived his Miranda right to counsel before the custodial interrogation. And though the defendant later told the police interrogator "Maybe I should talk to a lawyer" and reiterated that he was "not sure," his statements were too ambiguous to effectively request counsel. Therefore, the interrogator was free to continue questioning the defendant without counsel present and the court should deny the defendant's motion to suppress his statement that he killed the clerk.

(Choices A & D) Since the defendant was validly arrested (custody) and the police interrogator's questioning was reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response (interrogation), the question "Why would you want to talk to a lawyer?" does constitute custodial interrogation. But since the defendant validly waived his Miranda rights and did not effectively assert his right to counsel, his answer is admissible at trial.

(Choice C) After being Mirandized, the defendant clearly stated that he understood his rights and that he was willing to give up those rights and talk to the interrogator. Therefore, the defendant unequivocally and validly waived his Miranda rights.

📌 Educational Objective

Police are free to question a suspect who waives his/her Fifth Amendment (Miranda) right to counsel. However, if the suspect later makes an unambiguous request for counsel, police must stop questioning until the suspect's lawyer is present. If the police continue questioning, the suspect's responses should be suppressed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V.
  • Davis v. United States, 512 U.S. 452 (1994) (ineffective assertion of right to counsel).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因谋杀一名商店店员而被合法逮捕，并被带到警察局，在那里他被告知了 Miranda 警告。当审讯人员问被告：“你是否理解你的 Miranda 权利，并愿意放弃这些权利与我们交谈？”被告回答：“是的。”当被问及：“你是否杀害了店员？”被告回答：“没有。”当被问及：“店员被杀害那天你在哪里？”被告回答：“也许我应该和律师谈谈。”审讯人员问道：“你确定吗？”被告回答：“我不确定。”审讯人员接着问：“你为什么想和律师谈？”被告回答：“因为我杀了那个店员。那是个意外，我认为我需要一个律师为我辩护。”此时，所有审讯都停止了。后来，被告被正式指控谋杀该店员。

被告已提出动议，以其“我杀了店员”的陈述是在违反其 Miranda 权利的情况下诱导得出的为由，要求排除该陈述证据。被告的动议应被批准吗？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为尽管被告有效地主张了获得律师帮助的权利，但“你为什么想和律师谈？”这个问题不构成羁押讯问。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为被告并未有效地主张获得律师帮助的权利，并且他在做出该陈述之前的行为构成了对其 Miranda 权利的有效放弃。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为尽管被告并未有效地主张获得律师帮助的权利，但他在做出该陈述之前的行为并不构成对其 Miranda 权利的有效放弃。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为被告有效地主张了获得律师帮助的权利，并且“你为什么想和律师谈？”这个问题构成了羁押讯问。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Miranda Rights

正确答案：B 法院不应批准排除证据的动议。因为被告没有有效地主张律师帮助权，且之前的行为构成了有效的权利放弃 (Waiver)。
核心考点：律师帮助权的援引标准

本题的核心在于：嫌疑人在接受讯问时，如何才能有效地援引（Invoke）其 Miranda 权利中的律师帮助权？

Davis v. United States (1994)
最高法院确立了“明确无误原则” (Unambiguous Request Rule)。

根据该原则，嫌疑人必须清晰、明确且毫不含糊地表达希望律师在场的意愿。如果陈述模棱两可 (Ambiguous) 或犹豫不决 (Equivocal)，警方没有义务停止讯问。

陈述类型 示例 (Example) 警方义务
明确请求
(Unambiguous)		 "I want a lawyer."
"I will not talk without a lawyer."		 必须立即停止讯问。
含糊陈述
(Ambiguous)		 "Maybe I should talk to a lawyer."
"I think I need a lawyer."		 可以继续讯问。
(警方可以澄清，但非必须)
案情具体分析

在本案中，被告经历了三个关键阶段：

  1. 有效放弃 (Valid Waiver)： 被告最初明确表示理解权利并愿意交谈。这构成了一个知情、自愿的放弃。
  2. 含糊的请求 (Ambiguous Request)： 当被告说 "Maybe I should talk to a lawyer"（也许我应该和律师谈谈）时，这是一个典型的模棱两可的陈述。根据 Davis 案，这不足以触发停止讯问的义务。
  3. 澄清与自白： 警察问 "Are you sure?" 和 "Why?" 属于澄清性问题（虽然法律甚至不强制要求警察进行澄清）。被告随后的回答构成了自白。

因此，由于被告从未有效地援引律师权，他最初的放弃 (Waiver) 仍然有效，自白可以作为证据。

为什么其他选项错误？
  • 选项 A & D (关于讯问的定义)： 警察问“你为什么想找律师？”确实可能引出有罪供述，因此在技术上属于“羁押讯问” (Custodial Interrogation)。但是，这不影响结果，因为被告没有有效地援引权利，所以警察本来就有权继续讯问。
  • 选项 C (关于放弃的有效性)： 题目明确指出被告在被告知权利后说“Yes”并愿意交谈。没有证据表明存在胁迫或神志不清，因此最初的放弃是绝对有效的。
💡MBE 考试技巧：
看到 "Maybe" (也许), "I think" (我想), "I might" (我可能) 搭配 "lawyer" 时，立刻联想 Davis v. United States。

记住结论：含糊的请求 = 无效的请求。警方不需要停止，也不需要澄清（虽然他们通常会澄清）。只要没有明确说 "Stop" 或 "I want a lawyer"，讯问就可以继续。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state legislature passed a statute providing that juries in criminal trials were to consist of 6 jurors, rather than 12, and that jury verdicts did not have to be unanimous but could be based on 5 votes out of 6 jurors.
A defendant was tried for murder. Over his objection, he was tried by a jury composed of 6 jurors. The jurors found him guilty by a vote of 5 to 1, and over the defendant's objection, the court entered a judgment of conviction, which was affirmed on appeal by the state's highest court.
The defendant seeks to overturn his conviction in a habeas corpus proceeding in federal court, claiming that the trial court violated his constitutional rights by allowing both a non-unanimous jury verdict and a jury composed of fewer than 12 members.
How is the federal court likely to rule in this action?

choices.A: It will set aside the conviction, because the 6-person jury verdict was not unanimous.
choices.B: It will set aside the conviction, because the jury was composed of fewer than 12 members.
choices.C: It will set aside the conviction, both because the jury was composed of fewer than 12 members and because the 6-person jury verdict was not unanimous.
choices.D: It will uphold the conviction.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to jury trial
Applies to serious
crimes
  • General rule – possible sentence of > 6 months' imprisonment (or actual sentence of > 6 months if no statutory maximum provided)
  • Exception – sentence ≤ 6 months if additional penalties are so severe that legislature likely intended for crime to be serious
Waiver
  • Free, knowing & intelligent request for bench trial
Composition
  • Jury pool – fair cross section of community
  • Impaneled jury – impartial & unbiased
Size
  • State court – at least 6 jury members
  • Federal court – 12 jury members unless parties stipulate otherwise
Unanimity
  • Unanimous verdict required to convict

A petition for a writ of habeas corpus is generally used as a post-conviction remedy to collaterally attack an unlawful imprisonment. If the petitioner is incarcerated for a state conviction, the petition can only be filed in federal court if the petitioner has exhausted all state appellate remedies. The federal court will only grant the petition and set aside the conviction if the petitioner's incarceration violates the U.S. Constitution.

The Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial attaches to any criminal proceeding where the defendant could be sentenced to more than six months in prison. This right, applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment, requires that a jury (1) have at least six members and (2) reach a unanimous verdict to convict a defendant. If these requirements are not met, any conviction and subsequent incarceration are unconstitutional.

Here, the defendant properly filed a petition for a writ of habeas corpus in federal court since the state's highest court had affirmed his conviction (exhaustion of state appellate remedies). Although the defendant was properly tried by a six-member jury (Choices B & C), the conviction was unconstitutional since it was based on a vote of 5 to 1—not a unanimous guilty verdict. Therefore, the federal court will likely set aside the conviction (Choice D).

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial entitles criminal defendants who could be sentenced to more than six months in prison to a jury composed of at least six members. The defendant can then be convicted only by a unanimous jury verdict.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to jury trial).
  • Baldwin v. New York, 399 U.S. 66, 69 (1970) (explaining that the Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial applies when a criminal defendant's prison sentence could exceed six months).
  • Williams v. Florida, 399 U.S. 78, 86 (1970) (affirming that criminal juries can be composed of six members).
  • Ramos v. Louisiana, 140 S. Ct. 1390, 1397 (2020) (holding that the Sixth Amendment right to a unanimous jury verdict applies to federal and state courts).
questions.zh-question:
一个州立法机关通过了一项法规，规定刑事审判中的陪审团应由6名陪审员组成，而非12名，并且陪审团的裁决无需全体一致，可以基于6名陪审员中的5票作出。

一名被告因谋杀罪受审。不顾其反对，他由一个6名陪审员组成的陪审团进行审判。陪审员以5比1的投票结果裁定他有罪，并且不顾被告的反对，法院作出了定罪判决，该判决经州最高法院上诉维持。

该被告在联邦法院通过人身保护令程序寻求推翻其定罪，声称审判法院允许非一致的陪审团裁决和少于12名成员的陪审团，侵犯了他的宪法权利。

联邦法院可能会如何裁决此案？

zh-choices.A: 法院将撤销定罪，因为6人陪审团的裁决并非全体一致。
zh-choices.B: 法院将撤销定罪，因为陪审团的成员少于12人。
zh-choices.C: 法院将撤销定罪，因为陪审团的成员少于12人，并且6人陪审团的裁决并非全体一致。
zh-choices.D: 法院将维持定罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法刑事程序 (Constitutional Criminal Procedure)

✅ 正确答案：A

联邦法院将撤销定罪，因为 6 人陪审团的裁决并非全体一致 (Not Unanimous)。

虽然 6 人陪审团本身是合宪的，但在 6 人陪审团的情况下，裁决必须是全体一致的；且根据最新判例，所有重罪陪审团裁决均需一致。

⚖️ 法律依据与推理

Sixth Amendment Jury Trial

1. 陪审团人数 (Jury Size)

规则：宪法并不要求州法院必须使用 12 人陪审团。最高法院在 Williams v. Florida (1970) 中裁定，州刑事审判中陪审团人数最少可为 6 人。

应用：本案中，州法律规定使用 6 人陪审团，这本身没有违反宪法。因此，选项 B 和 C 声称“少于 12 人违宪”是错误的。

2. 裁决一致性 (Unanimity)

旧规则 (本题背景)：在 Burch v. Louisiana (1979) 中，最高法院裁定：虽然 6 人陪审团是合宪的，但如果陪审团只有 6 人，其裁决必须是全体一致的。5:1 的裁决严重削弱了陪审团功能的实质，因此违宪。

新规则 (2020年更新)：在 Ramos v. Louisiana (2020) 中，最高法院进一步裁定，无论陪审团人数多少（6人或12人），宪法第六修正案都要求在重罪审判中必须达成全体一致 (Unanimous Verdict) 才能定罪。

结论：无论是基于本题出题时的判例 (Burch) 还是现行法律 (Ramos)，5比1的定罪裁决都是违宪的。

❌ 干扰项分析

  • 选项 B (人数问题)：错误。宪法允许 6 人陪审团。只有当人数少于 6 人（如 5 人）时才违宪 (Ballew v. Georgia)。
  • 选项 C (双重理由)：错误。前半部分理由（人数少于12人）不成立。
  • 选项 D (维持定罪)：错误。非一致裁决侵犯了被告的第六修正案权利，联邦法院在人身保护令 (Habeas Corpus) 程序中会纠正这一宪法性错误。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant, who was represented by a lawyer, was arraigned on a burglary charge and released from custody after posting bail. The defendant's lawyer warned him not to speak to anyone about the case without the lawyer present.
The following day, a police officer approached the defendant outside his apartment building. The officer believed that others, who had not yet been arrested or charged, were also involved in the burglary. The officer asked the defendant if he was willing to discuss the burglary, told him that he was free to decline the request, and read him his Miranda warnings. The defendant thought he could convince the officer that his accomplices were solely responsible for the crime, so he agreed to speak with the officer. During the officer's questioning, the defendant made a statement that implicated him in the burglary.
At trial, the prosecution intends to introduce the defendant's incriminating statement into evidence. The defendant has filed a motion to suppress the statement, contending that it was obtained in violation of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel.
What is the prosecution's best argument that the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel was NOT violated?

choices.A: The defendant understood the nature of his offense and was aware of his right to counsel when he voluntarily spoke to the police officer.
choices.B: The defendant was not in custody when he provided the incriminating statement.
choices.C: The police officer's questioning occurred during a noncritical stage in the proceedings that did not require the presence of counsel.
choices.D: The police officer's questioning was not reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response.

questions.explanation:
Waiver of Sixth Amendment right to counsel
Knowing
  • • Aware of right to counsel
Intelligent
  • • Understands nature of charges
  • • Knows range of punishment
  • • Recognizes disadvantages of self-representation
Voluntary
  • • Waiver is given freely
  • • Not choosing self-representation over incompetent counsel

A court should suppress any statement taken in violation of a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel. This right automatically attaches when judicial proceedings commence (e.g., when the defendant is arraigned. It guarantees a defendant access to an attorney at every critical stage of prosecution, including post-indictment interrogations (custodial or otherwise). However, a defendant may waive the Sixth Amendment right to counsel so long as relinquishment of the right is voluntary, knowing, and intelligent.

Here, the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attached when he was arraigned. This right applied when the officer approached the defendant outside his apartment building to question him about the burglary. This is because a post-indictment interrogation is a critical stage of prosecution—regardless of whether the defendant is in custody (Choices B and C). And questioning the defendant about others' involvement in the burglary is a critical stage because it was reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response (Choice D).

Therefore, the prosecution's best argument that the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel was not violated is that he understood the nature of his offense and was aware of his right to counsel when he voluntarily spoke to the officer. In other words, the defendant validly waived his right to counsel, so his statement is admissible.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel can be waived so long as relinquishment of this right is voluntary, knowing, and intelligent.

📚 References
  • Paterson v. Illinois, 487 U.S. 285 (1988) (holding that Miranda warnings given during post-indictment questioning was sufficient to make defendant aware of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel).
  • Brewer v. Williams, 430 U.S. 387 (1977) (stating that the prosecution must prove an intentional relinquishment or abandonment of one's Sixth Amendment right to counsel to constitute waiver).
questions.zh-question:
一名由律师代理的被告，因入室盗窃罪被传讯，并在缴纳保释金后获释。被告的律师警告他，在律师不在场的情况下，不要与任何人谈论此案。
次日，一名警官在被告的公寓楼外接近了他。警官认为，其他尚未被逮捕或起诉的人也参与了此次入室盗窃。警官询问被告是否愿意讨论入室盗窃案，告知他可以拒绝该请求，并向他宣读了 Miranda 警告。被告认为他可以说服警官，他的同伙应对此罪行负全责，因此他同意与警官交谈。在警官的讯问过程中，被告做出了牵连他本人参与入室盗窃的陈述。
在审判中，控方打算将被告的自证其罪的陈述作为证据提交。被告已提交动议排除该陈述，声称其是在违反其 Sixth Amendment 律师权的情况下获得的。
控方最好的论点是什么，以证明被告的 Sixth Amendment 律师权没有被侵犯？

zh-choices.A: 被告在自愿与警官交谈时，理解其罪行的性质并知晓其律师权。
zh-choices.B: 被告在提供自证其罪的陈述时并未被羁押。
zh-choices.C: 警官的讯问发生在诉讼的非关键阶段，该阶段不需要律师在场。
zh-choices.D: 警官的讯问并非合理地可能引出有罪供述。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A man entered the police station and announced that he wanted to confess to a murder. The police advised the man of the Miranda warnings, and the man signed a written waiver. The man then described the murder in detail and pinpointed the location where a murder victim had been found a few weeks before.
Later, a court-appointed psychiatrist determined that the man was suffering from a serious mental illness that induced his confession. The psychiatrist also stated that the mental illness did not interfere with the man's ability to understand his rights.
Is the man's confession admissible at trial?

choices.A: No, because the man's confession was a product of his mental illness and was therefore involuntary.
choices.B: No, because under these circumstances, there was no valid waiver of Miranda warnings.
choices.C: Yes, because the man was not in custody.
choices.D: Yes, because there was no coercive police conduct in obtaining the man's statement.

questions.explanation:
Constitutional protections for involuntary confessions
5th Amendment
(self-incrimination) 		Miranda warnings required when suspect is both:
• in custody and
• subjected to police interrogation
6th Amendment
(attorney) 		Suspect has right to assistance of counsel:
• once judicial proceedings commence and
• during all critical stages of prosecution thereafter
14th Amendment
(due process) 		Confession must be voluntary:
• product of free & deliberate choice rather than police coercion

The due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment precludes the use of involuntary confessions at trial. A confession is involuntary if the totality of the circumstances shows that it was a product of police coercion—ie, when police use physical force, threats, or psychological pressure to force a suspect to confess. But a confession is admissible if it was induced by a suspect's mental illness—not by police coercion.

Here, the man entered the police station and stated that he committed a murder. After being informed of his Miranda rights, he signed a written waiver and explained the details of the murder. And though the man's mental illness induced his confession, at no point did the police coerce him into confessing. Therefore, the man's confession was voluntary and is admissible at trial (Choice A).

(Choice B) A defendant's waiver of his/her Miranda rights is valid if it was given knowingly, intelligently, and voluntarily (ie, free from police coercion). Here, the man's waiver is likely valid because he understood his Miranda rights despite his mental illness, and his waiver was not coerced.

(Choice C) A person is in custody when he/she is formally arrested or his/her freedom of movement is restrained to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave. Here, the man was in custody since a reasonable person would not feel free to leave a police station after announcing that he/she had committed murder.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant's confession is involuntary if the totality of the circumstances shows that the confession was the product of coercive police conduct. Therefore, a confession induced by the defendant's mental condition—not police coercion—is still admissible.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (due process clause).
  • Colorado v. Connelly, 479 U.S. 157, 167 (1986) (holding that mental illness alone is insufficient to show that a confession was involuntary).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子走进警察局，声称他想坦白一起谋杀案。警察向该男子告知了 Miranda 警告，该男子签署了一份书面弃权声明。该男子随后详细描述了谋杀过程，并指出了几周前发现一名谋杀案受害者的地点。

后来，一名法院指定的精神病医生确定该男子患有严重的精神疾病，该疾病诱使其做出供述。该精神病医生还指出，该精神疾病并未影响该男子理解其权利的能力。

该男子的供述在审判中是否可以采纳？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该男子的供述是其精神疾病的产物，因此是非自愿的。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为在这种情况下，对 Miranda 警告的弃权无效。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为该男子未被羁押。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为在获取该男子的陈述过程中，没有胁迫性的警察行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法保护与刑事诉讼程序
核心法律原则 (The Rule)

根据美国宪法第十四修正案的正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause)，供述必须是“自愿的” (Voluntary) 才能在法庭上被采纳。判断供述是否非自愿，关键在于是否存在胁迫性的警察行为 (Coercive Police Conduct)。

深度解析：为何选 D？

本题的正确答案是 D。这道题直接考察了美国最高法院的著名判例 Colorado v. Connelly (1986)。

1. 精神疾病 vs. 警察胁迫

虽然该男子的供述是由其“严重的精神疾病” (Serious Mental Illness) 诱发的（在 Connelly 案中，被告人声称听到上帝的声音让他自首），但这并不足以让供述在宪法意义上变成“非自愿” (Involuntary)。

2. 宪法的门槛：国家行为 (State Action)

正当程序条款旨在限制政府的行为，而不是个人的内部心理斗争。要认定供述无效，必须证明供述是警察不当行为的产物。如果警察没有使用威胁、暴力或不当的心理施压，那么即便嫌疑人是因为精神错乱而自首，该供述依然是可以采纳的。

3. 本案事实应用

  • 男子主动走进警局（无初始胁迫）。
  • 警察按程序宣读了 Miranda 警告。
  • 精神科医生确认该男子虽然有病，但有能力理解其权利 (Competent to understand rights)。
  • 警察没有任何不当行为。

因此，因为缺乏“胁迫性的警察行为”，该供述在法律上被视为自愿的。

排除干扰项
选项 A (错误)

理由：虽然供述是精神疾病的产物，但缺乏警察的因果关系。没有警察的胁迫，单纯的内部心理强迫不构成宪法上的“非自愿”。

选项 B (错误)

理由：题目明确指出医生判定该疾病“并未影响该男子理解其权利的能力”。只要弃权是明知 (Knowing) 和 理智 (Intelligent) 的，且没有外部胁迫，弃权就是有效的。

选项 C (错误)

理由：这是一个诱导性选项。虽然该男子最初是自愿走进警局的，但一旦他供认谋杀，任何理性的人都会认为自己不再自由（即进入了羁押状态 / Custody）。但这并不影响结论，因为即使在羁押中，只要没有胁迫且经过了 Miranda 弃权，供述依然有效。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理涉及供述自愿性 (Voluntariness) 的题目时，请务必寻找“警察的不当行为” (Police Misconduct)。

公式：
精神错乱 + 警察无过错 = 供述可采纳 (Admissible)
精神错乱 + 警察利用该弱点施压 = 供述不可采纳 (Inadmissible)

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state statute provides that the crime of assault is generally punishable by a maximum of five years in prison. It further provides that the maximum punishment increases to 10 years in prison if the defendant possessed a deadly weapon during the assault. The statute designates the deadly weapon element as a sentencing factor.
A defendant charged with assault has pleaded not guilty and has requested a jury trial. The prosecutor has announced that she will be seeking a 10-year sentence based on the defendant's alleged possession of a deadly weapon.
What finding regarding the defendant's possession of a deadly weapon is necessary for the court to impose a 10-year sentence?

choices.A: A judicial finding by a preponderance of the evidence.
choices.B: A jury finding by a preponderance of the evidence.
choices.C: A judicial finding beyond a reasonable doubt.
choices.D: A jury finding beyond a reasonable doubt.

questions.explanation:
Increasing statutory sentencing range
Assault
  • Attempted battery or
  • Intentionally created reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm
Statutory range: 0 to 5 years
(judicial sentencing allowed)
0
5
+
Sentencing factor
  • Possession of deadly weapon
Increased range: 5 to 10 years
(jury sentencing required)
0
10

Due process requires the prosecution to prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. This includes sentencing factors (other than a previous conviction) that, if proven, would increase the statutorily imposed sentencing range. And when a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to an impartial jury has been invoked, a jury must determine whether the prosecution has met that burden. Therefore, these sentencing factors can only be imposed if the jury finds that the prosecution has proven them beyond a reasonable doubt.

Here, the defendant was charged with assault, which generally carries a five-year maximum sentence. But the prosecutor announced that she will seek a 10-year sentence based on the defendant's alleged possession of a deadly weapon. Since this sentence would heighten the statute's maximum sentencing range, it can only be imposed if a jury finds beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant possessed a deadly weapon (Choices A, B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

A sentencing factor is considered an element of a criminal offense when it would increase the statutorily imposed sentencing range (if proven). Therefore, when the Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial has been invoked, the factor can only be imposed if a jury finds that the prosecution has proven it beyond a reasonable doubt.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to jury trial).
  • Apprendi v. New Jersey, 530 U.S. 466, 490 (2000) (explaining that a jury must decide facts that would increase the sentencing range).
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause).
  • In re Winship, 397 U.S. 358, 364 (1970) (holding that the prosecution must prove every element of a crime beyond a reasonable doubt).
questions.zh-question:
某州法规规定，攻击罪通常可处以最高五年监禁。法规还进一步规定，如果被告在攻击过程中持有致命武器，最高刑罚将增至十年监禁。该法规将持有致命武器这一情节指定为量刑因素。

一名被控犯有攻击罪的被告已作无罪辩护，并要求进行陪审团审判。检察官宣布，她将以被告涉嫌持有致命武器为由，寻求判处十年徒刑。

法院若要判处十年徒刑，需要对被告持有致命武器作出何种裁定？

zh-choices.A: 法官根据优势证据作出的裁定。
zh-choices.B: 陪审团根据优势证据作出的裁定。
zh-choices.C: 法官根据“排除合理怀疑”标准作出的裁定。
zh-choices.D: 陪审团根据“排除合理怀疑”标准作出的裁定。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law / Constitutional Law
正确答案：D 陪审团根据“排除合理怀疑”标准作出的裁定。
(A jury finding beyond a reasonable doubt.)

本题考察的是美国宪法第六修正案（陪审团审判权）和第十四修正案（正当程序条款）在刑事量刑中的核心原则，即著名的 Apprendi 规则。

Apprendi v. New Jersey (2000)

规则核心：除了前科（prior conviction）这一事实外，任何能够增加犯罪法定最高刑罚（statutory maximum）的事实，都必须：

  1. 提交给陪审团（Jury）；
  2. 并由陪审团以“排除合理怀疑”（Beyond a reasonable doubt）的标准予以证实。

⚖️ 法律推理逻辑

1. 标签不重要，效果才重要
虽然题目中的法规将“持有致命武器”标记为“量刑因素”（Sentencing Factor），但这并不意味着法官可以随意裁量。最高法院认为，如果一个事实的认定会导致被告面临的刑罚超过了原本法规规定的最高限度，那么这个事实在宪法意义上就等同于犯罪的构成要件（Element of the crime）。

2. 本案的具体分析

情形 最高刑期 裁决者 & 标准
普通攻击罪 5年 陪审团 / 排除合理怀疑
攻击 + 致命武器 10年 ?

由于“持有致命武器”这一事实将最高刑期从5年提高到了10年，根据 Apprendi 规则，它必须被视为犯罪构成要件处理。因此：

  • 谁来决定？ 必须是陪审团（除非被告放弃陪审团权利），不能是法官。
  • 什么标准？ 必须是刑事定罪的最高标准——排除合理怀疑（Beyond a reasonable doubt），而不能是民事或普通量刑听证中使用的“优势证据”（Preponderance of the evidence）标准。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 A & B (优势证据): 刑事案件中，任何增加法定最高刑罚的事实必须达到“排除合理怀疑”的证明标准。优势证据标准（>50%可能性）仅适用于不改变法定刑罚范围的普通量刑因素。
  • 选项 A & C (法官裁定): 既然该事实增加了法定最高刑，被告就有权要求由陪审团对此事实进行裁决。法官无权单方面认定该事实来突破原有的5年上限。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
看到题目中出现“Sentence Enhancement”（刑罚加重）或“Sentencing Factor”（量刑因素）时，请立即检查该因素是否提高了法定最高刑（Statutory Maximum）。

  • 如果提高了上限 ➡️ 必须由陪审团按排除合理怀疑标准认定（Apprendi Rule）。
  • 如果只是在原有范围内影响法官的量刑裁量（例如从0-5年变为3-5年，但上限仍是5年） ➡️ 法官可以根据优势证据认定。
MBE Criminal Law Review

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man and a woman were charged with murder. Each gave a confession to the police that implicated both of them. The woman later retracted her confession, claiming that it was coerced. The man and the woman were tried together. The prosecutor offered both confessions into evidence. The man and woman objected.
After a hearing, the trial judge found that both confessions were voluntary and admitted both into evidence. The woman testified at trial. She denied any involvement in the crime and claimed that her confession was false and the result of coercion. Both defendants were convicted.
On appeal, the woman contends her conviction should be reversed because of the admission into evidence of the man's confession.
Will the woman likely prevail on her appeal?

choices.A: No, because the woman testified at trial on her own behalf.
choices.B: No, because the woman's own confession was properly admitted into evidence.
choices.C: Yes, unless the man testified at trial.
choices.D: Yes, whether or not the man testified at trial.

questions.explanation:
Brutonrule
Codefendant's out-of-court statement admissible if:
  • codefendant testifies
  • statement redacts (removes) reference to defendant, statement refers to defendant neutrally (e.g., "other person") & jury provided with limiting instruction or
  • statement used to rebut claim of coerced confession & jury is instructed as such

Most errors made by the trial court will be reviewed on appeal for harmless error. Under the harmless error test, the government must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the error did not contribute to the defendant's conviction or the conviction will be reversed. Error occurs when the trial court violates a defendant's constitutional rights.

In a joint jury trial, two or more defendants are tried before the same jury for charges related to the same facts. Each defendant has the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination and can refuse to testify at trial. But each defendant also has the Sixth Amendment right to confront (ie, cross-examine) adverse witnesses. So, if the trial court admits an out-of-court statement made by a non-testifying co-defendant that is adverse to the other defendant (eg, implicates that defendant in the crime), it violates that defendant's right to confrontation.

Here, the man and the woman each gave a confession to the police that implicated them both for murder. During their joint jury trial, the prosecution offered their prior confessions into evidence. Since the man's confession implicated the woman in the crime, the trial court's decision to admit his prior confession into evidence violated her right to confrontation if he did not testify at trial. Therefore, the woman will likely prevail on her appeal unless the man testified and was thereby subject to cross-examination (Choice D).

(Choice A) Although the woman testified at trial on her own behalf, she could not confront the man through cross-examination if he did not testify. And since her testimony did not render the erroneous admission of the man's confession harmless beyond a reasonable doubt, her conviction should be reversed on appeal.

(Choice B) The woman's confession was properly admitted into evidence because she testified at trial. Although her confession may have aided in her conviction, this fails to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the man's confession did not contribute to her conviction.

📌 Educational Objective

In a joint jury trial, the Sixth Amendment confrontation clause is violated when a non-testifying co-defendant's prior statement implicating the other defendant in the crime is admitted at trial.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (confrontation clause).
  • Bruton v. United States, 391 U.S. 123, 136 (1968) (analyzing the right to confront co-defendant).
  • Schneble v. Florida, 405 U.S. 427, 430 (1972) (recognizing that the standard of appellate review for a confrontation issue is harmless error).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子和一名女子被控谋杀。两人都向警方供认，供词牵涉到对方。该女子后来撤回了她的供词，声称是受到了胁迫。该男子和女子被并案审理。检察官将两份供词作为证据提交。该男子和女子提出了反对意见。

经过听证，初审法官认定两份供词均为自愿作出，并采纳其为证据。该女子在审判中出庭作证。她否认参与该罪行，并声称她的供词是虚假的，是胁迫的结果。两名被告均被定罪。

在上诉中，该女子主张，由于采纳了男子的供词作为证据，她的定罪应被撤销。

该女子在上诉中可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该女子在审判中为自己作证。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该女子自己的供词被合法地采纳为证据。
zh-choices.C: 会，除非该男子在审判中出庭作证。
zh-choices.D: 会，无论该男子是否在审判中出庭作证。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法保护：对质条款与共同被告

正确答案：C 会，除非该男子在审判中出庭作证。
(Yes, unless the man testified at trial.)
核心考点：Bruton 规则

本题考查美国宪法第六修正案的对质条款 (Confrontation Clause)。

根据著名判例 Bruton v. United States (1968)，在共同审判 (Joint Trial) 中，如果检察官引入了未出庭作证的共同被告 (Non-testifying Co-defendant) 的供词，且该供词牵涉到另一名被告，这侵犯了该被告的对质权。

1. 问题的根源

男子和女子被共同审判。男子的供词指控了女子。如果男子不出庭作证，他就在行使第五修正案的沉默权。这意味着女子的律师无法对他进行交叉询问 (Cross-examination)。无法交叉询问指控自己的人，即违反了第六修正案。

2. 为什么选项 C 是正确的？

对质条款的核心是“对质”的机会。如果该男子出庭作证（放弃沉默权），那么女子就可以通过律师对他进行交叉询问，宪法权利因此得到满足（参见 Nelson v. O'Neil）。

因此，女子能否胜诉的关键在于：男子是否出庭？

  • 如果男子未出庭：侵犯对质权 → 女子胜诉。
  • 如果男子出庭：满足对质权 → 女子败诉。

选项 C 准确地指出了这一决定性条件。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (女子自己作证了):
错误。女子作证只能让她接受交叉询问，但这并不能解决她无法交叉询问男子的问题。男子的供词依然是针对她的不可靠证据。

选项 B (女子的供词也被采纳):
错误。这涉及“连锁供词” (Interlocking Confessions) 问题。根据 Cruz v. New York (1987)，即使被告自己的供词也被采纳，共同被告的供词（如果共同被告未作证）仍然不可采纳。因为陪审团可能会利用共同被告的供词来证实被告供词的真实性，从而造成损害。

选项 D (无论男子是否作证):
错误。如上所述，如果男子作证并接受交叉询问，对质条款的问题就解决了，女子就没有理由以此为由推翻定罪。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Joint Trial"（共同审判） + "Confession"（供词）时，立即警惕 Bruton Rule。

检查两个条件：

  1. 供词是否牵涉另一名被告？(Facially incriminating)
  2. 作供词的被告是否出庭接受交叉询问？

如果牵涉对方且未出庭，即为违宪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man kidnapped a victim in State A and transported the victim across the state border into State B. These actions violated the kidnapping laws of both states, which are identical. A jury convicted the man in a State A court, but the trial judge gave what prosecutors in State B deemed an unduly lenient sentence. The state prosecutor in State B then commenced a kidnapping case against the man for violating State B's kidnapping statute.
The man's lawyer has filed a motion in State B to dismiss the charge based on the double jeopardy protection against a second prosecution for the man's single act of kidnapping.
Should the court grant the motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because the double jeopardy protection only prohibits a second prosecution following an acquittal for the same offense.
choices.B: No, because the man's conduct violated the laws of two different states, and each has the right to enforce its laws.
choices.C: Yes, because the double jeopardy protection prohibits a second prosecution following a conviction for the same offense.
choices.D: Yes, because the government is collaterally estopped under the double jeopardy protection from prosecuting a defendant a second time for the same conduct that led to an earlier conviction.

questions.explanation:
Dual sovereignty doctrine

(prosecution under identical statutes permitted in
State A, State B & federal courts)

Federal
courts
State A
State B

The Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause (applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment) protects a criminal defendant from undue harassment, embarrassment, and expense by prohibiting all of the following:

  • Multiple punishments for the same offense
  • Second prosecution for the same offense after a conviction (ie, judgment of guilt)
  • Second prosecution for the same offense after an acquittal (ie, judgment of not guilty)

Different sovereigns (ie, governments) may have identical criminal statutes. But under the dual sovereignty doctrine, those statutes are considered distinct offenses because each sovereign derives its power from a different source (eg, its own state constitution). Therefore, different sovereigns can prosecute a defendant for the same criminal act without violating the double jeopardy clause.

Here, State A convicted the man for violating its kidnapping law. State B then sought to prosecute him for the same kidnapping act under State B's kidnapping law. Although the kidnapping laws of both states are identical, each law constitutes a distinct offense because State A and State B are separate sovereigns.

Therefore, State B can prosecute the man for kidnapping without violating the double jeopardy clause, and the court should deny his motion to dismiss the charge (Choice C).

(Choice A) Double jeopardy prohibits a second prosecution following an acquittal or a conviction for the same offense. And though the man was convicted (not acquitted) of kidnapping in State A, he can still be prosecuted for that same criminal act under State B's kidnapping statute (a distinct offense under the dual sovereignty doctrine).

(Choice D) Double jeopardy embodies the doctrine of collateral estoppel (ie, issue preclusion), which prevents the relitigation of any issue of ultimate fact that has already been determined by a prior final judgment. However, this doctrine does not apply to successive prosecutions for the same criminal act by different sovereigns (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The dual sovereignty doctrine allows different sovereigns to prosecute a defendant for the same criminal act without violating the Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • Heath v. Alabama, 474 U.S. 82, 88 (1985) ("[S]uccessive prosecutions by two States for the same conduct are not barred by the Double Jeopardy Clause.").
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在A州绑架了一名受害者，并将其跨越州界运送至B州。这些行为违反了两州内容相同的绑架法。A州法院的陪审团判定该男子有罪，但初审法官的判决被B州的检察官认为过于宽大。于是，B州的州检察官以违反B州绑架法规为由，对该男子提起了绑架案的诉讼。

该男子的律师以双重危险保护（禁止对单一绑架行为进行二次起诉）为由，在B州提出驳回指控的动议。

法院是否应批准该驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: A. 不应批准，因为双重危险保护仅禁止在因同一罪行被宣告无罪后进行二次起诉。
zh-choices.B: B. 不应批准，因为该男子的行为违反了两个不同州的法律，而每个州都有权执行其法律。
zh-choices.C: C. 应批准，因为双重危险保护禁止在因同一罪行被定罪后进行二次起诉。
zh-choices.D: D. 应批准，因为根据双重危险保护中的附带禁反言原则，政府不得因导致先前定罪的同一行为而对被告进行二次起诉。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Double Jeopardy
📚 核心考点：双重主权原则 (Dual Sovereignty Doctrine)

虽然美国宪法第五修正案禁止双重危险 (Double Jeopardy)，即禁止对同一罪行进行二次起诉，但这一保护仅限于同一主权实体 (Same Sovereign)。

如果两个不同的主权实体（如两个不同的州，或联邦政府与州政府）分别起诉，即使是针对同一行为 (Same Conduct)，也不违反双重危险条款。

✅ 正确答案解析
正确选项 B

理由：本题中，A州和B州是两个独立的主权实体。

根据最高法院在 Heath v. Alabama (1985) 中的判例，当被告的行为同时违反了两个州的法律时，每个州都拥有独立的主权权力来执行其刑法。因此，A州的定罪并不阻碍B州对同一行为提起诉讼。

这被视为两个不同的罪行 (Distinct Offenses)，而非对同一罪行的重复起诉。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A 错误

双重危险保护不仅适用于无罪释放 (Acquittal)，也适用于定罪 (Conviction)。如果是在同一个州内，定罪后再次起诉同一罪行是违宪的。该选项对法律规则的陈述不完整。

选项 C 错误

这是考生最容易误选的项。虽然双重危险确实禁止二次起诉，但它忽略了本题的核心考点——双重主权例外。因为涉及两个不同的州，所以该禁止令不适用。
