选项 D 错误

附带禁反言 (Collateral Estoppel) 或争点排除 (Issue Preclusion) 确实是双重危险的一部分（见 Ashe v. Swenson），但它要求诉讼双方是同一方。由于B州不是A州诉讼的一方，B州不受A州判决的约束。

💡 MBE 实战技巧

在遇到 Double Jeopardy 题目时，请按以下步骤检查：

  1. 看主体：是同一个政府在起诉吗？
    • 联邦 vs. 州 = ✅ 允许 (双重主权)
    • 州 A vs. 州 B = ✅ 允许 (双重主权)
    • 州 vs. 该州内的市/县 = ❌ 禁止 (视为同一主权，见 Waller v. Florida)
  2. 看罪行：是否包含相同的要素 (Blockburger Test)？

本题只要识别出是跨州 (State A vs. State B)，即可直接应用双重主权原则锁定答案。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state statute provides as follows: "In all criminal cases, whenever the U.S. Constitution permits, the burden of proof as to a defense claimed by the defendant shall rest on the defendant, and the magnitude of the burden shall be as great as the Constitution permits."
The same state defines the crime of forcible rape as follows: "Forcible rape consists of sexual penetration inflicted on an unconsenting person by means of force or violence. Consent of the victim is a complete defense to a charge of rape."
At a defendant's trial for forcible rape, he testified that the alleged victim had consented to having sexual intercourse with him.
How should the trial judge instruct the jury regarding the burden of proof on the issue of consent?

choices.A: The defendant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the victim consented.
choices.B: The defendant must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the victim consented.
choices.C: The defendant must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the victim consented.
choices.D: The prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the victim did not consent.

questions.explanation:
Burden of proof hierarchy
affirmative defense
to criminal prosecution
Beyond a reasonable doubt
(eg, criminal prosecutions)
Clear and convincing evidence
(eg, fraud, child custody)
Preponderance of the evidence
(eg, most civil cases)

Due process requires that the government prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, even when the defendant asserts a defense that negates an element of the crime (eg, lack of intent, alibi), the burden of proof must remain on the prosecution to prove that element—it cannot be placed on the defendant. Since a jury instruction must reflect this constitutional requirement, an instruction violates due process if it places the burden on the defendant to prove any element of the crime.

In this state, forcible rape requires proof that: (1) sexual penetration occurred, (2) the victim did not consent, and (3) the defendant used force or violence. Since the defendant testified that the alleged victim consented to having sexual intercourse, he is asserting a defense (consent) that negates the second element of the crime (no consent). Therefore, to comply with due process, the judge should instruct the jury that the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the victim did not consent.

(Choices A, B & C) Since consent is a defense that challenges an element of the crime, the prosecution must bear the burden of proving that element (and disproving that defense) beyond a reasonable doubt. But had the defendant raised an affirmative defense—ie, a defense that justifies or excuses criminal conduct but does not negate an element of the crime—he could have been required to prove that defense under any evidentiary standard (eg, preponderance of the evidence, clear and convincing evidence, beyond a reasonable doubt).

📌 Educational Objective

Due process requires that the prosecution prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt to convict a defendant—even when the defendant asserts a defense that negates an element of the crime.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause applied to the states).
  • Patterson v. New York, 432 U.S. 197, 210 (1977) (explaining that the prosecution must prove every element of a crime beyond a reasonable doubt).
questions.zh-question:
某州的一项法规规定如下： "在所有刑事案件中，只要 U.S. Constitution 允许，被告人提出的抗辩的证明责任应由被告人承担，且该责任的程度应达到 U.S. Constitution 所允许的最大限度。"

该州对强奸罪的定义如下： "强奸罪是指以武力或暴力手段对未同意者进行性侵入。受害人的同意是对强奸指控的完全抗辩。"

在被告人因强奸罪受审时，他作证称，所谓的受害人同意与他发生性关系。

关于同意问题的证明责任，主审法官应如何指示陪审团？

zh-choices.A: 被告人必须以“优势证据”证明受害人同意。
zh-choices.B: 被告人必须以“清晰且有说服力的证据”证明受害人同意。
zh-choices.C: 被告人必须以“排除合理怀疑”的证明标准证明受害人同意。
zh-choices.D: 控方必须以“排除合理怀疑”的证明标准证明受害人未同意。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Protection & Burden of Proof
核心法律原则

本题考察的是美国宪法第十四修正案下的正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 对刑事案件证明责任的要求。

In re Winship (1970) 原则：
控方 (Prosecution) 必须以“排除合理怀疑” (Beyond a Reasonable Doubt) 的标准，证明犯罪的每一个构成要件 (Every Element)。
案情拆解与分析

让我们分析题目中该州对“强奸罪” (Forcible Rape) 的定义：

  • 1. 性侵入 (Sexual penetration)
  • 2. 使用武力或暴力 (Force or violence)
  • 3. 针对未同意者 (On an unconsenting person) 👈 关键点

逻辑推演：

由于法规将“未同意者” (Unconsenting person) 直接写在犯罪定义中，因此“缺乏同意” (Lack of Consent) 是该罪的一个核心构成要件 (Element)。

被告辩称受害人“同意”了。这并不是在承认犯罪行为的同时提出借口（如正当防卫），而是在直接否定上述第3个构成要件。

正确答案解析
✅ 选项 D 正确

理由：

既然“缺乏同意”是犯罪构成要件，根据宪法要求，控方必须承担证明该要件的全部责任。

题目中的州法虽然试图转移举证责任，但有一个限制条件：“只要 U.S. Constitution 允许” (whenever the U.S. Constitution permits)。

因为宪法不允许将“否定犯罪构成要件”的证明责任转移给被告，所以该限制条件生效，证明责任必须留在控方，且标准必须是“排除合理怀疑”。

考点陷阱：积极抗辩 vs. 否定要件

这是 MBE 常见的混淆点，请务必区分：

1. 否定构成要件 (Negating an Element)
例如：被告说“我没做”或“她是同意的”（针对强奸罪）。
➡ 证明责任永远在控方 (BARD)。
2. 积极抗辩 (Affirmative Defense)
例如：精神错乱 (Insanity)、正当防卫 (Self-defense)（在某些州）。即“我做了，但是我有合法理由”。
➡ 宪法允许州法律将证明责任转移给被告（通常是优势证据标准）。
本题关键：因为“未同意”被写进了犯罪定义，所以“同意”是在否定要件，而非积极抗辩。因此选项 A、B、C 试图将被告置于举证地位，均违反宪法。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到“Burden of Proof”题目时，第一步先看法规定义的犯罪元素。如果被告的抗辩只是在说“犯罪元素之一不存在”，那么证明责任绝不能转移给被告。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A federal officer had probable cause to believe that a woman had participated in a bank robbery. Two days after the robbery, the woman checked into a local hotel. When the woman left her room for the evening, the hotel manager opened the hotel room door so that the officer could enter the room and look inside. The officer did not find any of the stolen money but did see, lying open on the bed, the woman's diary. The diary contained an entry describing the woman's involvement in robbing the bank.
The woman was charged in federal court with bank robbery. She has moved to suppress the diary.
Should the court suppress the diary?

choices.A: No, because the hotel manager had actual authority to allow the officer into the hotel room.
choices.B: No, because the officer reasonably relied on the hotel manager's apparent authority to allow the officer into the hotel room.
choices.C: Yes, because admitting the diary would violate the woman's privilege against self-incrimination.
choices.D: Yes, because the officer had no warrant.

questions.explanation:
Admissibility of evidence obtained by Fourth Amendment violation
Did government conduct search?
  • Physical trespass: intrusion of constitutionally protected area
    OR
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy: invasion of subjectively and objectively reasonable privacy expectation
Admissible
↓
Was search unreasonable?
  • No warrant
    AND
  • No applicable exception
    • Search incident to valid arrest
    • Administrative search of highly regulated industry
    • Stop and frisk
    • Plain view doctrine
    • Automobile exception
    • Consent
    • Exigent circumstance
    • Special government purpose
Mnemonic: SAD SPACES
Admissible
↓
Inadmissible

A court should suppress evidence obtained during an unreasonable Fourth Amendment search. A search is unreasonable if it is conducted without a warrant based on probable cause and no exception to the warrant requirement applies. Consent is an exception that allows police to conduct a warrantless search when (1) consent is given voluntarily (ie, the product of free will, not police coercion), (2) the search is limited to the scope of the consent, and (3) the person giving consent has the actual or apparent authority to do so.

• Actual authority exists when the person giving consent has the right to use or occupy the property
—eg, a registered hotel guest.

• Apparent authority exists when police reasonably (but erroneously) believe that the person giving consent has actual authority to do so—eg, the person answering the hotel room door falsely states that he/she is staying in the room.

Hotel managers do not have actual authority to consent to a warrantless search of a guest's room because they have no right to use or occupy the room during the guest's stay (Choice A). And in Stoner v. California, the Supreme Court held that hotel managers lack apparent authority because police cannot reasonably believe that managers have actual authority to consent (Choice B). Therefore, the hotel manager could not consent to the officer's warrantless entry of the woman's hotel room, and the diary found during that search should be suppressed.

(Choice C) The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects individuals from being compelled to create or produce self-incriminating evidence. Here, the woman's diary entry described her involvement in the bank robbery (self-incriminating evidence). But since she voluntarily wrote that entry (no compelled creation) and the diary was discovered during a search of her hotel room (no compelled production), it will not be suppressed on Fifth Amendment grounds.

📌 Educational Objective

Consent to a search must be given by a person with (1) actual authority—the right to use or occupy the property—or (2) apparent authority—police reasonably, but erroneously, believe that the person has actual authority to consent. Therefore, hotel managers have no authority to consent to a warrantless search of a guest's hotel room.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Stoner v. California, 376 U.S. 483, 489–90 (1964) (explaining that a hotel guest has a reasonable expectation of privacy in his/her room and a hotel manager cannot consent to a search of the room).
questions.zh-question:
一名联邦执法人员有相当理由相信一名女子参与了一起银行抢劫案。抢劫案发生两天后，该女子入住了一家当地酒店。当晚该女子离开房间后，酒店经理打开房门，让该执法人员进入房间查看。该执法人员没有找到任何被盗钱款，但看到该女子的日记摊开在床上。日记中有一则条目描述了该女子参与抢劫银行的经过。

该女子在联邦法院被控犯有银行抢劫罪。她已申请排除该日记作为证据。

法院是否应当排除该日记？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为酒店经理拥有允许执法人员进入酒店房间的实际权限。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为执法人员合理信赖酒店经理拥有允许其进入酒店房间的表见权限。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为采纳该日记将侵犯该女子反对自证其罪的特权。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该执法人员没有搜查令。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Search & Seizure
正确答案：D 是，因为该执法人员没有搜查令。
(Yes, because the officer had no warrant.)

本题的核心考点在于第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）对搜查的要求，特别是第三方同意（Third-Party Consent）在酒店环境中的适用性。

⚖️ 法律推理 (Legal Reasoning)

根据美国宪法第四修正案，警方进行搜查通常需要基于相当理由（Probable Cause）并取得搜查令（Warrant）。无证搜查（Warrantless Search）原则上被视为不合理，除非适用特定的例外情况（如同意、紧急情况等）。

本案中，执法人员没有搜查令，而是依赖酒店经理的“同意”进入房间。这里涉及两个关键概念：

  • 实际权限 (Actual Authority)： 酒店经理虽然有权进入房间进行打扫或维修，但没有权利代表客人放弃其隐私权，允许警方进行搜查。
  • 表见权限 (Apparent Authority)： 警方是否可以“合理地相信”经理有权同意？最高法院已明确裁定，警方依赖酒店职员的同意进入客房是不合理的。
Stoner v. California (1964)

这是一个经典的 MBE 判例。最高法院裁定，酒店客人对自己的房间享有合理的隐私期待 (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。虽然客人默示同意酒店员工（如清洁工）进入，但这并不意味着同意让警察进入搜查。因此，酒店经理无权同意警方的无证搜查。

由于经理的同意无效，警方的进入是非法的。因此，即使日记是“一目了然”（Plain View）地放在床上，由于警方非法进入在先，该证据是毒树之果（Fruit of the Poisonous Tree），必须被排除。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A (实际权限) 错误：
如上所述，酒店经理拥有管理酒店的权限，但没有“实际权限”去放弃客人的宪法权利。客人支付房费后，在该期间内拥有房间的专属占有权。
选项 B (表见权限) 错误：
表见权限要求警方的信赖是“合理的”（Reasonable）。由于法律明确规定酒店经理无权同意搜查，执法人员如果认为经理有权同意，这种信念是法律上的错误，不被视为合理信赖。
选项 C (第五修正案) 错误：
这是一个常见的干扰项。第五修正案（Privilege against Self-Incrimination）保护的是不被“强迫”自证其罪。日记是该女子自愿写下的，并非警方强迫她写的。搜查日记属于第四修正案（搜查与扣押）的问题，而非第五修正案的问题。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理搜查与扣押 (Search and Seizure) 的题目时，请遵循以下逻辑链条：

  1. 政府行为？ (是，联邦官员)
  2. 合理的隐私期待？ (是，酒店房间如同家一样受保护)
  3. 有搜查令吗？ (无)
  4. 有例外情况吗？ (本题考察“同意”例外)

记住： 房东（Landlord）和酒店经理（Hotel Manager）通常不能同意警方搜查租客或客人的房间。如果题目中警察仅凭房东或经理开门就进去搜查，该搜查通常是非法的。

MBE 模拟题解析 | Constitutional Law & Criminal Procedure

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An executive director of an equal housing opportunity organization was the leader of a sit-in at the offices of a real estate management company. The protest was designed to call attention to the company's racially discriminatory rental practices. When police demanded that the director desist from trespassing on the company's property, she refused and was arrested.
In the director's trial for trespass, the prosecution peremptorily excused all nonwhites from the jury, arguing to the court that even though the director was white, minority groups would automatically support her because of her fight against racism in housing accommodations.
The director is convicted of trespass by an all-white jury and appeals, claiming a violation of her constitutional rights.
How will the court likely rule on appeal?

choices.A: Affirm the conviction, because peremptory challenge of the nonwhites did not deny the director the right to an impartial jury.
choices.B: Affirm the conviction, because the director was not a member of the class discriminated against.
choices.C: Reverse the conviction, because racially based peremptory challenges violate equal protection of the law.
choices.D: Reverse the conviction, because the director was denied the right to have her case heard by a fair cross section of the community.

questions.explanation:
Jury panel challenges
Peremptory Disqualify potential juror for any reason except discrimination based on race, ethnicity, or sex
For cause Disqualify potential juror for a stated reason for believing juror cannot be fair or impartial (eg, bias, prejudice, past experience)

A peremptory challenge is an objection to a potential juror that can be raised without any reason or explanation during the jury-selection process. However, the prosecution's use of peremptory challenges must comply with the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause, which prohibits striking potential jurors based solely on their race, ethnicity, or sex. To successfully contest a peremptory challenge on equal protections grounds (Batson challenge) and receive a new trial on appeal:

  • the defendant must establish a prima facie case of discrimination (eg, the prosecution used peremptory challenges to strike only female jurors)
  • the prosecution may then provide a sufficiently neutral reason for the peremptory challenges (eg, the strikes were based on age, not gender) and
  • if it does so, the defendant must then prove intentional discrimination—that the prosecution's reasoning is insufficient or implausible (eg, the prosecution purportedly struck a 21-year-old woman due to her age but did not strike a 21-year-old man).

Here, the prosecution used its peremptory challenges to strike all nonwhites from the jury (prima facie racial discrimination). The prosecution explained that it did so because it believed minority groups would automatically support the director due to her civil rights background (non-neutral reason). Therefore, the prosecution's strikes violated the equal protection clause and the appellate court will likely reverse the director's conviction.

(Choice A) Under the Sixth Amendment, a criminal defendant must be tried by an impartial jury that can decide the case on the evidence presented—not personal biases. Here, there is no evidence that the all-white jury was biased when it convicted the director, so the prosecution's peremptory challenges of all nonwhites did not violate her right to an impartial jury. However, her conviction can still be reversed on equal protection grounds.

(Choice B) A defendant can make a Batson challenge even if he/she is not a member of the class of stricken jurors. Therefore, the fact that the director is white and the stricken jurors are nonwhite does not prevent the appellate court from holding that the peremptory challenges violated the director's right to equal protection.

(Choice D) The Sixth Amendment requirement that a jury be drawn from a fair cross section of the community applies to the composition of the jury venire (the panel of citizens from which a jury is selected)—not the empaneled jury (citizens selected from the jury venire to hear the case).

📌 Educational Objective

Peremptory challenges can be used to strike potential jurors without any reason or explanation, unless they are used to exclude potential jurors based solely on their race, ethnicity, or sex.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV § 1 (equal protection clause).
  • Batson v. Kentucky, 476 U.S. 79, 89 (1986) (holding that peremptory challenges cannot be used to strike jurors based on their race).
  • Powers v. Ohio, 499 U.S. 400, 409 (1991) (explaining that peremptory challenges cannot be used to strike jurors based on race even if defendant and stricken jurors are different races).
questions.zh-question:
一个平等住房机会组织的执行总监在一家房地产管理公司的办公室领导了一场静坐示威。该抗议旨在引起人们对该公司种族歧视性租赁行为的关注。当警察要求该总监停止非法侵入公司财产时，她拒绝了，并因此被捕。

在该总监因非法侵入罪受审时，检方以无因回避的方式排除了所有非白人陪审员，并向法庭辩称，尽管该总监是白人，但少数族裔群体会因为她在住房问题上反对种族主义的斗争而自动支持她。

该总监被一个全由白人组成的陪审团裁定犯有非法侵入罪，并提起上诉，声称她的宪法权利受到侵犯。

上诉法院可能会如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 维持原判，因为对非白人陪审员的无因回避并未剥夺该总监获得公正陪审团审判的权利。
zh-choices.B: 维持原判，因为该总监并非被歧视群体的成员。
zh-choices.C: 推翻原判，因为基于种族的无因回避违反了法律的平等保护原则。
zh-choices.D: 推翻原判，因为该总监被剥夺了由能公平代表社区横断面的陪审团审理其案件的权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法保护与刑事诉讼程序
正确答案：选项 C

推翻原判，因为基于种族的无因回避违反了法律的平等保护原则 (Equal Protection Clause)。

核心考点：Batson Challenge

本题考查的是著名的 Batson v. Kentucky (1986) 规则。该规则确立了以下原则：

  • 规则内容：虽然无因回避 (Peremptory Challenge) 通常不需要理由，但检方不得仅基于种族 (Race)、族裔或性别来排除潜在陪审员。
  • 宪法依据：这种做法违反了美国宪法第十四修正案的平等保护条款 (Equal Protection Clause)。
关键难点：被告种族是否重要？

很多考生会因为被告是白人，而被排除的陪审员是非白人而感到困惑（选项B的陷阱）。

法律规则 (Powers v. Ohio, 1991)：

最高法院裁定，刑事被告有权对基于种族的陪审员排除提出异议，无论被告与被排除的陪审员是否属于同一种族。

理由：被告有权由通过非歧视程序选出的陪审团进行审判。此外，被告是在主张被排除陪审员的平等保护权利。

本案分析

在本题中，检方不仅排除了所有非白人，而且明确承认了理由是基于种族的刻板印象（认为少数族裔会自动支持反种族歧视的被告）。

这构成了直接的蓄意歧视 (Intentional Discrimination)。即使检方辩称这是为了“赢得官司”而非出于恶意，基于种族的归类本身就是违宪的。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误：
虽然第六修正案保障“公正的陪审团”，但本案的核心是第十四修正案的“平等保护”。即使最终的全白人陪审团是公正的，甄选过程中的种族歧视本身就是可逆转的错误 (Reversible Error)。
选项 B 错误：
如前所述，根据 Powers v. Ohio，被告无需是被排除群体的成员即可提出 Batson 异议。
选项 D 错误（常见混淆点）：
“公平代表社区横断面” (Fair Cross-Section) 的要求仅适用于陪审员候选库 (Jury Venire) 的组成，而不适用于最终选出的审判陪审团 (Empaneled Jury)。只要候选库是随机抽取的，最终陪审团全白并不自动违反第六修正案，除非是因为违宪的无因回避导致的（这回到了选项C的理由）。

💡 MBE 考试通关秘籍

当你在题目中看到：

  1. Jury Selection (陪审团甄选)
  2. Peremptory Challenge (无因回避)
  3. Race/Gender (种族/性别)

请立即联想到 Batson Challenge 和 Equal Protection。

切记：无论被告是什么种族，只要检方基于种族排除陪审员，就是违宪，定罪必须被推翻。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was charged with manslaughter. At the preliminary hearing, the magistrate dismissed the charge on the ground that the evidence was insufficient. The prosecutor then brought the case before a grand jury. After hearing the evidence presented by the prosecutor, the grand jury refused to return an indictment.
The prosecutor waited a few months until a new grand jury had been impaneled and brought the case before that grand jury, which returned an indictment charging the defendant with manslaughter. The defendant has moved to dismiss the indictment on double jeopardy grounds.
Should the motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because jeopardy had not attached before either grand jury was impaneled.
choices.B: No, because there has been no conviction or acquittal.
choices.C: Yes, because any proceeding after the preliminary hearing would violate double jeopardy.
choices.D: Yes, because bringing the case before the second grand jury violated the double jeopardy clause.

A court should dismiss an indictment—a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a criminal offense—that violates the Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause. Double jeopardy prohibits (1) multiple punishments for the same offense and (2) a second prosecution for the same offense following a conviction or an acquittal. This prohibition only applies after jeopardy attaches—ie:

  • in a jury trial when the jury is impaneled and sworn or
  • in a bench trial when the judge begins to hear evidence (eg, when the first witness is sworn).

Jeopardy does not attach at preliminary hearings or grand jury proceedings because a defendant is not yet on trial before a trier of fact (judge or jury). Therefore, the magistrate's dismissal of the defendant's manslaughter charge at a preliminary hearing and the grand jury's refusal to return an indictment did not trigger double jeopardy protections. As a result, the prosecution did not violate double jeopardy when it presented the same manslaughter case to a new grand jury that returned an indictment. The court should therefore deny the defendant's motion to dismiss the indictment (Choices C & D).

(Choice B) Double jeopardy protections attach as soon as a jury has been sworn or a judge has heard evidence—not when the defendant has been convicted or acquitted. Therefore, had jeopardy attached in this case, the indictment could have been dismissed on double jeopardy grounds even though the defendant had not been convicted or acquitted of manslaughter.

📌 Educational Objective

The Fifth Amendment double jeopardy protections attach when a jury has been impaneled and sworn OR a judge has begun to hear evidence—not at preliminary hearings or grand jury proceedings.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • Serfass v. United States, 420 U.S. 377, 388 (1975) (explaining when jeopardy attaches).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告被指控犯有非预谋杀人罪（manslaughter）。在预审听证（preliminary hearing）中，治安法官（magistrate）以证据不足为由驳回了该指控。检察官随后将此案提交给大陪审团（grand jury）。在听取了检察官提交的证据后，大陪审团拒绝发出正式起诉书（indictment）。

检察官等待了几个月，直到一个新的大陪审团成立（impaneled），然后将案件提交给该大陪审团，该陪审团发出了指控被告犯有非预谋杀人罪的正式起诉书。被告以“一事不再理”（double jeopardy）为由，请求驳回该正式起诉书。

该动议应被批准吗？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为在任一大陪审团成立之前，危险（jeopardy）均未附着。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为尚未有定罪或无罪判决。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为预审听证后的任何程序都将违反“一事不再理”原则。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为将案件提交给第二个大陪审团违反了“一事不再理”条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Double Jeopardy
⚖️ 核心规则：危险何时附着？
(When does Jeopardy Attach?)

根据美国宪法第五修正案，"一事不再理" (Double Jeopardy) 的保护仅在危险附着 (Jeopardy Attaches) 之后才生效。

  • 陪审团审判 (Jury Trial)： 当陪审团被选定并宣誓 (Empaneled and Sworn) 时。
  • 法官审判 (Bench Trial)： 当第一位证人宣誓 (First witness is sworn) 时。

🔍 本案流程分析

预审听证 (Preliminary Hearing)
法官因证据不足驳回指控。
❌ 危险未附着
大陪审团 #1 (Grand Jury)
拒绝发出起诉书 (No Bill)。
❌ 危险未附着
大陪审团 #2 (Grand Jury)
发出正式起诉书 (Indictment)。
✅ 程序合法

结论： 在本案的所有早期阶段（预审和大陪审团），被告从未面对事实审理者（Trier of Fact），因此危险从未附着。检察官可以不断尝试起诉，直到大陪审团同意或诉讼时效已过。

✅ 正确答案 A：
动议不应被批准，因为在任一大陪审团成立之前，危险均未附着。这是对法律规则的直接应用。
⚠️ 易错选项 B：
"不应批准，因为尚未有定罪或无罪判决。"

为什么错？ 这是一个经典的干扰项。Double Jeopardy 的保护不需要等到最终判决（定罪或无罪）。一旦陪审团宣誓，危险就附着了。如果在那之后法官错误地宣布无效审判（Mistrial），被告也可以主张 Double Jeopardy，即使当时还没有判决结果。

考试技巧： 只要看到 "Grand Jury" 或 "Preliminary Hearing"，就要立刻反应出 "Jeopardy has NOT attached"。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was lawfully arrested for bank robbery, without an arrest warrant. He was not given Miranda warnings but was immediately taken to a police station, where he and five other men were placed in a lineup to be viewed by the bank teller who had been on duty at the time of the robbery. Each man was required to say the words spoken by the bank robber: "Give me all your money. I've got a gun." After all the men in the lineup spoke those words, the teller identified the defendant as the robber.
The defendant subsequently moved to suppress the teller's testimony, claiming that the lineup violated his privilege against self-incrimination. At the suppression hearing, the teller testified that she had not gotten a good look at the robber's face, because the robber had been wearing a hat pulled down over most of his face, but that she was certain the defendant was the robber because she had recognized his voice at the lineup.
Should the defendant's motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because being required to speak at the lineup, while compelled, was not testimonial or communicative.
choices.B: No, because testimony of a witness based on firsthand observation is not subject to exclusion as the fruit of the poisonous tree.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant was compelled to speak at the lineup, and this compelled speech led to the teller's identification testimony.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant was never informed that he could refuse to make a statement and that any statement could be used as evidence against him.

questions.explanation:
Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination
Testimonial
communications(privileged)
  • Oral testimony
  • Act of producing documents
Real or physical evidence(not privileged)
  • Fingerprints
  • Handwriting samples
  • Voice tests
  • Photographs
  • Physical characteristics & clothing
  • Movements or gestures
  • Blood, DNA, urine samples

A court should grant a motion to suppress if the defendant's statement was taken in violation of his/her Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. This privilege protects a suspect from being compelled to provide incriminating evidence. But the privilege only applies to compelled testimonial communications (eg, oral testimony)—not real or physical evidence (eg, fingerprinting, voice identification).

Here, the police arrested the defendant and forced him to say the words spoken by the bank robber in a lineup (compulsion). The teller then identified the defendant as the robber by his voice (incriminating evidence). But since the privilege against self-incrimination does not apply to real or physical evidence (eg, voice identification), the court should deny the defendant's motion to suppress.

(Choice B) The fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine excludes evidence and testimony obtained from unconstitutional police actions. Here, since the police validly conducted a voice identification procedure and the defendant's constitutional rights were not otherwise violated, this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice C) The privilege against self-incrimination applies to compelled testimony (discloses the defendant's knowledge)—not compelled speech (discloses the characteristics of the defendant's voice). Since the defendant was compelled to disclose his vocal characteristics (not what he knew), the privilege against self-incrimination does not apply.

(Choice D) Police must give a suspect Miranda warnings (eg, suspect has the right to remain silent, any statement can be used against him/her at trial) when he/she is subject to a custodial interrogation. Here, though the defendant was lawfully arrested (custody), the purpose of the lineup was to identify his voice—not to elicit an incriminating statement (no interrogation). Therefore, Miranda warnings were not required.

📌 Educational Objective

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects a suspect from being compelled to provide incriminating testimonial communications, but not real or physical evidence.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • United States v. Wade, 388 U.S. 218, 222–23 (1967) (recognizing that voice identification is not a testimonial communication since it does not disclose the defendant's knowledge).
  • United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 35 (2000) ("[E]ven though the act may provide incriminating evidence, a criminal suspect may be compelled . . . to make a recording of his voice").
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因银行抢劫被合法逮捕，逮捕时没有逮捕令。他未被告知米兰达警告 (Miranda warnings)，但被立即带到警察局，在那里，他和其他五名男子被安排在一个阵容中，由抢劫案发生时当值的银行出纳员进行辨认。每名男子都被要求说出银行劫匪说过的话：“把所有的钱都给我。我有枪。”在阵容中的所有人都说了这些话之后，出纳员指认被告为劫匪。

被告随后动议排除该出纳员的证词，声称该阵容辨认侵犯了他反对自证其罪的特权。在排除证据的听证会上，该出纳员作证说，她没有看清劫匪的脸，因为劫匪戴着一顶帽子，帽子拉得很低，遮住了大半张脸，但她确定被告就是劫匪，因为她在阵容辨认中认出了他的声音。

被告的动议应被批准吗？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为在阵容中被要求说话，虽然是受强迫的，但并非证言性质或信息交流性质。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为基于第一手观察的证人证词，不适用作为“毒树之果”予以排除的规则。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为被告在阵容中被强迫说话，而这种强迫的言语导致了出纳员的指认证词。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为被告从未被告知他可以拒绝陈述，以及任何陈述都可能被用作对他不利的证据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / 5th Amendment
✅ 正确答案：A

动议不应被批准。虽然被告在列队辨认（Lineup）中被强迫说话，但这并不属于证言性质（Testimonial）或信息交流性质（Communicative）的证据。

核心考点：第五修正案的保护范围

第五修正案（5th Amendment）保护嫌疑人免受“自证其罪”（Self-Incrimination）。但MBE考试中最重要的区分在于：

受保护 (Privileged) 不受保护 (Not Privileged)
证言性质 (Testimonial) 实物/物理性质 (Physical/Real)
涉及思想、知识或信念的表达。 涉及身体特征的展示。
例如：审讯回答、日记、供词。 例如：声音样本、笔迹、指纹、DNA、试穿衣物。

在本案中，要求被告说出劫匪的话（"Give me all your money..."）并不是为了让他承认这句话的内容是他说的，而是为了展示其声音的物理特征供证人比对。因此，这被视为物理证据，不受第五修正案保护。

相关判例：United States v. Wade (1967)
最高法院裁定，强迫嫌疑人在列队辨认中说话以进行声音识别，并不侵犯其反对自证其罪的特权。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
  • 选项 B 错误：提到了“毒树之果”（Fruit of the Poisonous Tree）。由于警方的行为（不给 Warrant 逮捕、进行声音辨认）本身是合法的，没有“毒树”，自然没有“毒果”。
  • 选项 C 错误：虽然是被迫（Compelled）的，但第五修正案仅禁止“被强迫的证言”。如果只是被强迫展示身体特征（如声音），不构成违宪。
  • 选项 D 错误（常见陷阱）：关于 Miranda Warnings。

    Miranda 仅适用于“羁押讯问”（Custodial Interrogation）。

    虽然被告处于羁押状态（Custody），但列队辨认（Lineup）不是讯问（Interrogation）。讯问旨在引出供词，而列队辨认是收集物理证据的过程。因此，此时不需要 Miranda 警告，律师也不需要在场（除非是起诉后的列队辨认，但本题未提及已起诉）。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理第五修正案（Self-Incrimination）题目时，请使用“身体 vs. 大脑”测试：

  • 如果警察要的是嫌疑人的大脑内容（他在想什么、知道什么），则受保护。
  • 如果警察要的是嫌疑人的身体特征（声音、长相、血液、笔迹），则不受保护。

本题中，声音属于“身体”特征。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was indicted in a state court in January 2015 for a robbery and murder that occurred in December 2012. He retained counsel, who filed a motion to dismiss on the ground that the man had been prejudiced by a 25-month delay in obtaining the indictment. Thereafter, the man appeared in court with his counsel for arraignment and stated that he wished to plead guilty.
The presiding judge asked the man whether he understood the nature and essential elements of the charges, possible defenses, and maximum allowable sentences. The man replied that he did, and the judge reviewed all of those matters with him. He then asked the man whether he understood that he did not have to plead guilty. When the man responded that he knew that, the judge accepted the plea and sentenced him to 25 years.
Six months later, the man filed a motion to set aside his guilty plea on each of the following grounds.
Which of these grounds provides a constitutional basis for relief?

choices.A: The judge did not determine that the man had robbed and killed the victim.
choices.B: The judge did not determine whether the man understood that he had a right to jury trial.
choices.C: The judge did not determine whether the prosecutor's file contained any undisclosed exculpatory material.
choices.D: The judge did not rule on the man's motion to dismiss before accepting the guilty plea.

questions.explanation:
Due process requirements for guilty plea
Voluntary Defendant's free & deliberate choice
Knowing &
intelligent		 Defendant aware of:
  • nature & essential elements of offense
  • consequences of plea
  • waiver of constitutional right to:
    • plead not guilty & proceed to jury trial
    • remain silent
    • counsel (Sixth Amendment)
    • confront adverse witnesses
    • subpoena witness testimony (compulsory process)

Due process requires that a guilty plea be made (1) voluntarily—the product of the defendant's free and deliberate choice and (2) knowingly and intelligently—with sufficient awareness of the relevant circumstances and likely consequences of the plea. Therefore, before accepting a guilty plea, the trial judge must ensure (in open court and on the record) that the defendant is aware of the following:

  • the nature and essential elements of the charged offense
  • the maximum and any mandatory minimum sentence that can be imposed after a guilty plea and
  • the constitutional rights being waived—e.g., right to trial by jury.

If the judge fails to do so, the guilty plea is constitutionally invalid and should be set aside. The defendant is then entitled to plead anew (i.e., plead not guilty and stand trial).

Here, the man notified the judge that he wished to plead guilty. The judge then asked if the man understood the nature and essential elements of his charges, the maximum allowable sentence, and that he did not have to plead guilty. But since the judge failed to also determine if the man understood that he had a right to a jury trial—and that this constitutional right (and others) would be waived if he pled guilty—the plea was invalid and should be set aside.

(Choice A) A judge need not determine whether the defendant actually committed the charged crime before accepting his/her guilty plea.

(Choice C) The judge is not required to determine if the prosecutor's file contains undisclosed exculpatory material—i.e., evidence used to negate a defendant's guilt or mitigate punishment—before accepting a guilty plea. Additionally, the prosecution need only disclose such material before trial, not before a guilty plea.

(Choice D) The defendant is required to obtain a ruling on a motion before entering a guilty plea. If the defendant fails to do so (as seen here), the judge need not rule on the motion since it is considered waived. However, the defendant can reassert the motion if the guilty plea is set aside and he/she pleads not guilty.

📌 Educational Objective

Due process requires that guilty pleas be made (1) voluntarily—a free and deliberate choice and (2) knowingly and intelligently—with sufficient awareness of the nature and essential elements of the charged offense, the ranges of possible punishment, and the constitutional rights being waived.

📚 References
  • McCarthy v. United States, 394 U.S. 459, 466 (1969) (recognizing that a plea of guilty must be voluntary, knowing, and intelligent to comply with due process).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子于2015年1月因2012年12月发生的一起抢劫和谋杀案在州法院被起诉。他聘请了律师，律师以该男子因获得起诉书的25个月延误而受到不利影响为由，提出了驳回动议。此后，该男子与他的律师一同出庭接受提审，并表示希望作有罪答辩。

主审法官询问该男子是否理解指控的性质和基本要素、可能的抗辩理由以及最高可判处的刑期。该男子回答说他理解，法官便与他一起复核了所有这些事项。然后，法官问该男子是否明白他不必作有罪答辩。当该男子回答说他知道时，法官接受了该答辩，并判处他25年监禁。

六个月后，该男子基于以下各项理由，提出了撤销其有罪答辩的动议。

以下哪项理由为寻求救济提供了宪法依据？

zh-choices.A: 法官没有确定该男子是否抢劫并杀害了受害者。
zh-choices.B: 法官没有确定该男子是否理解他有权接受陪审团审判。
zh-choices.C: 法官没有确定检察官的案卷中是否包含任何未披露的脱罪材料。
zh-choices.D: 法官在接受有罪答辩之前，没有对该男子的驳回动议作出裁决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Constitutional Protection
⚖️ 核心考点：有罪答辩的正当程序要求

根据美国宪法正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause)，有罪答辩 (Guilty Plea) 必须是：

  • 自愿的 (Voluntary)
  • 知情的 (Knowing)
  • 明智的 (Intelligent)

法官必须在公开法庭记录 (on the record) 中确认被告人理解其正在放弃的三大宪法权利（源自 Boykin v. Alabama）：
1. 陪审团审判权 (Right to Jury Trial)
2. 与原告对质权 (Right to Confront Accusers)
3. 反对自证其罪的特权 (Privilege Against Self-Incrimination)

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 B)
理由：法官没有确定该男子是否理解他有权接受陪审团审判。

深度剖析：
有罪答辩本质上是对宪法权利的放弃 (Waiver)。为了使这种放弃在宪法上有效，记录必须明确显示被告人知晓他正在放弃哪些权利。

在本题中，法官虽然询问了指控性质、刑期和“不必认罪”的权利，但遗漏了关键的一项：明确告知被告人他拥有接受陪审团审判的权利 (Right to Jury Trial)。

如果法官未能确保被告人理解这一特定权利将被放弃，那么该答辩就不是“知情且明智的” (Knowing and Intelligent)，因此违反了正当程序，必须被撤销。

❌ 干扰项陷阱排除
选项 A (事实基础)：
虽然联邦规则 (Fed. R. Crim. P. 11) 要求确立事实基础，但从宪法角度看，只要答辩是自愿且明智的，法官无需确定被告人实际上实施了犯罪（参见 North Carolina v. Alford）。
选项 C (Brady 材料)：
最高法院在 United States v. Ruiz 中裁定，宪法不要求检察官在辩诉交易阶段披露弹劾证据 (Impeachment evidence) 或脱罪材料。这是审判权利，而非答辩权利。
选项 D (未决动议)：
无条件地进行有罪答辩通常会放弃 (Waive) 所有非管辖权性质的缺陷，包括未决的驳回动议。法官没有义务在接受答辩前先裁决该动议；答辩本身就使动议失效了。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

遇到 Guilty Plea 的题目，脑中要立刻浮现“法官的清单” (Judge's Colloquy Checklist)：

  1. 指控的性质 (Nature of charge)
  2. 最高刑期/强制最低刑 (Max/Min penalty)
  3. 放弃审判的权利 (Right to plead not guilty & have a trial)

如果题目中法官漏掉了上述任何一项（特别是权利的放弃），该答辩就是可撤销的。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was indicted and arrested for bank robbery. The defendant had an initial appearance before a magistrate judge in which he was notified of the charges and told that counsel would be appointed for him the next day. The police then required the defendant to participate with other prisoners in a lineup in which each person had to wear a white T-shirt and say, "Put your hands in the air." At the lineup, witnesses to the bank robbery identified the defendant as the bank robber. The next day, counsel was provided and the defendant was arraigned on the charges.
The defendant argues that his Sixth Amendment right to counsel was violated when he was denied counsel at two critical stages of the proceeding: his initial appearance in court before the magistrate judge and the lineup identification.
Was the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel violated?

choices.A: No.
choices.B: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the initial appearance.
choices.C: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the lineup.
choices.D: Yes, based on the denial of counsel at both stages of the proceeding.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel

(critical stages after prosecution has commenced)

  • Interrogations & lineups
  • Preliminary hearings & arraignments
  • Plea negotiations & hearings
  • Trial & sentencing
  • Appeals

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

• automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence (eg, indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

• guarantees that criminal defendants will have the assistance of counsel during all critical stages of prosecution—any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

An indictment is a judicial proceeding that triggers a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel. And a post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution because suggestive lineup procedures can lead to an unreliable and prejudicial identification. Since an attorney would have helped to ensure that the lineup was conducted fairly and protected the defendant's right to a fair trial, the denial of counsel violated his Sixth Amendment right.

In contrast, an initial appearance is not a critical stage if the judge merely conducts administrative tasks like notifying the defendant of the charges and explaining that an attorney will be appointed the next day. As a result, the defendant did not have a Sixth Amendment right to counsel during his initial appearance (Choices A, B & D). But had the defendant been required to make decisions that might adversely affect the outcome of his trial (eg, deciding whether to enter an affirmative defense), then his initial appearance would have been a critical stage.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once judicial proceedings begin and applies to all critical stages of prosecution. A critical stage is any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to assistance of counsel).
  • Rothgery v. Gillespie County, 554 U.S. 191, 198 (2008) (explaining that right to counsel attaches at commencement of judicial proceedings).
  • United States v. Wade, 388 U.S. 218, 237 (1967) (recognizing that post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因银行抢劫被起诉并逮捕。该被告在治安法官面前进行了首次出庭，在庭上他被告知了所控罪名，并被告知第二天将为他指定律师。随后，警方要求该被告与其他囚犯一起参加一个列队指认程序，其中每个人都必须穿白色T恤并说：“把手举起来。”在列队指认中，银行抢劫案的目击者指认该被告为银行劫匪。第二天，律师被提供给了被告，被告就这些指控被传讯。

被告辩称，由于他在两个关键诉讼阶段被拒绝提供律师，即在治安法官面前的首次出庭和列队指认，其第六修正案的律师权受到了侵犯。

被告的第六修正案律师权是否受到了侵犯？

zh-choices.A: 没有。
zh-choices.B: 是，但仅基于在首次出庭时被拒绝提供律师。
zh-choices.C: 是，但仅基于在列队指认时被拒绝提供律师。
zh-choices.D: 是，基于在这两个诉讼阶段均被拒绝提供律师。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Right to Counsel
⚖️ 第六修正案律师权 (Sixth Amendment)

分析律师权是否受侵犯，必须遵循两步走逻辑：

  1. 权利附着 (Attachment)： 对抗性司法程序（如起诉 Indictment）开始了吗？
  2. 关键阶段 (Critical Stage)： 这是一个没有律师在场就会导致不公的关键阶段吗？

本题中，被告已被起诉 (Indicted)，因此第六修正案权利已经附着。现在的核心问题是：题目中的两个事件是否属于“关键阶段”？

1. 首次出庭 (Initial Appearance) 未侵权

虽然权利已附着，但如果法官仅进行行政性告知（通知罪名、告知将指派律师），且被告未被要求进行任何可能损害其审判权利的决定（如抗辩 Plea），则此时不是关键阶段。

参考判例：Rothgery v. Gillespie County (2008) - 权利虽在此刻附着，但若无实质性损害，律师缺席不构成违宪。
2. 起诉后列队指认 (Post-indictment Lineup) 侵犯权利

起诉后的列队指认属于关键阶段。因为指认具有暗示性风险，律师在场可以监督程序的公平性，防止不可靠的指认成为审判证据。

注意：这里是被告亲自参与的列队指认（Corporeal lineup），而非照片指认（Photo array）。

参考判例：United States v. Wade (1967) - 起诉后的列队指认必须有律师在场。
💡 MBE 避坑指南

考生常混淆“权利附着”与“权利受侵犯”。

  • 附着 (Attachment)： 只要起诉或正式指控，权利就有了。
  • 侵犯 (Violation)： 只有在随后的“关键阶段”拒绝提供律师，才算侵犯。

本题中，首次出庭时权利已附着，但因其非关键阶段，故无侵犯；列队指认既在附着后，又是关键阶段，故构成侵犯。

✅ 正确答案：C (仅基于列队指认)

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Without a warrant, police officers searched the garbage cans in the alley behind a man's house and discovered chemicals used to make methamphetamine, as well as cooking utensils and containers with the man's fingerprints on them. The alley was a public thoroughfare maintained by the city, and the garbage was picked up once a week by a private sanitation company. The items were found inside the garbage cans in plastic bags that had been tied closed and further secured with tape. The man was charged in federal court with the manufacture of methamphetamine.
Did the search of the garbage cans violate the Fourth Amendment?

choices.A: No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage left in the alley.
choices.B: No, because the probative value of the evidence outweighs the man's modest privacy claims in his garbage.
choices.C: Yes, because the alley was within the curtilage of the man's home and entry without a warrant was unconstitutional.
choices.D: Yes, because there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in one's secured garbage containers.

questions.explanation:
The Fourth Amendment is violated when the government conducts an unreasonable search or seizure—ie, when police act without a warrant and no exception applies. A Fourth Amendment search occurs if one of the following tests is met:

  • Physical trespass test – the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information (eg, an intrusion upon the curtilage—the area immediately surrounding and commonly associated with a person's dwelling).
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invaded a person's subjective expectation of privacy that society would find objectively reasonable.

In California v. Greenwood, the Supreme Court held that (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in items that are accessible or visible to anyone (including police). Therefore, police may freely inspect items left in a public area or exposed to the public.

Here, the officers did not conduct a search under the physical trespass test since the garbage cans were in a public thoroughfare located behind the man's house—not a constitutionally protected area (Choice C). Additionally, there was no search under the reasonable expectation of privacy test since the man had no objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage cans that were readily accessible in a public alley (Choice D). Therefore, the officers did not violate the Fourth Amendment when they rummaged through the garbage cans.

(Choice B) The probative value of the evidence sought (ie, its tendency to make a fact more or less probable) cannot justify a violation of the defendant's Fourth Amendment right to privacy—no matter how modest. Instead, probative value is used to determine whether the evidence is relevant and admissible at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

The government does not need a warrant to inspect items left in a public area or exposed to the public since (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in such items.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • California v. Greenwood, 486 U.S. 35, 40–41 (1988) (recognizing that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage placed on a public street).
questions.zh-question:
在没有搜查令的情况下，警察搜查了一名男子房屋后的小巷里的垃圾桶，发现了用于制造甲基苯丙胺的化学品，以及带有该男子指纹的炊具和容器。该小巷是由市政府维护的公共通道，垃圾每周由一家私营环卫公司收走一次。这些物品是在垃圾桶内的塑料袋中发现的，袋子被扎紧并用胶带进一步加固。该男子在联邦法院被控制造甲基苯丙胺。

对垃圾桶的搜查是否违反了第四修正案？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该男子对遗留在小巷里的垃圾没有合理的隐私期待。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为证据的证明价值超过了该男子对其垃圾的有限隐私主张。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为小巷位于该男子住宅的庭园范围内，无证进入是违宪的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为个人对已加固的垃圾容器存在合理的隐私期待。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A
否，因为该男子对遗留在小巷里的垃圾没有合理的隐私期待。

本题的核心考点是：第四修正案对被遗弃在公共区域等待收集的垃圾是否提供保护？

核心判例与规则
California v. Greenwood (1988)
美国最高法院在该案中确立了规则：一旦垃圾被放置在房屋外部（curtilage 之外）的公共区域（如路边或小巷）等待收集，原主对该垃圾便不再拥有“合理的隐私期待” (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。

根据第四修正案，搜查（Search）的定义基于 Katz 测试的两个分支：

  1. 主观期待：个人是否表现出了实际的隐私期待？（本题中男子将袋子扎紧并封口，表现了主观期待）。
  2. 客观合理性：社会是否认为这种期待是合理的？（关键点：法院认为不合理）。
隐私期待范围图解
住宅内部
(最高保护)
庭园范围
(部分保护)
公共小巷
(无保护)

▲ 垃圾一旦进入公共区域，即失去宪法保护

本题案情拆解
1
位置 (Location)：垃圾桶位于“公共通道”(public thoroughfare) 的小巷中。这通常不属于住宅的庭园范围 (Curtilage)。
2
第三方接触 (Third Party Access)：垃圾是留给私营环卫公司收走的。最高法院认为，当你将物品交给第三方（收垃圾的人）时，你已经承担了该物品可能被其他人（包括警察、拾荒者、动物）翻阅的风险。
3
加固措施无效：虽然袋子被扎紧并用胶带封住（试图保护隐私），但这并不能改变其位于公共区域且准备被“销毁/带走”的本质。因此，客观上不存在合理的隐私期待。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B 错误：“证据的证明价值” (Probative value) 永远不能用来事后证成搜查的合法性。宪法权利的衡量不基于证据是否有用，而基于搜查行为本身是否合理。
选项 C 错误：题目明确指出小巷是“由市政府维护的公共通道”。这不属于庭园范围 (Curtilage)。即使在庭园边缘，如果是为了公共收集而放置，通常也不受保护。
选项 D 错误：这是最大的干扰项。虽然使用了不透明袋子和胶带（Opague bags and tape），但这仅代表主观意愿。在 Greenwood 案中，法院明确指出，不透明的塑料袋不足以在公共街道上建立第四修正案的保护。
MBE 解题技巧： 遇到“翻垃圾” (Trash Pull) 的题目，只要垃圾是在公共区域等待收集，警察就不需要搜查令。记住关键词：No Reasonable Expectation of Privacy (REP).

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
FBI agents, without a warrant and without the permission of foreign law enforcement or judicial officers, entered a foreign country, kidnapped a businessman—a U.S. citizen wanted in the United States for drug-smuggling violations—on the street, and forcibly drove him back to State A. Thereafter, the agents, again without a warrant, broke into the State A home of the businessman's girlfriend and arrested her.
The businessman and his girlfriend were both indicted for narcotics violations. Both moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment.
How should the court rule on their motions to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny both motions.
choices.B: Grant the businessman's motion but deny the girlfriend's motion.
choices.C: Grant the girlfriend's motion but deny the businessman's motion.
choices.D: Grant both motions.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for dismissing indictment
Deficient indictment
  • Fails to charge actual crime
  • Omits elements of crime
  • Statute of limitations has run
  • Improper venue or jurisdiction
Defective grand jury
proceedings
  • Admission of unqualified grand juror
  • Exclusion of grand juror based on race/gender
  • Prosecutorial misconduct
Constitutional violation
  • Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause
  • Sixth Amendment right to speedy trial
  • Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process clauses

An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a criminal offense after a finding of probable cause. It can be dismissed for (1) defective grand jury proceedings, (2) deficiencies in the indictment, or (3) violations of certain constitutional rights. Here, both defendants moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment. But since a Fourth Amendment violation is not a proper basis to dismiss an indictment, both motions should be denied (Choices B, C, & D).

And even if an indictment could be dismissed based on a Fourth Amendment violation, the businessman's arrest was proper. Police can lawfully arrest persons:

  • outside their home if police have probable cause to believe that they committed a felony or
  • inside their home if police have a valid warrant authorizing their arrest.

Here, FBI agents kidnapped the businessman in a foreign country and drove him back to State A to face charges for narcotics violations. This arrest was valid since (1) it occurred on the street (outside his home) and (2) the police had probable cause to believe that he had committed a felony (drug smuggling). And under the Ker/Frisbie doctrine, a defendant can be prosecuted in the United States even if he/she was forcibly abducted from another country without a warrant or the other country's permission. Therefore, the businessman was properly indicted.

In contrast, the girlfriend's arrest was invalid since (1) it occurred inside her State A home but (2) the police had no arrest warrant. And though the court will not dismiss the indictment on this basis, she can move to suppress any evidence discovered from that illegal arrest at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

An illegal Fourth Amendment arrest is not a valid basis to dismiss an indictment, but evidence obtained from an illegal arrest can be suppressed at trial.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Crews, 445 U.S. 463, 474 (1980) ("An illegal arrest, without more, has never been viewed as a bar to subsequent prosecution . . . .")
  • Ker v. Illinois, 119 U.S. 436, 444 (1886); Frisbie v. Collins, 342 U.S. 519, 522 (1952) (holding that a forcible abduction does not preclude prosecution).
questions.zh-question:
该商人和他的女友均因麻醉品犯罪被起诉。两人都以逮捕行为违反了Fourth Amendment为由，请求驳回起诉。

法院应如何裁定他们驳回起诉的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回两项动议。
zh-choices.B: 批准商人的动议，但驳回女友的动议。
zh-choices.C: 批准女友的动议，但驳回商人的动议。
zh-choices.D: 批准两项动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A (Deny both motions) 法院应驳回两人的动议。无论是商人的跨境绑架，还是女友的非法逮捕，都不能成为驳回起诉（Dismissal of Indictment）的理由。
核心考点：非法逮捕的后果

这是本题最大的陷阱。考生容易混淆“非法逮捕的后果”与“非法搜查的后果”。

  • 规则： 非法逮捕本身（Illegal Arrest）并不是驳回起诉（Indictment）的理由。
  • 救济措施： 如果逮捕违反了 Fourth Amendment，正确的救济措施是排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule)，即禁止在审判中使用因非法逮捕而获得的证据（如供述、搜出的物品）。
  • 结论： 即使逮捕完全非法，政府仍然可以将该被告带上法庭进行审判（只要有其他独立证据证明其有罪）。
United States v. Crews (1980)
最高法院明确指出："An illegal arrest, without more, has never been viewed as a bar to subsequent prosecution."（仅有非法逮捕这一事实，从未被视为阻止后续起诉的障碍。）
商人的情况：跨境绑架

对于被FBI从国外“绑架”回来的商人，适用著名的 Ker-Frisbie Doctrine。

即使被告是被强行绑架（forcible abduction）带入法院管辖区域的，法院依然拥有对该被告的对人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction)。

⚠️ 注意： 除非美国与该国签署的引渡条约中有明确条款规定“绑架即丧失管辖权”（这极其罕见），否则违反国际法或外国法律的绑架行为不影响美国法院的审判权。
女友的情况：无证入室逮捕

FBI在没有逮捕令的情况下闯入女友家中逮捕她，这确实违反了 Fourth Amendment（参见 Payton v. New York）。

  • 违宪点： 警方在住宅内逮捕嫌疑人通常需要逮捕令。
  • 后果： 逮捕是非法的。
  • 判决逻辑： 尽管逮捕非法，但如前所述，救济手段不是驳回起诉。她可以申请排除逮捕时获得的证据，但不能要求直接撤销案件。
💡 考试通关技巧

在 MBE 刑诉法题目中，当你看到被告提出 "Motion to Dismiss Indictment"（驳回起诉动议）时，请务必警惕：

  1. 大陪审团程序缺陷（如种族歧视）👉 可能驳回。
  2. 双重危险 (Double Jeopardy) 👉 可能驳回。
  3. 违反 Fourth Amendment (非法搜查/逮捕) 👉 绝不会驳回起诉，只能排除证据。

本题中，两人都试图用 Fourth Amendment 违宪来攻击 Indictment 本身，这在法律上是行不通的。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A man was in jail after being arrested for burglary. When the police attempted to question him, the man invoked his Miranda rights and refused to answer any questions. The man was subsequently tried, convicted, and sentenced to a prison term for the burglary. Three years later, while the man was serving his prison sentence for the burglary, a police detective from a nearby town questioned him about an unsolved homicide. The detective did not know that the man had invoked Miranda at an earlier time. The man waived his Miranda rights and made several incriminating statements to the detective. When he was later charged with the homicide, the man moved to suppress these statements, claiming that his earlier refusal to waive his Miranda rights should have been honored.
Should the court suppress the statements?

choices.A: No, because the detective was unaware that the man had originally invoked his Miranda rights.
choices.B: No, because the man's prior invocation of his Miranda rights did not preclude the later interrogation.
choices.C: Yes, because the man had earlier invoked his Miranda rights, and the police were not permitted to resume questioning, even after a time lapse of years.
choices.D: Yes, because the man was incarcerated, and his earlier invocation of his Miranda rights shielded him from further questioning until he was released.

Question

A motion to suppress should be granted if the defendant's statement was taken in violation of his/her Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. To comply with this privilege, police must give a suspect Miranda warnings (eg, the right to speak to an attorney) before conducting a custodial interrogation. If the suspect invokes his/her right to counsel, any custodial interrogation must stop until:

  • the suspect's attorney is present
  • the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the interrogation or
  • 14 days have passed since the suspect was released from police custody OR was no longer subject to coercive pressures associated with police custody (Choices C & D).

Here, the man invoked his Miranda right to counsel during a prior custodial interrogation, after which he was convicted and sent to prison (released from police custody). Three years later, a detective interrogated the man about a homicide. Since more than 14 days had passed since the man was released from police custody, the detective was free to question him after he waived his Miranda rights. Therefore, the man's motion to suppress should be denied.

(Choice A) An invocation of the right to counsel is valid against all police officers—including subsequent interrogators who are unaware of the invocation. Therefore, the court would not deny the man's motion to suppress merely because the detective did not know that the man had invoked his Miranda rights in a prior interrogation.

📌 Educational Objective

When a suspect invokes his/her Miranda right to counsel, all police interrogation must stop until (1) the suspect's attorney is present, (2) the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the questioning, or (3) fourteen days have passed since the suspect was released from custody or free of coercive pressures associated with police custody.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Arizona v. Roberson, 486 U.S. 675, 682–85 (1988) (recognizing that the invocation of Miranda rights extends to interrogations about other crimes).
  • Maryland v. Shatzer, 559 U.S. 98, 110 (2010) (holding that a break in the chain of custody ends Miranda protection).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因入室盗窃被捕后入狱。当警方试图审问他时，该男子援引其米兰达权利，拒绝回答任何问题。该男子随后因入室盗窃罪被审判、定罪并被判处有期徒刑。三年后，当该男子因入室盗窃罪服刑期间，一名来自邻近城镇的警探就一宗未决的凶杀案对他进行了审问。该警探并不知道该男子早前曾援引过米兰达权利。该男子放弃了他的米兰达权利，并向警探作出了几项对其不利的陈述。当他后来被指控犯有凶杀罪时，该男子动议排除这些陈述，声称他早前拒绝放弃米兰达权利的决定应得到尊重。

法院是否应该排除这些陈述？

zh-choices.A: 不应排除，因为警探不知道该男子最初曾援引其米兰达权利。
zh-choices.B: 不应排除，因为该男子先前援引其米兰达权利并不妨碍后来的审讯。
zh-choices.C: 应排除，因为该男子早前已援引其米兰达权利，即使时隔数年，警方也不得恢复审问。
zh-choices.D: 应排除，因为该男子被监禁，他早前援引米兰达权利保护他免于进一步审问，直到他被释放为止。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

米兰达权利的“有效期”与羁押中断

核心考点：羁押中断规则

本题考察的是美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中关于米兰达权利（Miranda Rights）援引后的时效性问题。

关键判例：Maryland v. Shatzer (2010)

根据 Edwards v. Arizona 确立的规则，一旦嫌疑人援引了律师帮助权（Right to Counsel），警方必须停止审讯，直到律师在场。

但是，Shatzer 案确立了一个重要的例外：

如果嫌疑人经历了“羁押中断” (Break in Custody)，且时间超过 14天，警方可以重新接触嫌疑人，再次宣读米兰达警告并寻求放弃权利（Waiver）。

案情分析与正确答案

在本案中：

  • 第一次审讯：嫌疑人援引了米兰达权利。
  • 中间过程：嫌疑人被定罪并入狱服刑，时间过去了三年。
  • 第二次审讯：新的警探重新宣读权利，嫌疑人放弃权利并招供。

关键点监狱服刑算不算“羁押”？

最高法院在 Shatzer 案中裁定，回到普通监狱人口（General Prison Population）服刑，被视为米兰达语境下的“羁押中断”。因为在普通监狱生活中，嫌疑人已经习惯了环境，不再受到当初被捕时那种高强度的、旨在迫使招供的强制性压力（Coercive Pressure）。

结论：

由于时间间隔（3年）远超 14 天，且嫌疑人已处于服刑状态（视为羁押中断），之前的米兰达援引已经失效。警方可以重新审讯。

正确答案是 B。

不应排除证据，因为先前的援引并不永久禁止后续的审讯。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (错误)：警探不知情

这是一个常见的陷阱。根据 Arizona v. Roberson，米兰达权利的援引对所有执法人员有效。警方的知识是“推定的”（Imputed Knowledge）。如果还在 14 天保护期内，即使第二个警探真的不知道，审讯也是违法的。本题的关键在于时间间隔，而不是警探的主观知情状态。

选项 C (错误)：永久禁止

米兰达权利的援引并不是永久的“护身符”。Shatzer 案明确拒绝了这种永久性的保护，设立了 14 天的界限。

选项 D (错误)：监禁即羁押

虽然嫌疑人在物理上被“监禁”（Incarcerated），但在米兰达法律分析中，已判刑的囚犯在普通监区的生活不被视为 Miranda 意义上的“羁押性审讯环境”（Custodial Interrogation Context）。因此，他在监狱里的这段时间构成了“羁押中断”。

💡 考试技巧

在 MBE 刑法题中，当你看到：

  1. 嫌疑人援引权利（我要律师）；
  2. 警方停止审讯；
  3. 释放 或 回到监狱普通监区；
  4. 时间流逝（注意 14天 这个数字）；

一定要立刻联想到 14-Day Rule (Maryland v. Shatzer)。只要超过14天，警方就可以“重启”游戏。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman who is a computer expert decided to dedicate herself to exposing persons who trafficked in child pornography. She posted a number of sexually oriented photographs on her website. The file for each photograph contained an embedded Trojan horse program (a program that would allow the woman to enter the computer of anyone who downloaded the photograph). A man downloaded one of those photographs onto his personal computer. Using the embedded program, the woman entered the man's computer and found a file containing a pornographic photograph of a child. She copied the file and turned it over to a federal law enforcement agency. A federal agent told her that a successful prosecution would require more than one photograph and offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman entered the man's computer again, and this time she found hundreds of child pornography photographs, which she turned over to the federal agency.
The man was charged with multiple counts of violating federal child pornography statutes. He has moved to suppress the photographs that the woman discovered on his computer. The motion is based on both the Fourth Amendment and a federal statute forbidding interception of electronic communication without permission. The parties have stipulated that the woman's conduct in downloading photographs from the man's computer violated the interception statute.
How should the court rule on the defendant's motion to suppress?

choices.A: Deny the motion as to all photographs.
choices.B: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman acted without probable cause.
choices.C: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman violated the federal interception statute.
choices.D: Grant the motion only as to the second set of photographs.

    government’s behalf

Violation

The exclusionary rule requires the suppression of evidence obtained in violation of the law or a defendant's constitutional rights (eg, from a warrantless search). Since this rule seeks to deter government misconduct, it only applies to the actions of government agents (eg, government employees, persons working on the government's behalf). Therefore, evidence is admissible if it was obtained by a private individual acting on his/her own behalf, without the government's knowledge or participation (eg, concerned citizens, vigilantes).

Here, the woman used an embedded Trojan horse program to conduct two searches of the man's computer. During the first search, the woman discovered a child pornography photograph. Since that search was motivated by her personal desire to expose persons who trafficked in child pornography, she was acting as a private individual without the government's knowledge or participation. Therefore, the exclusionary rule does not apply, and the court should deny the man's motion to suppress the first photograph.

Once the woman gave that photograph to the federal law enforcement agency, a federal agent offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman then conducted a second search of the man's computer on the agency's behalf. Therefore, she was acting as a government agent during that search. And since the search violated the Fourth Amendment (no warrant) and the federal interception statute, the court should grant the man's motion to suppress the second set of photographs (Choice D).

(Choice A) Government agents generally need a warrant based on probable cause to conduct a Fourth Amendment search, but private individuals do not. Therefore, the fact that the woman acted without probable cause would only support the suppression of photographs obtained during her second (government) search—not her first (private) search.

(Choice B) Government agents generally need a warrant based on probable cause to conduct a Fourth Amendment search, but private individuals do not. Therefore, the fact that the woman acted without probable cause would only support the suppression of photographs obtained during her second (government) search—not her first (private) search.

(Choice C) Although the parties stipulated that the woman's conduct violated the federal interception statute, that stipulation only supports the exclusion of the second set of photographs (government search).

📌 Educational Objective

The exclusionary rule requires suppression of evidence that was illegally or unconstitutionally obtained by government agents—not private individuals acting without the government's knowledge or participation.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Jacobsen, 466 U.S. 109, 113 (1984) (finding that the Fourth Amendment applies to searches conducted by the government and individuals working on its behalf, but not private individuals).
  • Nardone v. United States, 308 U.S. 338, 340–41 (1939) (explaining that evidence obtained in violation of a federal statute is subject to the exclusionary rule).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性计算机专家决定致力于揭露贩卖儿童色情制品的人。她在自己的网站上发布了多张性导向的照片。每张照片的文件都含有一个嵌入的木马程序（一种允许该女子进入任何下载该照片者电脑的程序）。一名男子将其中一张照片下载到了他的个人电脑上。利用这个嵌入的程序，该女子进入了该男子的电脑，并发现了一个包含儿童色情照片的文件。她复制了该文件并将其交给了联邦执法机构。一名联邦探员告诉她，成功的起诉需要不止一张照片，并向她提供了金钱奖励，以换取能导致该男子定罪的更多照片。该女子再次进入该男子的电脑，这一次她发现了数百张儿童色情照片，并将它们交给了联邦机构。

该男子被控多项违反联邦儿童色情法规的罪名。他已提出动议，要求排除（suppress）该女子在其电脑上发现的照片作为证据。该动议的依据是《Fourth Amendment》和一项禁止未经许可（permission）截取电子通信的联邦法规。双方当事人已约定（stipulated），该女子从该男子电脑下载照片的行为违反了该截取法规。

法院应如何裁定被告的排除证据动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回针对所有照片的动议。
zh-choices.B: 批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子在没有“合理理由”（probable cause）的情况下行事。
zh-choices.C: 批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子违反了联邦截取法规。
zh-choices.D: 仅批准针对第二组照片的动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：第四修正案与私人搜查

本题考察的核心是美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）的适用范围，特别是“政府行为”（State Action）与“私人行为”（Private Action）的界限。

核心原则：
第四修正案仅保护公民免受政府（Government）的不合理搜查和扣押。它不适用于私人（Private Individual）的行为，除非该私人是作为政府的代理人或工具行事。

案情两阶段分析

要正确回答此题，必须将该女子的行为分为两个独立的时间段进行分析：

第一阶段：私人搜查
行为：女子出于个人意愿（揭露色情贩子），利用木马程序搜查并发现第一张照片。
法律定性：这是纯粹的私人行为。政府并未参与、不知情，也未鼓励。
结果：证据可采 (Admissible)。
即使该行为违反了截取法规，但由于不是政府行为，宪法排除规则不适用。
第二阶段：政府代理
行为：联邦探员提供金钱奖励（Reward），要求更多证据。女子为了奖励再次搜查。
法律定性：此时身份发生了质的转变。由于政府的鼓励（金钱诱惑）和具体指示，她已成为政府探员（Government Agent）。
结果：证据排除 (Suppressed)。
作为政府代理人，她没有搜查令（Warrant），且违反了截取法规，因此触发证据排除法则。

判决逻辑 (Rationale)

法院应仅批准针对第二组照片的动议（选项 D）。

  • 针对第一组照片：虽然违反了联邦法规，但证据排除法则（Exclusionary Rule）旨在威慑警察的不当行为，不适用于私人。因此，第一张照片可以作为证据。
  • 针对第二组照片：女子已变身为政府工具（Instrument of the state）。政府不能通过利用私人来规避第四修正案对搜查令的要求。因此，第二组照片是非法搜查所得，必须排除。
💡
MBE 考试技巧：
在涉及搜查（Search）的题目中，首先问自己：“这是谁干的？”
  • 如果是警察 → 检查是否有 Warrant 或例外情况。
  • 如果是普通公民 → 检查政府是否在背后“指使”或“参与”。
一旦政府介入（提供奖励、指示、协助），私人行为即转化为政府行为（State Action）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A federal grand jury that was investigating drug trafficking in the jurisdiction subpoenaed a witness to testify. The prosecutor advised the witness that he had a Fifth Amendment privilege not to testify if he so chose. The witness asked that his attorney be allowed to advise him inside the grand jury room, but the prosecutor refused to allow the attorney inside. After speaking with his attorney outside the grand jury room, the witness decided to testify. During his testimony, he made self-incriminating statements.
The witness was subsequently indicted for drug crimes. The indictment was based on the witness's grand jury testimony and on evidence seized in an unconstitutional search of the witness's home.
The witness has moved to dismiss the indictment.
Should the court dismiss the indictment?

choices.A: No, because the witness had no right to counsel inside the grand jury room and the illegally seized evidence did not affect the validity of the indictment.
choices.B: No, because the witness waived his constitutional rights by testifying.
choices.C: Yes, because the indictment was based upon illegally seized evidence.
choices.D: Yes, because the witness was denied his constitutional right to advice of counsel.

questions.explanation:
Rights & privileges that may be invoked at grand jury proceedings
Constitutional
rights
  • Privilege against self-incrimination (Fifth Amendment)
  • Equal protection (Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment)
  • Congressmen's privilege not to be questioned about legislative activities (speech or debate clause)
Privileges
  • Attorney-client privilege
  • Spousal privilege
  • Marital communications privilege
  • Psychotherapist-patient privilege

An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a crime after a finding of probable cause. But since a grand jury only has the investigatory power to indict (not the judicial power to convict), a witness may only invoke certain constitutional rights during grand jury proceedings.

A witness may consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room (as seen here). But since a witness has no Sixth Amendment right to have counsel inside the grand jury room, the prosecutor had the right to refuse the witness's request to have his attorney inside. Therefore, the witness's self-incriminating testimony before the grand jury did not violate the Sixth Amendment, and the subsequent indictment should not be dismissed on this basis (Choice D).

The indictment was also based on evidence seized during an unconstitutional Fourth Amendment search of the witness's home. Pursuant to the exclusionary rule, illegally seized evidence should be suppressed at trial to discourage unconstitutional police conduct. However, the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings since the grand jury is an investigatory body—not a judicial one. Therefore, the illegally seized evidence does not affect the validity of the indictment, and it should not be dismissed (Choice C).

(Choice B) Though the witness waived his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination by testifying, he did not waive his Fourth or Sixth Amendment rights because they do not apply during grand jury proceedings. And since witnesses can only waive rights they possess, this is not a basis to deny the motion.

📌 Educational Objective

Since grand jury proceedings are investigatory in nature, only certain constitutional protections apply. A grand jury witness can consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room but has no Sixth Amendment right to counsel inside that room. And the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • United States v. Mandujano, 425 U.S. 564, 581 (1976) (finding that a witness has no right to counsel inside the grand jury room).
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351–52 (1974) (holding that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).
questions.zh-question:
一个正在调查该司法管辖区内毒品贩运的联邦大陪审团传唤了一名证人作证。检察官告知该证人，如果他选择不作证，他拥有 Fifth Amendment 规定的不作证特权。该证人请求允许其律师在大陪审团室内为他提供建议，但检察官拒绝让律师进入。在与律师在大陪审团室外商谈后，该证人决定作证。在他的证词中，他做出了自证其罪的陈述。

该证人随后因毒品犯罪被起诉。该起诉是基于该证人向大陪审团提供的证词，以及通过对证人住宅的违宪搜查所扣押的证据。

该证人已动议驳回该起诉。

法院应否驳回该起诉？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为证人在大陪审团室内没有获得律师帮助的权利，且非法扣押的证据不影响起诉的有效性。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为证人通过作证放弃了他的宪法权利。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为该起诉是基于非法扣押的证据。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为证人被剥夺了其获得律师建议的宪法权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：大陪审团程序的特殊性

本题考察的是美国刑事诉讼法中关于大陪审团（Grand Jury）程序的两个核心考点：律师协助权的范围和证据排除规则的适用性。

正确答案：A

法院不应驳回起诉，因为证人在大陪审团室内无权要求律师在场，且非法获取的证据不影响起诉书的有效性。

核心考点一：证据排除规则不适用

规则：证据排除规则（Exclusionary Rule）通常禁止在刑事审判（Trial）中使用违反第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）获取的证据。但是，这一规则不适用于大陪审团程序。

法律依据：
大陪审团是一个调查机构（Investigatory Body），而非裁决机构。最高法院在 United States v. Calandra (1974) 中裁定，允许大陪审团使用非法搜查获得的证据，因为将排除规则延伸至此会阻碍大陪审团的调查职能。

结论：即使起诉书（Indictment）部分基于非法搜查获得的证据，该起诉书仍然有效。因此，选项 C 错误。

核心考点二：大陪审团室内的律师权

规则：虽然证人有权在作证间隙走出房间咨询律师，但第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）的律师协助权并不延伸至大陪审团室内部。

  • Outside: 证人可以离开房间咨询律师。
  • Inside: 律师不能进入大陪审团室陪伴证人。

法律依据：
在 United States v. Mandujano (1976) 中，法院确认证人没有宪法权利要求律师在大陪审团室内在场。

结论：检察官拒绝律师进入房间并未侵犯证人的宪法权利。因此，选项 D 错误。

其他选项分析

  • 选项 B (错误)： 虽然证人作证确实放弃了第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）的反对自证其罪特权，但这并不是法院拒绝驳回起诉的主要理由。法院拒绝驳回是因为起诉本身的程序和依据在法律上是允许的（即没有违反律师权，且可以使用非法证据）。

🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理涉及 Grand Jury 的 MBE 题目时，请记住它是“低保护区”：

  1. 证据规则宽松：可以使用传闻证据（Hearsay）和非法搜查得来的证据。
  2. 律师限制：律师只能在门外等候，不能进屋。
  3. 目的不同：它的目的是决定是否有“合理根据”（Probable Cause）起诉，而不是判定有罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police officers received a report that someone had been murdered. Upon arriving at the scene, a police detective interviewed the only eyewitness to the event. The detective's report, which was delivered to the prosecutor, stated that the eyewitness could not identify the perpetrator of the crime.
A man was subsequently charged with murder. His attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all evidence favorable to the defense. The prosecutor substantially complied with the request but inadvertently failed to disclose the detective's report. At trial, the eyewitness identified the man as the murderer.
The man's attorney learned of the report after the man was convicted. On appeal, the man's attorney argued that the prosecutor's failure to turn over the detective's report violated the man's constitutional rights. He further argued that there was a reasonable probability of a different outcome had the report been disclosed to the defense.
Should the appellate court reverse the man's conviction?

choices.A: No, because the evidence impeached the eyewitness's testimony but did not exonerate the man.
choices.B: No, because the prosecutor did not intentionally withhold the detective's report.
choices.C: Yes, because the man was prejudiced by the prosecutor's failure to disclose the detective's report.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all favorable evidence.
