In Brady v. Maryland, the Supreme Court held that a defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose evidence that is both:

  • favorable to the defendant – evidence used to negate a defendant's guilt or mitigate punishment (exculpatory evidence) or to discredit the prosecution's witness (impeachment evidence) and
  • material to guilt or punishment – there is a reasonable probability that, had the evidence been disclosed, the result of the proceeding would have been different.

Here, the prosecutor failed to turn over the detective's report, which stated that the sole eyewitness could not identify the perpetrator of the crime. This report was favorable to the man because it contradicted the eyewitness's in-court identification of the man. It was also material to the man's guilt because there was a reasonable probability that the result of the proceeding would have been different had the detective's report been disclosed. Because the man was prejudiced by the failure to disclose the report, the appellate court should reverse his conviction.

(Choice A) Evidence must be favorable and material to—but need not exonerate—the defendant to trigger the prosecution's duty to disclose. Here, the undisclosed report could have been used to impeach the eyewitness, and if it had, there is a reasonable probability that the man would have been acquitted. Therefore, the man's due process rights were violated.

(Choice B) Whether the prosecution intentionally withheld favorable and material evidence is irrelevant. What matters is whether the prosecutor's conduct (intentional or not) prejudiced the defendant.

(Choice D) Prosecutors have an affirmative duty to disclose favorable and material evidence to the defense—even if the defendant does not request it.

📌 Educational Objective

In Brady v. Maryland, the Supreme Court held that a defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose evidence that is both (1) favorable to the defendant and (2) material to guilt or punishment.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (due process clause as applicable to states).
  • Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83, 87 (1963) (recognizing that prosecution's withholding of favorable and material evidence violated due process).
  • United States v. Bagley, 473 U.S. 667, 682 (1985) (discussing when a failure to disclose evidence favorable to the defendant is material).
questions.zh-question: 警方接到报案称有人被谋杀。抵达现场后，一名警探采访了事件的唯一目击者。警探的报告（已提交给检察官）指出，目击者无法辨认犯罪嫌疑人。随后，一名男子被控谋杀。他的律师要求控方交出所有有利于辩方的证据。检察官基本遵守了该请求，但无意中未能披露警探的报告。庭审中，目击者指认该男子为凶手。该男子被定罪后，其律师才得知该报告。在上诉中，该男子的律师辩称，检察官未能交出警探报告侵犯了该男子的宪法权利。他进一步辩称，如果该报告已向辩方披露，则案件结果很可能不同。上诉法院是否应撤销该男子的定罪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该证据削弱了目击者的证词，但并未宣告该男子无罪。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为检察官并非故意隐瞒警探的报告。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为检察官未能披露警探报告对该男子造成了损害。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该男子的律师曾要求控方交出所有有利证据。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A 17-year-old high school student decided to rob a convenience store. The student entered the store, brandished a pistol, and threatened to shoot the clerk unless she placed the contents of the cash register into a bag. After the clerk emptied the cash register, the student ordered her to lie on the floor and count to 500. To discourage the clerk from moving, the student fired the pistol at the floor immediately beside the clerk. The bullet ricocheted off the floor and struck the clerk in the head, killing her.
The student is now 18 years old and on trial for felony murder.
Can the state constitutionally seek the death penalty?

choices.A: No, because the death penalty cannot be imposed in felony-murder cases.
choices.B: No, because the student was under 18 years of age when he committed the crime.
choices.C: Yes, because the homicide occurred during the commission of an inherently dangerous felony.
choices.D: Yes, because the punishment is not disproportionately excessive in relation to the crime committed.

questions.explanation:
Eighth Amendment cruel & unusual punishment
  • No death penalty for:
    • juveniles
    • intellectually deficient persons
    • adults convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No mandatory life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of homicide

The Eighth Amendment prohibits the imposition of cruel and unusual punishments, including punishments that are inherently barbaric (e.g., torture) or disproportionate to the crime. It also prohibits imposing a death sentence on a defendant who was younger than 18 years of age when the crime was committed.

Here, the student is currently 18 years old, but he was 17 years old when the felony murder was committed. Therefore, the state cannot constitutionally seek the death penalty.

(Choices A and C) Felony murder is an unintended killing proximately caused by and during the commission or attempted commission of an inherently dangerous felony. If a felony-murder defendant is over 18 years of age, then the death penalty can generally be imposed so long as the defendant was not acting as an accomplice and did not kill, attempt to kill, or intend to kill the victim (not seen here).

(Choice D) The Eighth Amendment bars punishments that are so disproportionate to the offense as to shock the moral sense of the community. In Roper v. Simmons, the U.S. Supreme Court determined that imposing the death penalty for any crime committed by a defendant who was under 18 years of age meets this criteria. Thus, the state cannot seek the death penalty against the defendant here.

📌 Educational Objective

The Eighth Amendment's prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment forbids imposing a death sentence on a defendant who was under 18 years of age when the crime was committed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VIII (prohibiting cruel and unusual punishment).
  • Roper v. Simmons, 543 U.S. 551, 578 (2005) (holding that the death penalty cannot be imposed on a defendant who was a juvenile under eighteen when the crime was committed).
questions.zh-question:
一名17岁的高中生决定抢劫一家便利店。该学生进入商店，挥舞手枪，并威胁店员，除非她将收银机里的钱放入袋中，否则就开枪。店员清空收银机后，学生命令她躺在地板上数到500。为阻止店员移动，学生朝店员身旁的地板开了一枪。子弹从地板反弹，击中店员头部，致其死亡。
该学生现年18岁，正因重罪谋杀（felony murder）受审。
州能否在宪法上寻求判处死刑？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为在重罪谋杀（felony-murder）案件中不能判处死刑。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为该学生在犯罪时未满18岁。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为该杀人行为发生在一个本质危险的重罪（inherently dangerous felony）实施过程中。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该惩罚与所犯罪行相比并非不成比例地过重。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man decided to rob a grocery store. During the robbery, he held a store clerk at gunpoint and hit the clerk in the face with the gun before fleeing the store. The police located the store clerk in the hospital the following day. While at the store clerk's bedside, the police officers presented a photo array of possible suspects to the store clerk and went through each photo without making any statements or gestures to him. The store clerk identified the man as the robber, and the man was subsequently arrested. Immediately after his arrest, the man was informed of his Miranda rights. He immediately invoked his right to counsel.
The man has been formally charged with armed robbery. Before trial, the man's attorney filed a motion to exclude the store clerk's identification.
How should the court rule?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the man had not been formally charged when the identification was made.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because there is no right to counsel at a photo array.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the man did not have the opportunity to select or object to the photos in advance.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the man invoked his right to counsel.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel
Critical
stages
  • Post-indictment: lineups, in-person identifications, interrogations
  • Arraignments, preliminary hearings, bail hearings, pretrial motions
  • Plea negotiations & hearings
  • Trial & sentencing
Noncritical
stages
  • Pre-charge lineups
  • Photo-array identification
  • Fingerprinting, handwriting & voice exemplars, blood samples
  • Initial appearances, hearings to determine probable cause to detain defendant
  • Discretionary appeals
  • Post-conviction proceedings (eg, parole or probation hearing)

The right to counsel arises under the Fifth Amendment and the Sixth Amendment. The Fifth Amendment right to counsel arises when (1) a suspect is subject to a custodial interrogation and (2) the suspect makes a specific, unambiguous statement asserting his desire to have counsel present. Here, the man is challenging the store clerk's identification—not an interrogation of the man. Therefore, the Fifth Amendment right to counsel does not apply.

In contrast, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

• automatically attaches once formal judicial proceedings commence (e.g., indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

• applies during all critical stages of prosecution (i.e., any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial).

However, a photo array is not considered a "critical stage of prosecution" to which the Sixth Amendment right to counsel applies (even if the Fifth Amendment right to counsel is invoked). Therefore, the fact that the identification was made before the man was formally charged does not affect its admissibility (Choices A and D). Accordingly, the man had no right to counsel at the photo array.

(Choice C) The defense has no right to select or object to photos in a photo array before a witness sees it.

📌 Educational Objective

A suspect has no right to have his counsel present when a witness is shown a photo array that includes the suspect, regardless of when the photo array is conducted.

📚 References
  • United States v. Ash, 413 U.S. 300, 321 (1973) (holding that the Sixth Amendment does not require that defense counsel be present when a witness views police or prosecution photo arrays).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定抢劫一家杂货店。抢劫过程中，他用枪指着一名店员，并在逃离商店前用枪打了店员的脸。次日，警方在医院找到了该店员。在店员床边，警官向店员展示了一组嫌疑人照片（photo array），并逐一查看每张照片，期间没有对店员发表任何言论或做出任何手势。店员指认该男子为抢劫犯，该男子随后被捕。逮捕后，该男子立即被告知其米兰达权利（Miranda rights）。他立即援引了其律师权（right to counsel）。
该男子已被正式指控武装抢劫。庭审前，该男子的律师提交了一份动议，要求排除店员的指认（identification）。
法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为在指认发生时，该男子尚未被正式指控。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为在照片指认（photo array）中没有律师权（right to counsel）。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为该男子没有机会事先选择或反对这些照片。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为该男子援引了其律师权（right to counsel）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was arrested and charged with arson. The indictment alleges that the man committed the crime three years ago. The defense has learned that the prosecutor had enough evidence to prosecute the man several months after the arson but made a good-faith decision to delay bringing charges to investigate whether others were involved in the crime. The man contends that the delay has prejudiced his defense because a friend who could have provided the man with an alibi has recently died.
The applicable jurisdiction does not have a statute of limitations regarding arson.
Has the prosecutor's delay violated the man's constitutional rights?

choices.A: No, because the Constitution does not protect a defendant from pre-accusation delay.
choices.B: No, because the delay was attributable to the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime.
choices.C: Yes, because the delay violated the man's right to a speedy trial under the Sixth Amendment.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's case was prejudiced by the delay.

questions.explanation:
The due process clause, along with state and federal statutes of limitations, protects criminal defendants from intentional and prejudicial pre-accusation delay. The defendant's due process rights may have been violated if a delay was used to obtain a tactical advantage for the prosecution or to harass the defendant. But there is no due process violation when delay results from an investigation conducted in good faith.

Here, the man was indicted for arson three years after the crime occurred. The man argued that this delay prejudiced his defense because an alibi witness has since died. However, the delay resulted from the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime—not from an attempt to gain a tactical advantage or harass the defendant. Therefore, the prosecutor's delay did not violate the man's constitutional rights.

(Choice A) The Constitution, by virtue of the due process clause, does protect defendants from pre-accusation delay.

(Choice B) The delay was attributable to the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime.

(Choice C) The Sixth Amendment right to a speedy trial protects defendants from post-accusation delay. Here, the man experienced a pre-accusation delay, so his Sixth Amendment rights were not violated.

(Choice D) Prejudice suffered by a defendant from a pre-accusation delay is one element of establishing a due process violation, but there must also be a showing that the prosecutor's delay was made in bad faith.

📌 Educational Objective

The due process clause protects defendants from intentional and prejudicial pre-accusation delay. However, delay due to an investigation conducted in good faith does not violate a defendant's due process rights.

📚 References
  • United States v. Lovasco, 431 U.S. 783 (1977) (holding that a pre-accusation delay does not violate a defendant's due process rights if the delay is the result of a good-faith investigation).
questions.zh-question: 一个男人因纵火罪被捕并被起诉。起诉书指控该男子在三年前犯下了此罪。辩方了解到，检察官在纵火案发生几个月后就有足够的证据起诉该男子，但出于善意决定延迟提起指控，以调查是否有其他人参与了该罪行。该男子声称，延迟损害了他的辩护，因为一位本可以为他提供不在场证明的朋友最近去世了。适用司法管辖区对纵火罪没有诉讼时效。检察官的延迟是否侵犯了该男子的宪法权利？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为宪法不保护被告免受起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）的影响。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为延迟是由于检察机关对犯罪的善意调查造成的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为延迟侵犯了该男子根据第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）享有的快速审判权（speedy trial）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该男子的案件因延迟而受到损害。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was tried for armed robbery. The state introduced evidence that a man, identified by witnesses as the defendant, entered a convenience store at 11:00 p.m. on March 5, threatened the clerk with a gun, and took $75 from the cash register.
The defendant did not testify, but his sister did. She testified that on March 5, at the time of the robbery, the defendant was with her in a city 300 miles away. On cross-examination, the sister admitted having given a statement to the police in which she had said that the defendant was not with her on March 5, but she claimed that the earlier statement was mistaken.
The court instructed the jurors that in order to convict the defendant, they had to find all of the elements of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt.
As to the defendant's claim of alibi, which of the following additional instructions would be proper?

choices.A: Alibi is a matter of defense and so must be established by the defendant; however, the burden of persuasion is by a preponderance of the evidence, not beyond a reasonable doubt.
choices.B: Before you may consider the defendant's claim of alibi, you must decide whether he has produced sufficient evidence to raise the issue.
choices.C: If the defendant's evidence has caused you to have a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, you must find him not guilty.
choices.D: If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty.

questions.explanation:
Criminal defenses:  burdens & standards of proof
Negation
defense
  • Challenges element of crime (eg, alibi, lack of intent)
  • Fifth Amendment assigns burden to prosecution to prove element beyond a reasonable doubt
Affirmative
defense
  • Justifies or excuses criminal conduct, but does not challenge element of crime (eg, entrapment, self-defense, duress)
  • Statute assigns burden (prosecution or defense) & standard of proof (eg, preponderance, clear & convincing, beyond a reasonable doubt)

Due process requires that the prosecution prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, when a defendant asserts a defense that negates an element of the crime (eg, an alibi defense), the prosecution bears the burden of proof—not the defendant. However, the prosecution is not required to disprove an affirmative defense (eg, self-defense, duress) since it justifies or excuses the defendant's criminal conduct but does not negate an element of the crime.

Here, the defendant was on trial for armed robbery, which requires proof that he was at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5. Since the defendant's sister testified that he was with her 300 miles away when the crime occurred, her alibi testimony challenges an element of the crime that the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the trial court should instruct the jury that if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was at the convenience store, it must find him not guilty.

(Choice A) The burden of proof can be placed on the defendant only for affirmative defenses—not for defenses that challenge an element of the criminal offense (eg, alibi, lack of intent). Additionally, any level of proof can be imposed—eg, preponderance of the evidence, clear and convincing evidence, beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice B) A defendant must produce sufficient evidence to raise an affirmative defense, but not to raise an alibi defense since it negates an element of the charged crime. Instead, the prosecution must produce sufficient evidence to establish all elements of the criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice C) Although the jury must find the defendant not guilty if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, this jury instruction wrongfully places the burden of proof for an element of the crime on the defendant.

📌 Educational Objective

The prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the prosecution bears the burden of proof when a defendant raises a defense that challenges an element of the offense.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause).
  • In re Winship, 397 U.S. 358, 364 (1970) (stating that the prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因持械抢劫罪受审。控方（州政府）出示证据，证明一名被证人指认为被告的男子，于3月5日晚11时进入一家便利店，用枪威胁店员，并从收银机中取走75美元。

被告没有作证，但他的姐姐作证了。她作证称，在3月5日抢劫案发生时，被告正和她在一起，身处300英里外的一座城市。在交叉询问中，姐姐承认曾向警方提供过一份陈述，其中她称被告在3月5日并未与她在一起，但她声称之前的陈述是错误的。

法庭指示陪审员，若要裁定被告有罪，他们必须毫无合理疑点地认定犯罪的所有要素。

关于被告的不在场证明主张，以下哪项附加指示是恰当的？

zh-choices.A: 不在场证明属于抗辩事由，因此必须由被告来确立；然而，其说服责任的标准是优势证据，而非毫无合理疑点。
zh-choices.B: 在你们可以考虑被告的不在场证明主张之前，你们必须判断他是否已提出充分证据来引出此争议点。
zh-choices.C: 如果被告的证据已使你们对他是否是抢劫犯产生合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。
zh-choices.D: 如果你们对于被告是否于3月5日晚11时左右在便利店现场存有合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Protection

核心原则

举证责任与正当程序

本题的核心考点在于宪法正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 对刑事案件举证责任的要求。

根据最高法院在 In re Winship (1970) 案中的裁定：

控方 (Prosecution) 必须承担证明刑事犯罪每一个构成要件 (Every Element) 的责任，且证明标准必须达到毫无合理疑点 (Beyond a Reasonable Doubt)。
难点辨析

不在场证明 (Alibi) 的性质

很多考生容易混淆“不在场证明”与“肯定性抗辩”。

  • 肯定性抗辩 (Affirmative Defense)： 如自卫 (Self-defense)、精神错乱 (Insanity)。被告承认做了该行为，但有正当理由。对于此类抗辩，法律允许将举证责任转移给被告。
  • 否定性抗辩 (Negation Defense)： 如不在场证明 (Alibi)。被告声称：“我当时不在那里，所以我不可能犯罪。”

关键逻辑： 不在场证明直接否定了犯罪的核心要素——被告在场 (Presence/Identity)。既然“被告在场”是控方必须证明的要素，那么控方就必须毫无合理疑点地证明它。

如果要求被告证明自己不在场，实际上就是免除了控方证明被告在场的责任，这违反了宪法。

答案详解

为什么选 D？

正确选项 D "If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty."

解析：

这个指示正确地将焦点放在了合理怀疑 (Reasonable Doubt) 上，并且针对的是犯罪要素（在场/时间/地点）。

它不需要被告去“证明”什么，而是告诉陪审团：只要对“被告是否在场”这一要素存疑（无论是因为控方证据不足，还是因为姐姐的证词），根据宪法，就必须判无罪。

选项 A 错误： 声称不在场证明必须由被告确立且标准是优势证据 (Preponderance of evidence)。这是违宪的，因为这转移了犯罪要素的举证责任。
选项 B 错误： 要求被告提出“充分证据”才能让陪审团考虑不在场证明。这同样暗示了被告有某种初始负担。实际上，只要证据记录中有任何内容引发了对“在场”的怀疑，陪审团都应考虑。
选项 C 错误（高干扰项）： "If the defendant's evidence has caused you..."
这个选项很狡猾。它暗示合理怀疑必须是由被告的证据引发的。但实际上，合理怀疑可能仅仅源于控方证人的不可靠。将怀疑的来源限制在被告的证据上，不恰当地加重了被告的负担。
MBE 考试技巧

如何秒杀此类题目

  1. 识别抗辩类型： 看到 Alibi（不在场）或 Lack of Intent（缺乏意图），立即反应这是在攻击犯罪要素 (Element)。
  2. 寻找举证责任： 对于攻击犯罪要素的抗辩，举证责任永远在控方 (Prosecution)。
  3. 警惕陷阱： 任何暗示“被告必须证明...” (Defendant must prove / establish) 的选项对于 Alibi 几乎都是错的。
  4. 最佳指示： 正确的 Jury Instruction 通常是：“如果陪审团对[该要素]有合理怀疑，必须判无罪。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A state grand jury investigating a murder learned that the key suspect might have kept a diary. The grand jury issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the suspect to produce any diary. The subpoena made clear that the grand jury was seeking only the diary and not any testimony from the suspect. The suspect refused to produce the diary, citing his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.
Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of his Fifth Amendment privilege?

choices.A: It may compel production without granting immunity, because the suspect was not compelled to write a diary.
choices.B: It may compel production if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity from the act of production.
choices.C: It may compel production only if the suspect is granted transactional immunity.
choices.D: It may not compel production of a private diary under any circumstances.

questions.explanation:

privilege against self-incrimination
Custodial interrogation

Question

  • government compulsion
  • testimonial communication
    • oral testimony
    • act of producing document
  • self-incrimination
Privilege
invoked
Privilege

Immunity granted
  • use & derivative use
  • transactional
Honor

Question
Question

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from being compelled to provide self-incriminating evidence that is testimonial or communicative in nature (ie, testimonial communications). For example, the compelled act of producing a document is privileged if that act would prove that:

  • the document exists
  • the suspect possesses the document or
  • the document is authentic (ie, was created or written by the suspect).

However, the contents of a document are not protected by this privilege since the suspect was not compelled to create that content (Choice A).

Here, the grand jury compelled the suspect to produce any diary when it issued a subpoena duces tecum.
The grand jury believed that the suspect might have kept a diary, so the suspect's act of production would prove that the diary exists, that he possesses it, and that it is authentic (self-incriminating evidence). As a result, the act of production is a privileged testimonial communication.

But the grand jury can still compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of this privilege if the suspect is granted either:

  • use and derivative use immunity – prevents the government from using self-incriminating testimonial communications (and any evidence derived from them) against the suspect in any way that could lead to a criminal prosecution (eg, to obtain a grand jury indictment, at trial) or
  • transactional immunity – protects the suspect from being prosecuted for any crimes associated with self-incriminating testimonial communications.

While testimony can be compelled by granting the suspect full transactional immunity, it is not necessary because the narrower use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment (Choice C). Therefore, the grand jury can compel production of the diary if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity (Choice D).

📌 Educational Objective

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from compelled testimonial communications—eg, the act of producing a document that would prove its existence, possession, and/or authenticity. However, self-incriminating testimony can still be compelled if the government grants use and derivative use immunity.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 43–44 (2000) (finding that the act of producing documents is a testimonial communication that can only be compelled by a grant of immunity).
  • Kastigar v. United States, 406 U.S. 441, 452–53 (1972) (holding that use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment).
questions.zh-question:
一个正在调查谋杀案的州大陪审团得知，关键嫌疑人可能写有日记。大陪审团签发了一份携带物证传票（subpoena duces tecum），要求嫌疑人交出任何日记。该传票明确指出，大陪审团只寻求日记，而非嫌疑人的任何证词。嫌疑人以其根据 Fifth Amendment（第五修正案）享有的反对自证其罪的特权为由，拒绝交出日记。

在何种情况下（若有），大陪审团可以不顾嫌疑人主张的 Fifth Amendment 特权，强制其交出日记？

zh-choices.A: 可以强制其交出而无需授予豁免权，因为嫌疑人并非被强迫写日记。
zh-choices.B: 如果嫌疑人因其交出行为而获得使用及派生使用豁免权，则可以强制其交出。
zh-choices.C: 只有在嫌疑人被授予交易豁免权（transactional immunity）的情况下，才能强制其交出。
zh-choices.D: 在任何情况下都不得强制交出私人日记。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / Fifth Amendment
核心考点：交出行为原则
本题考察的是第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中的反对自证其罪特权（Privilege Against Self-Incrimination）如何应用于文件传票（Subpoena Duces Tecum）。
关键区分：
第五修正案保护的是“被强迫的证言”（Compelled Testimony）。
1. 文件内容（Contents）： 通常不受保护。因为日记是嫌疑人过去自愿写的，政府现在并没有强迫他“写”日记，只是强迫他“交”出来。
2. 交出行为（Act of Production）： 受保护。虽然内容不受保护，但“交出文件”这个动作本身可能具有证言性质（Testimonial）。
为什么“交出行为”是证言？
根据最高法院判例（如 United States v. Hubbell），当政府不知道文件是否存在时，强迫嫌疑人交出文件，等于强迫嫌疑人承认以下三点：
📂 存在性 (Existence)： 文件确实存在。
✋ 持有权 (Possession)： 文件在我手里。
✅ 真实性 (Authentication)： 这些就是你们要找的文件。
在本题中，大陪审团只是听说嫌疑人“可能”（might）有日记。如果嫌疑人交出日记，就等于向政府提供了上述证言。因此，他可以行使第五修正案特权拒绝交出。
如何破解特权？(豁免权)
既然嫌疑人有权拒绝，政府若想强制获取日记，必须授予豁免权（Immunity）。
正确答案 B 的逻辑
使用及派生使用豁免权 (Use and Derivative Use Immunity)
根据 Kastigar v. United States，这是宪法要求的最低限度豁免权。
  • 它保证政府不会使用“交出行为”本身（或由此衍生的证据）来起诉嫌疑人。
  • 它不保护嫌疑人免受所有起诉（只要证据来源完全独立）。
因为这种豁免权已经消除了“自证其罪”的风险，嫌疑人就不能再拒绝交出日记了。
为什么其他选项错误？
❌
选项 A： 错误地认为只要内容是自愿写的就不受保护。它忽略了“交出行为”本身的证言性质。
❌
选项 C： 交易豁免权 (Transactional Immunity) 提供了更广泛的保护（完全免于起诉），但这并非宪法强制要求的。政府只需提供较窄的“使用豁免权”即可强制执行传票。
❌
选项 D： 私人日记并非绝对不可获取。只要解决了自证其罪的问题（通过豁免权），就可以强制交出。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到 Subpoena Duces Tecum 的题目，先看政府是否知道文件确切存在（Foregone Conclusion）。
如果政府是在“钓鱼”（Fishing Expedition），嫌疑人通常有权拒绝，除非政府授予 Use and Derivative Use Immunity。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man sought medical assistance for a gunshot wound to his leg in a hospital emergency room. He told a police officer at the hospital that he had been shot. The officer interviewed the man about the incident while the man was receiving medical treatment. At first, the man stated that he had been shot while attempting to buy drugs on a street corner. However, the discrepancies between the man's wound and his description of the shooting made the officer doubt the veracity of the man's story. The officer knew that the man was unable to leave the hospital due to his injuries, so the officer reminded the man that he did not have to talk with the officer. In response to further questioning, the man revealed that he had shot himself with his own gun.
The man had previously been convicted of a felony, so he was arrested and charged with illegal possession of a firearm by a felon. The man moved to suppress the statement that he had shot himself because he had not been provided with Miranda warnings.
Which of the following standards should the court apply to determine whether the man was in custody for Fifth Amendment purposes?

choices.A: Whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could terminate the interview.
choices.B: Whether it was reasonable for the police officer to believe that the man had shot himself.
choices.C: Whether the man believed that he could leave the hospital.
choices.D: Whether the police officer had probable cause to arrest the man.

questions.explanation:
Miranda custody requirement
Custody
No custody
Formal
arrest
Restricted
movement
Traffic
stop
Stop and frisk
(Terry stop)

In accordance with the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination, police must Mirandaize a suspect before a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation is questioning initiated by a known (as opposed to undercover) law enforcement officer after a person is in custody. A person is in custody for Miranda purposes when the person is (1) placed under formal arrest or (2) restrained in his freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave.

Here, the man was confined to the hospital due to medical necessity and had not been placed under formal arrest at the time of questioning. This means that the man would have been in custody only if his freedom of movement was restrained to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave. Accordingly, the court should determine whether the man was in custody for Fifth Amendment purposes by considering whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could terminate the officer's interview.

(Choices B and D) The determination of whether an individual was in custody does not turn on whether it was reasonable for police to believe the individual's account of relevant events, nor does it turn on whether the information possessed by the police was sufficient to arrest the individual.

(Choice C) The test for determining whether an individual is in custody is an objective one that focuses on what a reasonable person faced with similar circumstances would have believed—not on what the individual subjectively believed.

📌 Educational Objective

A person is in custody for Miranda purposes when the person is (1) placed under formal arrest or (2) restrained in his freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave.

📚 References
  • Thompson v. Keohane, 516 U.S. 99, 112 (1995) (providing that, if there has been no formal arrest, an "in custody" determination turns on whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could leave, given the totality of the circumstances).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因腿部枪伤在医院急诊室寻求医疗救助。他告诉医院里的一名警官他中枪了。警官在该男子接受医疗救治期间就该事件对他进行了询问。起初，该男子声称他是在街角试图购买毒品时中枪的。然而，该男子的伤口与他对枪击事件的描述之间的不符之处，使警官怀疑其说法的真实性。警官知道该男子因伤无法离开医院，因此提醒该男子他没有义务与警官交谈。在进一步的询问下，该男子透露他用自己的枪打伤了自己。
该男子此前曾被判犯有重罪（felony），因此他被捕并被控犯有重罪犯非法持有枪支罪。该男子动议排除（suppress）他自称打伤自己的陈述，理由是他未被告知 Miranda 警告。
法院应适用以下哪种标准来确定该男子是否为第五修正案目的而言处于羁押（custody）状态？

zh-choices.A: 合理的人是否会相信他可以终止询问。
zh-choices.B: 警官相信该男子打伤自己是否合理。
zh-choices.C: 该男子是否相信他可以离开医院。
zh-choices.D: 警官是否有合理根据（probable cause）逮捕该男子。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was on trial for the murder of his former business partner. During closing arguments, the prosecutor made a remark about the man's failure to testify during the proceedings. The man's attorney promptly objected to the prosecutor's remark and moved for a mistrial. The trial judge overruled the objection, denied the motion for mistrial, and ordered the prosecutor to carry on with her closing argument. After considering the overwhelming evidence of the man's guilt, the jury returned a guilty verdict. The man's attorney has challenged the man's conviction on appeal, arguing that the trial court erred in overruling the objection to the prosecutor's remark and denying the man's motion for mistrial.
How is the court of appeals likely to rule?

choices.A: Affirm the conviction, because of the harmless-error rule.
choices.B: Affirm the conviction, because of the plain-error rule.
choices.C: Reverse the conviction, because there was reversible error.
choices.D: Reverse the conviction, because there was structural error.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Fifth Amendment
  • Self-incrimination – secures right to refuse to testify against oneself
  • Grand jury – requires grand jury indictment for felony offense charged in federal court
  • Double jeopardy – bars multiple prosecutions for same offense
  • Due process – protects against unfair deprivation of life, liberty, or property
  • Takings – prohibits taking private property for public use without just compensation

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the prosecution from commenting on a criminal defendant's failure to testify at trial. However, a trial court's erroneous admission of such a comment does not result in the automatic reversal of a conviction on appeal. Instead, under the harmless-error rule, the appellate court should determine whether admission of the improper comment:

  • was sufficiently prejudicial as to require reversal or
  • constituted only harmless error.

An improper prosecutorial comment is sufficiently prejudicial to require reversal if the comment contributed to the guilty verdict. Conversely, if the appellate court is convinced beyond a reasonable doubt that the comment did not contribute to the verdict, then the erroneous admission constitutes harmless error.

Here, the trial court erroneously admitted a remark by the prosecutor regarding the man's failure to testify. But since there was overwhelming evidence of the man's guilt, the appellate court is likely to determine that the remark was not sufficiently prejudicial to require reversal (Choice C). Therefore, the appellate court is likely to affirm the man's conviction because of the harmless-error rule.

*The trial judge may attempt to cure potential error by immediately instructing the jury that the prosecutor's comment was improper and that the defendant has a constitutional right not to testify.

(Choice B) Under the plain-error doctrine, a defendant who failed to preserve a claim of error is still entitled to appellate relief if (1) the district court committed error under the law in effect at the time of the appeal, (2) the error was obvious under that law, and (3) the error affected the defendant's substantial rights. Here, the claim was preserved when the man's attorney objected and moved for mistrial, so this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice D) An appellate court should automatically reverse a defendant's conviction if the trial court committed structural error—ie, error that affected the entire framework of the criminal trial and rendered it fundamentally unfair. However, reference to the defendant's failure to testify does not constitute structural error.

📌 Educational Objective

The privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the prosecution from commenting on a defendant's failure to testify at trial. However, an improper prosecutorial comment warrants a reversal on appeal only if it contributed to the guilty conviction.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Chapman v. California, 386 U.S. 18, 24–26 (1967) (applying the harmless error rule to an improper prosecutorial comment).
  • Barbara E. Bergman et al., 3 Wharton's Criminal Evidence § 3:22 (15th ed. 2020) (discussing improper comments or inferences regarding a defendant's failure to testify).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因谋杀其前商业伙伴而受审。在结案陈词中，检察官对该男子在诉讼过程中未能作证一事发表了评论。该男子的律师立即对检察官的言论提出反对，并请求宣告审判无效。主审法官驳回了反对意见，拒绝了宣告审判无效的动议，并命令检察官继续其结案陈词。在考虑了该男子有罪的压倒性证据后，陪审团作出了有罪裁决。该男子的律师已对该男子的定罪提出上诉，主张初审法院在驳回对检察官言论的反对意见和拒绝该男子宣告审判无效的动议方面存在错误。

上诉法院可能会如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 维持定罪，因为适用无害错误规则。
zh-choices.B: 维持定罪，因为适用明显错误规则。
zh-choices.C: 撤销定罪，因为存在可撤销的错误。
zh-choices.D: 撤销定罪，因为存在结构性错误。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Law
核心考点：Griffin Rule

根据美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment），检察官禁止评论被告在审判中保持沉默（未能作证）的行为。这被称为 Griffin v. California 规则。

为什么选 A？

本题考察的是上诉法院审查宪法性错误时的标准。

✅ Harmless Error Rule (无害错误规则)

虽然检察官的评论确实侵犯了被告的宪法权利（Constitutional Error），但这并不意味着定罪会自动被撤销。

推理逻辑：

  • 前提：辩护律师在庭审时已经及时反对（Objected）并保留了异议。
  • 标准：对于已保留的宪法性错误，政府必须证明该错误在“排除合理怀疑”（Beyond a reasonable doubt）的程度上是无害的。
  • 应用：题目明确指出有“压倒性的有罪证据”（Overwhelming evidence of guilt）。这意味着，即使检察官没有那句不当评论，陪审团也几乎肯定会判被告有罪。

因此，法院会认定该错误未对判决结果产生实质影响，属于无害错误，从而维持定罪。

其他概念辨析
❌ Plain Error Rule (明显错误规则)

适用场景：当被告律师在庭审时未能提出反对（Failed to object）时使用。

本题情况：律师已经“promptly objected”（立即反对），因此不适用此规则。

❌ Structural Error (结构性错误)

定义：指那些从根本上破坏了审判公正框架的严重错误（如完全剥夺律师权、法官有偏见）。此类错误会导致自动撤销判决，无需进行无害分析。

本题情况：最高法院已裁定，违反 Griffin 规则（评论被告沉默）不属于结构性错误，必须进行无害错误分析。

💡 MBE 解题技巧

在处理上诉审查标准（Standard of Review）的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 有没有错误？（本题：有，检察官违宪评论）。
  2. 律师是否反对（Preserved）？
    • 没反对 ➡️ Plain Error（很难翻案）。
    • 反对了 ➡️ Harmless Error（政府需证明无害）。
  3. 证据强不强？
    • 如果题目说“证据确凿/压倒性” ➡️ 错误通常被视为Harmless，维持原判。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A suspect was taken into custody for questioning. After receiving Miranda warnings, which the suspect stated he understood, he was questioned by two detectives for three hours. The detectives told the suspect that the interrogation was about an illegal sale of automatic weapons. During this time, the suspect neither expressly waived nor expressly invoked his Miranda rights. Instead, he participated only sporadically in the conversation and responded to incriminating questions with silence.
Toward the end of the three-hour session, one of the detectives began to question the suspect about the recent murder of an arms dealer. The suspect was nonresponsive, so the detectives decided to pause the interrogation. As they were walking out of the interrogation room, one of the detectives asked the suspect, "Have you prayed for forgiveness for killing that man?" The suspect, tired from the hours of questioning, responded that he had. He then immediately told the detectives that he wanted to speak with an attorney. The detectives immediately terminated the interrogation and left the room.
If the suspect moves to suppress his admission about killing the arms dealer, how will the court likely rule on his motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the interrogation immediately ceased after the suspect asserted his right to counsel.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the suspect knowingly and voluntarily waived his right to remain silent by making the statement.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the detectives failed to advise the suspect of the full subject matter of the interrogation.
choices.D: Grant the motion, but allow the prosecution to use the suspect's incriminating statement at trial for impeachment purposes only.

questions.explanation:
Waiver of Miranda rights

Custodial interrogation

  • in custody
  • subjected to interrogation
↓

Miranda warnings

  • right to remain silent
  • statements can be used against you
  • right to an attorney
  • court-appointed attorney available
↓

Suspect's response

Rights
unambiguously
invoked
Express waiver
Implied waiver
Police must
honor request
Police may interrogate suspect
& use statements at trial

Incriminating statements obtained from a custodial interrogation may not be used against a suspect at a subsequent trial unless police provided procedural safeguards to secure the suspect's Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. Police safeguard this privilege by informing the suspect of his/her Miranda rights prior to a custodial interrogation (as seen here).

A suspect may then choose to specifically and unambiguously invoke a Miranda right — eg, by clearly and unambiguously asserting his/her desire to remain silent. Therefore, a suspect's silence in response to police questioning does not invoke Miranda rights, even if questioning was extensive. A suspect may also choose to expressly waive (eg, by signing a waiver form) or impliedly waive Miranda rights.

Waiver is implied when a suspect (1) has not asserted his/her Miranda rights, (2) understands those rights, and (3) engages in a course of conduct that indicates a knowing and voluntary waiver—eg, by making an uncoerced incriminating statement (as the suspect did here). Therefore, the court will likely deny the suspect's motion to suppress his admission about killing the arms dealer.

(Choice A) The suspect made the inculpatory statement before invoking his Fifth Amendment right to counsel and after initially waiving his right to remain silent. It is this—not the fact that the detectives immediately ceased their interrogation upon the suspect's request—that renders the statement admissible.

(Choice C) Police need not provide a suspect with the subject matter of the interrogation before administering Miranda warnings. Therefore, the detectives' failure to inform the suspect of the interrogation's full subject matter did not invalidate the suspect's waiver.

(Choice D) A voluntary and trustworthy statement taken in violation of Miranda is admissible to impeach a criminal defendant who gives contradictory testimony at trial. But an incriminating statement that does not violate Miranda is also admissible as substantive evidence.

📌 Educational Objective

Miranda rights may be expressly or impliedly waived. A waiver is implied when a suspect (1) has not asserted his/her Miranda rights, (2) understands those rights, and (3) engages in a course of conduct indicating a waiver.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berghuis v. Thompkins, 560 U.S. 370, 384–85 (2010) (holding that voluntary incriminating statement by suspect who has not invoked but understands rights constitutes waiver).
  • Colorado v. Spring, 479 U.S. 564, 577 (1987) (holding that a suspect's lack of awareness of an interrogation's possible subject matter does not invalidate the suspect's waiver of Fifth Amendment rights).
questions.zh-question:
一名嫌疑人因受审问而被拘留。在收到其声称已理解的Miranda警告后，他被两名警探审问了三个小时。警探告诉嫌疑人，审讯是关于一起非法销售自动武器的案件。在此期间，嫌疑人既未明确放弃也未明确援引其Miranda权利。相反，他只是零星地参与谈话，并以沉默回应有罪指控的问题。

在三个小时的审讯快结束时，一名警探开始就最近一名军火商的谋杀案向嫌疑人提问。嫌疑人没有回应，因此警探决定暂停审讯。当他们走出审讯室时，一名警探问嫌疑人："你为杀了那个人而祈求宽恕了吗？" 嫌疑人因数小时的审问而感到疲惫，回答说他祈求了。他随即告诉警探，他想和律师谈谈。警探立即终止了审讯并离开了房间。

如果嫌疑人动议排除其关于杀害军火商的供述，法院可能会如何裁定其动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为在嫌疑人主张其律师权后，审讯立即停止了。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为嫌疑人通过作出该陈述，知情且自愿地放弃了其保持沉默的权利。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为警探未能告知嫌疑人审讯的全部主题事项。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，但允许检方在审判中仅为弹劾目的使用嫌疑人的有罪陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Miranda Rights
核心考点：默示放弃 (Implied Waiver)

在 Miranda 规则下，保持沉默本身并不构成对权利的援引。如果嫌疑人理解了权利，未明确主张权利，且自愿作出了陈述，则视为默示放弃。

Berghuis v. Thompkins (2010)

⚖️ 法律推理逻辑

1. 权利的告知与理解
题目明确指出嫌疑人收到了 Miranda 警告并表示理解。这是放弃权利的前提条件。
2. 沉默 ≠ 援引权利 (Silence is not Invocation)
嫌疑人在审讯期间大部分时间保持沉默。根据 Berghuis v. Thompkins，单纯的沉默不足以援引第五修正案的沉默权。嫌疑人必须明确无误地 (unambiguously) 声明他希望保持沉默或要求律师。
3. 默示放弃的构成
当警探问及祈祷宽恕时，嫌疑人回答了“是的”。
  • 他理解自己的权利；
  • 他没有受到强迫 (Coercion)；
  • 他没有在此之前明确援引权利。
这一连串行为 (Course of conduct) 构成了对沉默权的默示放弃 (Implied Waiver)。
4. 律师请求的时间点
嫌疑人是在作出有罪供述之后才要求律师的。因此，之前的供述是合法的，之后的审讯必须停止（警探也确实停止了）。
✅ 正确答案：选项 B
法院将驳回动议，因为嫌疑人通过作出该陈述，知情且自愿地放弃了其保持沉默的权利。

🚫 常见陷阱分析

选项 A (停止审讯): 虽然警探确实在嫌疑人要求律师后停止了审讯，但这并不是供述可采的原因。供述可采是因为在说话的那一刻，权利已被默示放弃。
选项 C (审讯主题): 这是一个经典的 MBE 干扰项。 警方不需要在 Miranda 警告前告知嫌疑人所有可能的审讯主题。
Colorado v. Spring (1987)
即使嫌疑人以为只问非法武器，警方转而问谋杀也是合法的。
选项 D (仅用于弹劾): 只有在违反 Miranda 程序（如未给警告）但供述自愿的情况下，才仅限于弹劾使用。本案中警方完全遵守了程序，因此供述可作为实体证据 (Substantive Evidence)。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A grand jury was investigating the murder of a local businessman. The prosecutor suspected that the businessman's partner may have been involved, but had no concrete evidence implicating him as the murderer. The partner was subpoenaed to testify before the grand jury. The partner invoked his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination and refused to answer any questions, so the prosecutor granted the partner use and derivative use immunity for his testimony. The partner testified that he and his associate killed the businessman in order to assume full control of the company.
Both the partner and his associate were indicted for murder. The associate entered a plea to manslaughter on the condition that he testify against the partner. His testimony and the partner's grand jury testimony are the only evidence of who committed the murder.
The partner has objected to the admission of the associate's testimony at trial.
How should the court rule on the partner's objection?

choices.A: Overrule the objection, because the associate's testimony was obtained by the prosecution in exchange for a plea bargain.
choices.B: Overrule the objection, because the partner was a suspect before he was subpoenaed to testify before the grand jury.
choices.C: Sustain the objection, because the associate's testimony is derivative of the partner's grand jury testimony.
choices.D: Sustain the objection, because the constitutional rights of one codefendant cannot be bargained away in a deal with another.

questions.explanation:
Use and derivative use immunity timeline
Partner refuses
to testify
(5th Amendment)
Receives use
& derivative
use immunity
Testifies he
& associate
committed murder
Partner &
associate
indicted
Associate
agrees to
testify at trial
Prosecution
suspects only
partner
Prosecution learns
associate was
involved
Derived from
partner's immunized
testimony
= use and derivative use immunity applies

A person subpoenaed to testify before a grand jury can invoke the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination and refuse to testify. However, that person can be compelled to testify during this (or any other) proceeding if he/she is granted either:

  • transactional immunity – protects a person from being prosecuted for any crimes associated with his/her testimony or
  • use and derivative use immunity – prevents a person's testimony, and any evidence derived from it, from being used against him/her in any way that could lead to a criminal prosecution.

If the government prosecutes a person who was granted use and derivative use immunity, it can only use evidence obtained from an independent source. It cannot use any evidence derived from the defendant's immunized testimony.

Here, the partner was granted use and derivative use immunity before testifying that he and the associate committed the murder. The grand jury then indicted them both. The prosecutor later sought to have the associate testify against the partner. But the associate's testimony was derived from the partner's immunized testimony—not an independent source. Therefore, the court should sustain the partner's objection and prohibit the associate's testimony.

(Choice A) The associate agreed to testify in exchange for a reduced charge of manslaughter. But since the associate's testimony derived from the partner's immunized testimony, it is inadmissible.

(Choice B) Although the prosecutor suspected that the partner was involved in the businessman’s murder before the grand jury proceeding, he did not know of the associate's involvement until the partner testified. Therefore, the associate's testimony derives from the partner's immunized testimony and is inadmissible.

(Choice D) The constitutional rights of one codefendant cannot be bargained away in a deal with another—but this is not the dispositive issue. It is that the prosecution would improperly use the partner's immunized grand jury testimony if the associate's derivative testimony were presented against the partner at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

Use and derivative use immunity precludes the use of a person's testimony—and any evidence derived from it—against him/her in a criminal proceeding. However, evidence obtained from an independent source can be used.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Kastigar v. United States, 406 U.S. 441, 453 (1972) (explaining that use and derivative use immunity precludes the use of the suspect's testimony or any evidence derived from it against the suspect in a criminal prosecution).
questions.zh-question:
一个大陪审团正在调查一名当地商人的谋杀案。检察官怀疑该商人的合伙人可能涉案，但没有具体证据指证其为凶手。该合伙人被传唤至大陪审团作证。该合伙人援引其反对自证其罪的Fifth Amendment特权，拒绝回答任何问题，因此检察官就其证词授予了该合伙人使用和派生使用豁免权（use and derivative use immunity）。该合伙人作证称，他和他的同伙为了完全控制公司而杀害了该商人。

该合伙人及其同伙均被以谋杀罪起诉。该同伙承认了误杀罪（manslaughter），条件是其出庭作证指控该合伙人。他的证词以及该合伙人在大陪审团的证词是证明谁实施了谋杀的唯一证据。

该合伙人已对在审判中采纳该同伙的证词提出异议。

法院应如何裁定该合伙人的异议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回异议，因为同伙的证词是检方通过辩诉交易获得的。
zh-choices.B: 驳回异议，因为在该合伙人被传唤至大陪审团作证前，他已是嫌疑人。
zh-choices.C: 支持异议，因为同伙的证词是从该合伙人在大陪审团的证词派生而来的。
zh-choices.D: 支持异议，因为一名共同被告的宪法权利不能在与另一名被告的交易中被出卖。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fifth Amendment

核心考点：豁免权 (Immunity)

根据美国宪法第五修正案，政府可以通过授予豁免权来强制证人作证。最常见的类型是使用和派生使用豁免权 (Use and Derivative Use Immunity)。

这意味着：政府不能使用该证词，也不能使用从该证词中获得的任何线索或证据来指控该证人。

法律推理与案情分析

1 豁免权的范围
最高法院在 Kastigar v. United States (1972) 案中确立，如果政府授予了“使用和派生使用豁免权”，检方在随后对该证人进行刑事起诉时，负有举证责任，必须证明其证据来自完全独立的合法来源 (legitimate independent source)。
2 本案中的“毒树之果”
在本案中，检察官在合伙人 (Partner) 作证前并不知道同伙 (Associate) 的存在或参与。
  • 合伙人的受豁免证词供出了同伙。
  • 检方利用这一信息找到了同伙。
  • 同伙的证词因此直接派生 (derived) 于合伙人的受豁免证词。
3 结论
由于同伙的证词不是来自“独立来源”，而是直接源于合伙人被迫提供的证词，因此在针对合伙人的审判中引入该证词违反了豁免协议和第五修正案。
正确答案：C
支持异议，因为同伙的证词是从合伙人的大陪审团证词派生而来的。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (辩诉交易)
错误。虽然同伙确实达成了辩诉交易 (plea bargain)，但这与证据的可采性无关。关键问题在于该证据的来源是否受到豁免权的污染。
选项 B (嫌疑人身份)
错误。即使合伙人之前就是嫌疑人，检方并没有关于“同伙”的独立证据。检方对合伙人的怀疑不能洗白从受豁免证词中获得的新证据（即同伙的证词）。
选项 D (共同被告权利)
错误。这是一个干扰项。法律并不禁止利用共同被告的证词，只要该证词来源合法。本案的问题不在于“出卖权利”，而在于违反了豁免权保护的“派生使用”规则。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Use and Derivative Use Immunity" 时，请立即寻找检方证据的来源链条。

如果检方使用的证人、文件或线索是因为被告的受豁免证词才被发现的，那么这些证据就是“派生”的，通常不可用于指控该被告（除非检方能证明有独立来源）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A valid warrant was issued for a woman's arrest. The police learned that a person with the woman's name and physical description lived at a particular address. When police officers went to that address, the house appeared to be unoccupied: the windows and doors were boarded up with plywood, and the lawn had not been mowed for a long time. A neighbor confirmed that the house belonged to the woman but said that the woman had not been there for several months.
The officers knocked repeatedly on the front door and shouted, "Police! Open up!" Receiving no response, they tore the plywood off the door, smashed through the door with a sledgehammer, and entered the house. They found no one inside, but they did find an illegal sawed-off shotgun. Upon her return to the house a few weeks later, the woman was charged with unlawful possession of the shotgun.
The woman has moved to suppress the use of the shotgun as evidence at her trial.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because the officers acted in good faith under the authority of a valid warrant.
choices.B: No, because the officers did not violate any legitimate expectation of privacy in the house since the woman had abandoned it.
choices.C: Yes, because the officers entered the house by means of excessive force.
choices.D: Yes, because the officers had no reason to believe that the woman was in the house.

questions.explanation:
Forcible entry of a suspect's residence
Did police have a warrant?
Yes
Did police knock and
announce their presence?
Yes
Did occupant have a reasonable
opportunity to answer?
Yes
Did police reasonably
believe suspect was inside?
Yes
Entry allowed
No
No
No
No
Entry prohibited
No
Were there exigent circumstances?
  • Destruction of evidence (evanescent)
  • Threat of harm (emergency)
  • Fleeing felony suspect (hot pursuit)
Yes
Entry allowed

An arrest warrant authorizes officers to take a suspect into custody for criminal prosecution and is generally required to arrest a suspect in his/her home. However, an arrest warrant does not give officers unrestricted authority to intrude upon a suspect's privacy interests in his/her home. Therefore, officers may only forcibly enter a suspect's residence to execute an arrest warrant if they:

• knock and announce their presence
• allow a reasonable opportunity for someone to answer and
• have reason to believe that the suspect is inside.

Here, the officers went to the woman's home after they obtained a valid warrant for her arrest. They repeatedly knocked and announced their presence before smashing through the door (forcible entry). But since the home appeared vacant and a neighbor confirmed that the woman had not been there for several months, the officers had no reason to believe that she was inside. Therefore, their forcible entry was unlawful, and the shotgun discovered during that entry should be suppressed.

(Choice A) The good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule allows illegally seized evidence to be admitted if officers reasonably believed that they were acting lawfully. But this exception does not apply here since the valid warrant did not give the officers reason to believe that they could lawfully use force to enter the woman's apparently vacant home.

(Choice B) Since a person has no legitimate expectation of privacy in abandoned property, police may freely enter and search it. But police cannot reasonably assume that a poorly kept home is abandoned. Therefore, the boarded doors and windows and unmaintained lawn did not support an assumption that the woman's house was abandoned.

(Choice C) Although the officers entered the house by means of excessive force (since they had no reason to believe that the woman was inside), this does not support the suppression of evidence. Instead, the officers' excessive force may expose them to civil liability for damage caused to the house or other property.

📌 Educational Objective

An arrest warrant allows officers to arrest a suspect in his/her home. But officers can only forcibly enter that home to make the arrest if they: (1) knock and announce their presence, (2) allow a reasonable opportunity for someone to answer, and (3) have reason to believe that the suspect is inside.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Payton v. New York, 445 U.S. 573, 603 (1980) (explaining that an arrest warrant gives officers the authority to enter a suspect's dwelling when there is reason to believe the suspect is inside).
questions.zh-question:
一份有效的逮捕令被签发用于逮捕一名女子。警方得知，一名与该女子姓名和外貌特征相符的人居住在某个特定地址。当警察到达该地址时，房屋看似无人居住：门窗被胶合板封住，草坪也长时间未修剪。一位邻居证实该房屋属于这名女子，但表示她已有数月未在此处。

警察反复敲击前门并大喊：“警察！开门！”在没有得到任何回应后，他们撕掉了门上的胶合板，用大锤砸开门，进入了房屋。他们在屋内没有发现任何人，但发现了一支非法的短管霰弹枪。几周后，当该女子返回房屋时，她被指控非法持有该霰弹枪。

该女子已提出动议，要求在审判中排除使用该霰弹枪作为证据。

法院是否应批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为警察在有效逮捕令的授权下，是基于善意行事的。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该女子已经遗弃了该房屋，所以警察并未侵犯她对房屋的任何合法隐私期待。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为警察使用了过度武力进入房屋。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为警察没有理由相信该女子在房屋内。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment

核心考点：逮捕令的执行范围

根据最高法院判例 Payton v. New York (1980)，警方持有一份有效的逮捕令 (Arrest Warrant) 即可进入嫌疑人的住所进行逮捕，但必须满足两个前提条件：

  1. 有理由相信该处是嫌疑人的住所；并且
  2. 有理由相信嫌疑人当时正在屋内 (Reason to believe the suspect is within)。
本案逻辑推演
✓
逮捕令有效：警方持有有效的逮捕令，且确认了地址正确。
✓
敲门并表明身份：警方履行了 "Knock and Announce" 规则。
✕
相信嫌疑人在屋内：
这是本题的致命缺陷。
  • 门窗被封死 (Boarded up)
  • 草坪荒废 (Unmowed lawn)
  • 邻居证词：嫌疑人已数月未归
结论：警方没有理由相信嫌疑人在屋内。
正确答案：D
应批准动议，因为警察没有理由相信该女子在房屋内。

由于警方缺乏“嫌疑人在屋内”的合理确信，他们强行进入房屋的行为违反了第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment)。因此，这次进入是非法的搜查，所发现的霰弹枪作为“毒树之果” (Fruit of the Poisonous Tree) 必须被排除。

⚠️ 常见误区 (Distractors)
  • 选项 A (善意例外 Good Faith): 善意例外通常适用于搜查令无效的情况。这里的问题不是逮捕令无效，而是执行方式违宪（在明显无人的情况下强行进入）。
  • 选项 B (遗弃 Abandonment): 这是一个很强的干扰项。虽然房屋看似破败，但仅仅是“草坪未修剪”和“门窗封死”并不等同于法律上的遗弃。只要房主仍拥有产权且未明确放弃，她仍享有隐私期待。
  • 选项 C (过度武力 Excessive Force): 使用大锤破门确实看似暴力，但如果警方有理由相信嫌疑人在内且拒捕，这种武力是允许的。本案的关键在于进入本身非法，而不是破门工具的选择。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police received information from an undercover police officer that she had just seen two men (whom she described) in a red pickup truck selling marijuana to schoolchildren near the city's largest high school. A few minutes later, two police officers saw a pickup truck fitting the description a half block from the high school. The driver of the truck matched the description of one of the men described by the undercover officer. The only passenger was a young woman.
The police stopped the truck and searched the driver. In the pocket of the driver's jacket, the police found a small bottle of pills that they recognized as narcotics. They then broke open a locked toolbox attached to the flatbed of the truck and found a small sealed envelope inside. They opened it and found marijuana. They also found a quantity of cocaine in the glove compartment.
After completing their search of the driver and the truck, the driver was arrested and charged with unlawful possession of narcotics.
If the driver moves to suppress the use as evidence of the marijuana and cocaine found in the search of the truck, how should the court rule on his motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion as to both the marijuana and the cocaine.
choices.B: Deny the motion as to the marijuana but grant it as to the cocaine.
choices.C: Grant the motion as to both the marijuana and the cocaine.
choices.D: Grant the motion as to the marijuana but deny it as to the cocaine.

questions.explanation:
Exceptions to warrant requirement
Exceptions Elements
Search incident to arrest • Search of body & immediate surrounding area directly before or after lawful arrest
Administrative search of highly regulated industry • Regulatory scheme has substantial government interest
• Warrantless search necessary to further interest
• Scheme provides constitutionally adequate substitute for warrant
Stop and frisk
(Terry stop)		 • Reasonable suspicion person is (or was) involved in crime
• Search limited to:
◦ brief questioning to confirm or dispel suspicion
◦ frisk if reasonably believe person is armed
Plain view doctrine • Immediately recognizable contraband in plain view of officer lawfully in area
Automobile • Probable cause that vehicle contains evidence of crime
• Search limited to areas where evidence might be located
Consent • Given voluntarily by person with actual or apparent authority
• Search limited to scope of consent
Exigent circumstance • Evanescent evidence – destruction of evidence
• Emergency situation – threat of physical harm to police and/or public
• Hot pursuit – pursuit of fleeing felony suspect
Special government purpose • Inventory search – items searched under established routine
• Special needs (eg, search of students, government employees)
• Parolee – warrantless search as condition of parole
• Border search – national security allows search

Mnemonic: SAD SPACES

A court should suppress evidence obtained during an unreasonable Fourth Amendment search. An unreasonable search occurs when the government acts without a warrant based on probable cause and no exception to the warrant requirement applies. The automobile exception justifies a warrantless police search of a person's vehicle when:

  • police have probable cause to believe that the vehicle contains evidence of a crime and
  • the search is limited to areas where the evidence might be located.

During an automobile search, police can search any containers inside the vehicle—including locked containers—that might contain the illegal evidence. They can also seize any other illegal items discovered during this search.

Here, the police had probable cause to stop and search a truck and driver that matched the description given by the undercover officer. This allowed the police to then conduct a warrantless search of areas in the truck where the marijuana might be located—including the locked toolbox and the glove compartment. Since the police discovered marijuana and cocaine during that lawful search, they did not need a warrant to seize the illegal items. Therefore, the driver's motion to suppress should be denied (Choices B, C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

The automobile exception to the warrant requirement allows police to conduct a warrantless search of a vehicle if they have probable cause to believe it contains evidence of a crime. Officers can search any area within the vehicle where the evidence might be located, including locked containers.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Carroll v. United States, 267 U.S. 132, 153 (1925) (establishing the automobile exception to the warrant requirement).
  • United States v. Ross, 456 U.S. 798, 825 (1982) (holding that during an automobile search, police can also search containers that may contain evidence of the crime).
questions.zh-question:
警方从一名卧底警官处获得信息，称她刚刚看到两名男子（她描述了他们的特征）在一辆红色皮卡车上，在全市最大的高中附近向学童出售大麻。几分钟后，两名警官在离高中半个街区的地方，看到了一辆符合描述的皮卡车。该卡车司机与卧底警官所描述的其中一名男子的特征相符。车上唯一的乘客是一名年轻女子。

警方截停了卡车并搜查了司机。在司机夹克的口袋里，警方发现了一小瓶他们辨认为麻醉药品的药丸。随后，他们撬开了固定在卡车平板货厢上的一个上锁的工具箱，在里面发现了一个小的密封信封。他们打开信封，发现了大麻。他们还在手套箱里发现了一定量的可卡因。

在完成对司机和卡车的搜查后，司机被逮捕，并被控非法持有麻醉药品罪。

如果司机提出动议，要求排除在搜查卡车时发现的大麻和可卡因作为证据使用，法院应如何对其动议作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 就大麻和可卡因两者，均驳回该动议。
zh-choices.B: 就大麻驳回该动议，但就可卡因批准该动议。
zh-choices.C: 就大麻和可卡因两者，均批准该动议。
zh-choices.D: 就大麻批准该动议，但就可卡因驳回该动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑事诉讼法 (Criminal Procedure)
正确答案：A 法院应驳回排除大麻和可卡因证据的动议 (Deny the motion as to both)。
核心考点：车辆例外原则 (Automobile Exception)

根据美国宪法第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment)，如果警方有合理根据 (Probable Cause) 相信车辆内藏有犯罪证据或违禁品，他们可以在没有搜查令 (Warrantless) 的情况下搜查该车辆。

搜查范围 (Scope of Search)：
警方可以搜查车辆内任何可能藏匿该证据的地方，包括后备箱和所有容器（无论是否上锁），只要该容器在物理上能装下他们正在寻找的证据。

参考判例: United States v. Ross (1982)
本案逻辑推演

1. 合理根据的建立 (Establishment of Probable Cause)
警方从卧底警官处获得了具体描述（两名男子、红色皮卡、向学生出售大麻）。当警方发现符合描述的车辆和司机时，他们就有了合理根据 (Probable Cause) 相信车内藏有大麻。

2. 搜查的合法性 (Legality of the Search)
基于“车辆例外原则”，警方无需申请搜查令即可搜查整辆车。

3. 搜查范围与容器 (Containers)
警方正在寻找大麻 (Marijuana)。

  • 上锁的工具箱 (Locked Toolbox)：大麻可以藏在工具箱里吗？可以。因此，警方撬开工具箱是合法的。
  • 手套箱 (Glove Compartment)：大麻可以藏在手套箱里吗？可以。因此，搜查手套箱也是合法的。

4. 证据的可采性 (Admissibility)
大麻是在合法的搜查范围内发现的。
可卡因是在合法搜查手套箱（寻找大麻）的过程中发现的。根据一目了然原则 (Plain View Doctrine)，警方在合法搜查过程中发现的其他违禁品均可作为证据。

💡 MBE 避坑指南

考生常犯的错误是认为“上锁”的容器（如本题中的工具箱）享有更高的隐私期待，必须有搜查令才能打开。

请记住：在“车辆例外”原则下，锁 (Lock) 并不能阻挡基于合理根据 (Probable Cause) 的搜查。只要警察找的东西能塞进那个容器里，他们就可以开锁搜查。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
In a trial of a defendant for armed bank robbery, the prosecutor presented overwhelming evidence of guilt. Three tellers identified the defendant as the robber, a latent fingerprint found on the bank counter linked the defendant to the scene, and bank money had been found in the defendant's car. The police had arrested the defendant immediately after the robbery, as the defendant was driving away from the bank.
When the prosecution rested its case, the judge directed the jury to return a verdict of guilty. The defense attorney did not object at the time. The jury withdrew, discussed the case, and agreed to a guilty verdict. The jury returned to the courtroom and announced the guilty verdict. The defense attorney then voiced an objection to the judge's having directed the verdict. The court overruled the objection and sentenced the defendant to 20 years in prison.
On appeal, what should the appellate court do?

choices.A: Affirm the conviction, because the defense attorney failed to timely object to the judge's action.
choices.B: Affirm the conviction, because the prosecution presented both circumstantial and direct evidence conclusively establishing the defendant's guilt.
choices.C: Reverse the conviction, because the defense attorney's failure to timely object to the judge's action constituted ineffective assistance of counsel.
choices.D: Reverse the conviction, because the judge's action in directing the verdict denied the defendant his constitutional right to a trial by jury.

questions.explanation:
Structural errors
  • Biased judge
  • Deprivation of right to counsel
  • Attorney enters guilty plea over defendant's objection
  • Discriminatory selection of jurors
  • Exclusion of defendant from courtroom during trial
  • Denial of public trial and/or jury trial
  • Improper jury instruction on burden of proof

An appellate court should automatically reverse a defendant's conviction if the trial court committed a structural error. A structural error is an error that affects the entire framework of a criminal trial and renders it fundamentally unfair (eg, denial of the Sixth Amendment right to jury trial). Every criminal defendant who is charged with a serious offense—a crime that carries a possible prison sentence greater than six months (eg, armed bank robbery)—has the right to have a jury determine his/her guilt. Therefore, this right was violated when the judge directed the jury to return a guilty verdict,* and an automatic reversal of the defendant's conviction is warranted.

In contrast, no structural error would have occurred had the trial judge directed the jury to return a verdict of acquittal upon finding that there was insufficient evidence for a reasonable jury to find the defendant guilty.

(Choice A) A timely objection—an objection made when a judge can still correct the error (usually at the time the error occurred)—is generally required to preserve an error for appeal. Otherwise, that error is waived. However, a timely objection is not needed to challenge a structural error on appeal.

(Choice B) The prosecution presented circumstantial (latent fingerprint) and direct (tellers' identification) evidence that conclusively established the defendant's guilt. This evidence would ordinarily show that the alleged error was harmless (ie, did not affect the trial's outcome) and that the conviction should be affirmed. But since a structural error is never harmless, the conviction must be reversed—despite the overwhelming evidence of guilt.

(Choice C) An ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim requires proof that the defense attorney's performance was deficient (below an objective standard of reasonableness) and prejudicial (affected the result of the proceeding). Here, the defense attorney's failure to timely object was not deficient or prejudicial since this error can still be raised on appeal. Therefore, the defendant's conviction will not be reversed on this basis.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant charged with a serious criminal offense has a Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial, so a judge cannot direct the jury to return a guilty verdict. Doing so constitutes a structural error that requires automatic reversal of the defendant's conviction on appeal.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to jury trial).
  • Sparf v. United States, 156 U.S. 51, 105–06 (1895) (holding that a judge cannot direct the jury to find a criminal defendant guilty).
  • Rose v. Clark, 478 U.S. 570, 578 (1986) (explaining that a directed verdict against a criminal defendant constitutes structural error).
questions.zh-question:
在一场针对被告的持械银行抢劫案的审判中，检察官出示了压倒性的有罪证据。三名银行出纳员指认被告为抢劫犯，在银行柜台上发现的一枚潜指纹将被告与犯罪现场联系起来，并且在被告的车里发现了银行的钱款。抢劫案发生后，当被告驾车离开银行时，警方立即将其逮捕。

当控方陈述完其案情后，法官指示陪审团作出有罪裁决。辩护律师当时没有提出反对。陪审团退庭讨论此案，并一致同意作出有罪裁决。陪审团回到法庭，宣布了有罪裁决。辩护律师随后对法官指示裁决的行为表示反对。法院驳回了反对意见，并判处被告20年监禁。

在上诉中，上诉法院应如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 维持原判，因为辩护律师未能及时对法官的行为提出反对。
zh-choices.B: 维持原判，因为控方出示的间接证据和直接证据都确凿地证明了被告的有罪。
zh-choices.C: 推翻原判，因为辩护律师未能及时对法官的行为提出反对，构成了无效的律师协助。
zh-choices.D: 推翻原判，因为法官指示裁决的行为剥夺了被告受宪法保护的由陪审团审判的权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure | Right to Jury Trial

核心结论

上诉法院必须推翻定罪 (Reverse the conviction)。

理由：法官指示陪审团作出有罪裁决 (Directed Verdict of Guilty) 侵犯了被告的宪法权利，属于结构性错误 (Structural Error)，必须自动推翻，无论证据多么确凿。

法律规则解析

第六修正案 Right to Jury Trial

美国宪法第六修正案赋予刑事被告由陪审团审判的权利。这意味着：

  • 事实认定者： 陪审团是唯一的“事实认定者” (Fact Finder)。
  • 禁止行为： 法官绝对不能在刑事案件中指示陪审团作出有罪裁决 (Direct a verdict of guilty)。
  • 区别民事案件： 在民事案件中，如果证据一边倒，法官可以指示裁决 (JMOL)；但在刑事案件中，无论控方证据多么具有压倒性 (Overwhelming)，法官都无权剥夺陪审团判定“有罪”的权力。
关键概念：结构性错误 (Structural Error)
这类错误破坏了审判的根本框架，导致审判本质上不公平。

后果： 自动推翻判决 (Automatic Reversal)。
例外： 不适用“无害错误规则” (Harmless Error Rule)。即上诉法院不能因为“反正被告肯定有罪”而维持原判。
选项深度剖析
  • ✅ 选项 D (正确)
    法官指示有罪裁决剥夺了被告的陪审团审判权。这是宪法层面的结构性错误，不需要证明偏见 (Prejudice)，直接导致定罪无效。
  • ❌ 选项 A (错误 - 关于异议)
    虽然通常上诉需要“及时异议” (Timely Objection) 来保留错误，但结构性错误非常严重，通常被视为“明显错误” (Plain Error)，即使律师没有当场反对，上诉法院也会介入。此外，本题中律师在判决宣布后提出了反对，虽然稍晚，但对于此类根本性宪法错误已足够。
  • ❌ 选项 B (错误 - 关于证据)
    这是本题最大的陷阱。题目强调了“压倒性的证据” (Overwhelming Evidence)。如果你应用“无害错误” (Harmless Error) 分析，会选这个。但切记：结构性错误绝非无害。剥夺陪审团审判权不能用证据确凿来补救。
  • ❌ 选项 C (错误 - 关于律师)
    推翻判决的根本原因是法官的违宪行为，而不是律师的协助无效 (Ineffective Assistance of Counsel)。律师的表现并未导致结果改变（因为法官的行为本身就是可逆转的错误），所以这不是最佳理由。

🚀 MBE 提分锦囊

看到“Directed Verdict” (指示裁决) 时：

案件类型 针对被告 (Guilty) 针对无罪 (Acquittal)
刑事 (Criminal) 🚫 绝对禁止
(结构性错误)		 ✅ 允许
(若证据不足)
民事 (Civil) ✅ 允许 (若无合理陪审团能得出相反结论)

⚠️ 陷阱警报： 题目会用大量篇幅描述被告“铁证如山”。请忽略这些证据！只要法官在刑事案中指示“有罪”，就是自动推翻。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was charged with first-degree murder. Two lawyers were appointed to represent him because the prosecution planned to seek the death penalty. On the first day of trial, the air-conditioning malfunctioned in the courtroom, so the judge directed that the selection of the jurors take place in his chambers. Because of the large number of potential jurors, the judge directed that only one lawyer for the prosecution and one for the defense participate in the jury selection process. The defendant remained in the courtroom during the questioning of the jurors. Once the jury was selected, the trial was postponed until the next day, when the air-conditioning was again working.
Did the court's jury selection process violate the defendant's federal constitutional rights?

choices.A: No, because a defendant's confrontation rights are limited to witnesses rather than jurors.
choices.B: No, because there was good cause to conduct jury selection outside the defendant's presence.
choices.C: Yes, because excluding the defendant undercut the presumption of innocence.
choices.D: Yes, because jury selection is a critical stage at which a defendant is entitled to be present.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to be present at trial
Did proceeding hold significant
consequences for defendant (critical stage)?
No
Yes
Did defendant waive right to be present
by voluntarily leaving?
Yes
No
Was defendant excluded for good
cause after receiving a warning?
Yes
No
Exclusion prohibited

The Sixth Amendment right to confrontation guarantees a criminal defendant's right to be present at all critical stages of trial—ie, any event in a criminal proceeding that holds significant consequences for the defendant. Jury selection is a critical stage since the defendant's absence would deprive him/her of the opportunity to evaluate potential jurors in person and help decide whom to challenge. Therefore, a defendant has the right to be present during jury selection unless he/she:

  • waives this right by voluntarily leaving the proceedings or
  • is excluded for good cause (ie, misconduct) after receiving a warning from the court.

Here, jury selection occurred in the judge's chambers due to a malfunctioning air-conditioning system. Due to the limited space in the judge's chambers, the defendant had to remain in the courtroom. But since the defendant did not voluntarily leave or engage in misconduct, there was no good cause for his exclusion from the jury selection process (Choice B). Therefore, that exclusion violated his right to confrontation.

(Choice A) The confrontation clause gives criminal defendants the right to be personally present during all critical stages of trial—including jury selection—not just to confront witnesses.

(Choice C) Criminal defendants are presumed innocent until the prosecution proves their guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, excluding the defendant did not undercut this presumption since it had no effect on the prosecution's burden of proof.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment confrontation clause guarantees a criminal defendant the right to be present during all critical stages of trial—including jury selection. A defendant can only lose this right if he/she leaves voluntarily or is removed for good cause after receiving a warning from the court.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (confrontation clause).
  • Lewis v. United States, 146 U.S. 370, 372–73 (1892) (recognizing that the confrontation clause guarantees a criminal defendant's right to be personally present during every critical stage of trial).
  • Illinois v. Allen, 397 U.S. 337, 338 (1970) (holding that a defendant's right to be present at every stage of trial is lost when the defendant engages in disruptive behavior).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子被控一级谋杀罪。由于检方计划寻求死刑，法院为他指派了两名律师。审判的第一天，法庭的空调出现故障，因此法官指示在法官办公室内进行陪审员的甄选。由于潜在陪审员人数众多，法官指示控辩双方各派一名律师参与陪审团甄选过程。在询问陪审员期间，被告人留在法庭内。陪审团选定后，审判推迟到第二天，届时空调恢复正常。

法院的陪审团甄选程序是否侵犯了被告人的联邦宪法权利？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为被告的对质权仅限于证人，而非陪审员。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为有正当理由在被告不在场的情况下进行陪审团甄选。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为将被告排除在外削弱了无罪推定原则。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为陪审团甄选是一个关键阶段，被告有权在场。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure | 刑事诉讼法

⚖️ 核心考点：被告人的出席权

本题考察的是美国宪法第六修正案 (Sixth Amendment) 中的对质条款 (Confrontation Clause)。

法律规则：刑事被告人有权亲自出席审判的所有“关键阶段” (Critical Stages)。

✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 D)
结论： 是的，因为陪审团甄选是一个关键阶段，被告有权在场。

逻辑推演：

  • 定义关键阶段： 任何对被告有重大后果的诉讼环节都是关键阶段。
  • 陪审团甄选 (Jury Selection / Voir Dire)： 这是一个典型的关键阶段。被告需要在场观察潜在陪审员的举止和回答，以便协助律师决定行使“无因回避” (Peremptory Challenges) 或“有因回避” (Challenges for Cause)。
  • 本案情况： 虽然是因为空调故障这种“不可抗力”导致地点变更，但被告被物理隔离在法庭内，无法参与在法官办公室进行的甄选，这直接剥夺了他的宪法权利。
❌ 常见陷阱排除
选项 B (陷阱)： 错误地认为有“正当理由” (Good Cause)。

解析： 这是一个很强的干扰项。虽然空调坏了听起来像是一个合理的行政理由，但在宪法层面，剥夺被告出席权的“正当理由”通常仅限于被告自身的行为（例如：被告在法庭上大吵大闹、具有破坏性，经法官警告无效后被移除）。

仅仅因为房间太小或空调故障，不足以成为剥夺被告宪法权利的理由。

选项 A： 错误地限制了对质权的范围。

解析： 对质条款不仅仅是关于“交叉询问证人” (Cross-examination)。它保障被告在整个审判过程中与控方“对峙”的权利，包括陪审团甄选。

💡 MBE 解题技巧

在处理涉及Right to be Present (出席权) 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 判断阶段： 这是审判的“关键阶段”吗？(陪审团甄选、法官给陪审团的指示、判决宣读等通常都是)。
  2. 检查例外： 被告是否自愿放弃 (Waived) 了权利？或者是否因严重不当行为 (Misconduct) 被驱逐？
  3. 结论： 如果是关键阶段，且没有上述例外，无论法官的理由多么“务实”（如空调坏了、房间小），排除被告都是违宪的。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police officers received a tip that illegal drugs were being sold at a certain ground-floor apartment. They decided to stake out the apartment. The stakeout revealed that a significant number of people visited the apartment for short periods of time and then left. A man exited the apartment and started to walk briskly away. The officers grabbed the man and, when he struggled, wrestled him to the ground. They searched him and found a bag of heroin in one of his pockets. After discovering the heroin on the man, the officers decided to enter the apartment. They knocked on the door, which was opened by the woman who lived there. The officers asked if they could come inside, and the woman gave them permission to do so. Once inside, the officers observed several bags of heroin on the living room table.
The woman has been charged with possession of the heroin found on the living room table. She has filed a pretrial motion to suppress the heroin on the ground that it was obtained by an illegal search and seizure.
Should the woman's motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because the tip together with the heroin found in the man's pocket provided probable cause for the search.
choices.B: No, because the woman consented to the officers' entry.
choices.C: Yes, because the officers' decision to enter the apartment was the fruit of an illegal search of the man.
choices.D: Yes, because the officers did not inform the woman that she could refuse consent.

questions.explanation:
Plain view doctrine
Was item in officer's plain view?
  • Visible without moving other items
Yes ↓
Was item immediately recognizable as contraband?
  • Officer had probable cause to believe items were illegal evidence
Yes ↓
Was officer lawfully in area?
  • Warrant to search premises or
  • Another exception justifies presence
    (eg, consent, exigent circumstance)
Yes ↓
Applicable
(no warrant required)

A court should suppress evidence that was obtained during an unreasonable Fourth Amendment search or seizure. A search or seizure is unreasonable when it is conducted without a warrant and no exception to the warrant requirement applies. The plain view doctrine is an exception that allows an officer to seize an item without a warrant if:

• the item is in the officer's plain view
• it is immediately recognized as contraband and
• the officer is lawfully in the area.

An officer can lawfully enter a private area without a warrant if the officer obtains the owner's consent.
Consent is a valid basis for entering an area if (1) the owner's consent is given voluntarily (ie, without police coercion) and (2) any search is limited to the scope of the consent.

Here, the officers saw several bags on the woman's living room table (item in plain view) that contained heroin (immediately recognizable contraband) after they entered her apartment. And since the woman voluntarily consented to their entry and the officers limited their actions to the scope of her consent, the officers were lawfully in the area. Therefore, the plain view doctrine allowed the officers to seize the heroin without a warrant, and the court should deny the woman's motion to suppress that evidence.

(Choice A) The tip and the heroin found in the man's pocket may have given the officers probable cause to obtain a search warrant—but did not justify their warrantless search of the woman's apartment. Instead, that search was justified because the woman consented to their entry.

(Choice C) Under the fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine, a court should suppress evidence that stems from an unreasonable police search. However, that search must have violated the defendant's Fourth Amendment rights—not the rights of another. Therefore, the illegal search of the man is not a legitimate basis to grant the woman's motion.

(Choice D) Consent is valid when it is given voluntarily—informed consent is not required. Therefore, the officers did not need to inform the woman that she had the right to refuse consent to enter her home.

📌 Educational Objective

The plain view doctrine allows police to legally seize an item without a warrant if they (1) see the item in plain view, (2) immediately recognize it as contraband, and (3) are in the area lawfully (eg, consent).

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Coolidge v. New Hampshire, 403 U.S. 443, 465 (1971) (discussing the plain view doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
警官收到线报，称某底层公寓内有非法毒品交易。他们决定对该公寓进行监视。监视显示，有大量人员短暂进入该公寓后离开。一名男子从公寓出来，开始快步离开。警官抓住该男子，当他反抗时，将他摔倒在地。他们对他进行了搜查，并在他的一个口袋里发现了一袋海洛因。在该男子身上发现海洛因后，警官决定进入该公寓。他们敲了门，住在里面的女子打开了门。警官询问是否可以进入，该女子同意了。进入后，警官在客厅桌上看到了几袋海洛因。

该女子因客厅桌上发现的海洛因被控持有毒品罪。她已提出审前动议，以证据是通过非法搜查和扣押获得为由，请求排除该海洛因证据。

该女子的动议应被批准吗？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为线报以及在该男子口袋中发现的海洛因，为搜查提供了相当理由。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该女子同意了警官的进入。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为警官进入公寓的决定是对该男子进行非法搜查的毒树之果。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为警官没有告知该女子她可以拒绝同意。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：选项 B 不应批准动议，因为该女子同意了警官的进入。
(No, because the woman consented to the officers' entry.)

本题的核心考点在于无证搜查的例外情况，具体涉及“同意”（Consent）和“一目了然”（Plain View）原则。

1. 有效同意 (Valid Consent)

根据美国宪法第四修正案，警方进入私人住宅通常需要搜查令。但如果拥有共同居住权的人自愿同意（Voluntarily Consented），则无需搜查令。

  • 不需要知情同意： 警方不需要告知住户“你有权拒绝”。只要同意不是通过胁迫（Coercion）获得的，即视为有效。这直接排除了选项 D。
  • 判例支持： Schneckloth v. Bustamonte (1973)。
2. 一目了然原则 (Plain View Doctrine)

一旦警方合法地进入了该女子的公寓（基于她的同意），他们就有权扣押任何处于“一目了然”位置的违禁品。

三要素：

  1. 警方合法处于该位置 (Lawful vantage point)；
  2. 物品处于视线范围内；
  3. 物品的违法性质是显而易见的 (Immediately apparent)。

本案中，警方进屋后直接在桌上看到了海洛因，符合上述所有条件。

MBE 常见陷阱：毒树之果与当事人资格

很多考生会误选 选项 C，认为对男子的非法搜查（毒树）导致了后续的发现（毒果）。

为什么这是错的？

这里涉及到一个关键概念：当事人资格 (Standing)。

  • 第四修正案的权利是个人的 (Personal)。
  • 该女子不能主张警官侵犯了该男子的权利。即使警方对男子的搜查是非法的，该女子也无权以此为由要求排除在她家中发现的证据，因为那是他人的宪法权利被侵犯，而非她自己的。
  • 排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule) 只有在被告人自己的第四修正案权利被侵犯时才适用。

Rakas v. Illinois (1978)

🎓 考试技巧

在做 Criminal Procedure 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 政府行为： 是警察干的吗？(Yes)
  2. 合理隐私期待 (REP)： 被告对被搜查区域有 REP 吗？(Yes，这是她家)
  3. 搜查令： 有搜查令吗？(No)
  4. 例外情况： 有例外吗？(Yes, Consent)
  5. 资格 (Standing)： 谁的权利被侵犯了？(如果是别人被非法搜查，被告通常不能以此为由排除证据)

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
